## 1. Overview of Magento 2 Product Types

Magento 2 ships with **six core product types**, each serving a distinct use case. Selecting the wrong product type is a common source of bugs and misconfiguration in real projects.

```
+------------------+--------------------------------------------+
| Product Type     | Primary Use Case                           |
+------------------+--------------------------------------------+
| Simple           | Single physical item, one SKU              |
| Configurable     | One product, multiple variations (size/color)|
| Grouped          | Several related products shown together    |
| Bundle           | Build-your-own product from options        |
| Virtual          | Service/fee — no shipping required         |
| Downloadable     | Digital files or links                     |
+------------------+--------------------------------------------+
```

> **Exam focus:** You must know which product type to recommend for a given scenario — this is tested both in scenario questions and drag-and-drop matching questions.

---

## 2. Simple Product

### What It Is

A **Simple product** represents a single, standalone SKU. It is the most fundamental product type in Magento 2 and is also the **building block** for other types (Configurable, Grouped, Bundle).

### Key Characteristics

- **One SKU** per product
- Has its own price, weight, and inventory count
- Can be sold standalone **or** used as a child/component of other product types
- Supports all standard product attributes

### Admin Form Sections (Simple Product)

```
Catalog > Products > Add Product > Simple Product
  |
  +-- Product Information
  |     |-- Attribute Set (dropdown)
  |     |-- SKU
  |     |-- Price
  |     |-- Quantity / Stock Status
  |     |-- Weight (required — affects shipping)
  |
  +-- Images & Videos
  +-- Search Engine Optimization
  +-- Related Products / Up-sells / Cross-sells
  +-- Customizable Options (per-item custom text, file upload, etc.)
```

### Customizable Options

Simple products support **Customizable Options** — these allow one-off per-order customizations (e.g., engraving text) **without** creating separate SKUs.

```
Options Types:
  - Text (field, area)
  - File (upload)
  - Select (drop-down, radio, checkbox, multiple select)
  - Date (date, date & time, time)
```

> **Exam focus:** Customizable options do **not** create new SKUs; they add a price delta to the base product price. A configurable product uses separate child SKUs instead.

---

## 3. Configurable Product

### What It Is

A **Configurable product** presents as a single product page where the customer selects attributes (e.g., Size, Color) and those selections resolve to a **child Simple product** that is actually added to the cart.

```
Configurable Parent (no own stock, no own price in strict sense)
  |
  +-- Child Simple: SKU = shirt-red-S  (Color=Red, Size=S)
  +-- Child Simple: SKU = shirt-red-M  (Color=Red, Size=M)
  +-- Child Simple: SKU = shirt-blue-S (Color=Blue, Size=S)
  +-- Child Simple: SKU = shirt-blue-M (Color=Blue, Size=M)
```

### Key Characteristics

- Parent product has **no own inventory** — stock is tracked at the child simple level
- Price shown on the parent PDP is derived from the **lowest priced** child (by default)
- Requires a **unique attribute** (or combination) that uses `Use To Create Configurable Product = Yes` in its configuration
- Child simples can exist as standalone products (if visible individually) or be hidden

### Configurable Attribute Requirements

For an attribute to be used as a configurable axis:

| Requirement | Value |
|---|---|
| Input Type | Dropdown (or Visual/Text Swatch) |
| Scope | Global |
| Use To Create Configurable Product | Yes |

> **Exam focus:** The attribute **must be of type Dropdown, Visual Swatch, or Text Swatch** and scoped **Globally**. Text-type attributes cannot be used as configurable axes. This is a very common exam question.

### Admin Creation Flow

```
1. Catalog > Products > Add Product > Configurable Product
2. Select Attribute Set
3. Fill in basic info (Name, SKU, Price as placeholder)
4. Click "Create Configurations" (Configuration tab)
   a. Select configurable attributes (e.g., Color, Size)
   b. Select or create attribute values
   c. Bulk-assign images, price, quantity per variation
   d. Generate child simples
5. Save the parent
```

### How the Price Is Displayed

```
Default behavior:
  PDP shows lowest child price
  (can be "as low as $X")

After variant selection:
  Price updates via AJAX/JS to reflect selected child's price
```

> **Exam focus:** The **parent configurable product does NOT carry its own saleable stock**. If all child simples are out of stock, the configurable appears out of stock. The parent `qty` field in the database (`cataloginventory_stock_item`) for a configurable is typically `0` or ignored.

---

## 4. Grouped Product

### What It Is

A **Grouped product** is a collection of **Simple (or Virtual) products** displayed together on a single product page. The customer can choose quantities of each item independently.

```
"Bedroom Furniture Set" (Grouped Product)
  |
  +-- Bed Frame       (Simple) — customer enters qty: 1  — Price: $299
  +-- Nightstand      (Simple) — customer enters qty: 2  — Price: $89 each
  +-- Dresser         (Simple) — customer enters qty: 1  — Price: $199
```

### Key Characteristics

- **No group-level price** — each associated simple product has its own price
- **No group-level SKU** added to cart — individual simples are added as separate line items
- Customer can set qty = 0 for any item to exclude it
- Can set a **default quantity** per associated product in Admin
- Associated products retain their own stock levels

> **Exam focus:** A Grouped product has **no price of its own**. The price displayed is the individual price of each member product. This is a classic trick question — "what is the price of a Grouped product?" → **there is no single group price**.

> **Exam focus:** Items added to cart from a Grouped product appear as **separate line items** in the cart, not as a single bundled line.

### Admin Form Notes

```
Catalog > Products > Grouped Product
  |
  +-- NO "Price" field (grayed out / not present)
  +-- NO "Weight" field at group level
  +-- "Grouped Products" section:
        Add products by search, set Default Qty per item
```

---

## 5. Bundle Product

### What It Is

A **Bundle product** lets customers build their own product by selecting from predefined option sets. Think of it as a "choose your own components" product.

```
"Custom PC Bundle"
  |
  +-- Option: CPU      (required, radio) 
  |     +-- Intel i5  (+$0)
  |     +-- Intel i7  (+$100)
  |
  +-- Option: RAM      (required, dropdown)
  |     +-- 8GB        (+$0)
  |     +-- 16GB       (+$50)
  |
  +-- Option: SSD      (optional, checkbox)
        +-- 512GB      (+$80)
        +-- 1TB        (+$150)
```

### Bundle Pricing Types

This is one of the most-tested areas for Bundle products:

#### Dynamic Pricing (Default)

```
Final Price = SUM of all selected option prices

Example:
  Base Bundle = $0 (or a base set elsewhere)
  + i7 selected  = $300
  + 16GB RAM     = $80
  + 512GB SSD    = $60
  -------------------------
  Total          = $440
```

- Price shown as **"From $X"** range when no selection made
- Discounts and special prices apply to the **individual simple components**
- Tax is calculated on components

#### Fixed Pricing

```
Final Price = Bundle base price + sum of selection price adjustments

Each selection can have a price adjustment:
  - Fixed: a specific dollar amount added to the base price
  - Percent: a percentage of the bundle base price

Example:
  Bundle base price = $399
  + "i7 upgrade" selection  = +$100 (fixed adjustment)
  + "16GB RAM" selection    = +10% of base ($39.90)
  -------------------------
  Total = $538.90

If all selection price values are set to $0:
  Total = $399 (base only, regardless of selections)
```

- The Bundle product has its own editable base price
- Each option selection can add a fixed dollar or percentage-based price adjustment on top of the base price
- If all selections have a price value of $0, the total equals the base price regardless of choices
- Discount/special price applies to the Bundle's own base price

> **Exam focus:** **Dynamic pricing** = sum of actual product prices of selected options (bundle base price is $0). **Fixed pricing** = bundle base price + selection price adjustments (fixed $ or % of base). If all selection adjustments are $0, total equals base price. This distinction is heavily tested.

### Bundle SKU Types

| SKU Type | Behavior |
|---|---|
| **Dynamic SKU** | SKU auto-generated from Bundle SKU + selected option SKUs |
| **Fixed SKU** | One static SKU defined on the Bundle, never changes |

> **Exam focus:** Bundle has **two independent type settings**: Price Type (Dynamic/Fixed) AND SKU Type (Dynamic/Fixed). They can be mixed (e.g., Fixed Price + Dynamic SKU).

### Bundle Option Input Types

```
- Drop-down
- Radio buttons
- Checkbox      (allows multiple selections from one option)
- Multiple Select
```

### Admin Form Key Sections

```
Catalog > Products > Bundle Product
  |
  +-- Dynamic Price toggle (Yes = Dynamic, No = Fixed)
  +-- Dynamic SKU toggle
  +-- Price field (only active when Dynamic Price = No)
  +-- Bundle Items section:
        +-- Add Option (title, required y/n, input type)
              +-- Add Products to Option (search simples/virtuals)
                    +-- Set qty, default selection, user-defined qty
```

---

## 6. Virtual Product

### What It Is

A **Virtual product** is identical to a Simple product **except it has no weight** and does **not require shipping**. Used for services, memberships, warranties, and other non-physical items.

### Key Characteristics

- No `weight` attribute
- Does **not trigger shipping step** in checkout (if cart contains only virtual products)
- Billing address may be used as shipping address (or shipping step skipped entirely)
- Can be a member of Grouped or Bundle products
- Has its own SKU, price, and inventory (can track stock)

```
Use Cases:
  - Extended warranty (+$49)
  - Consulting hour
  - Event ticket
  - Software license key (without file — use Downloadable for files)
```

> **Exam focus:** If a cart contains **only virtual products**, the **shipping step is skipped** in the checkout flow. If even one physical product is in the cart, shipping displays normally.

---

## 7. Downloadable Product

### What It Is

A **Downloadable product** is a virtual product that delivers one or more **files or URLs** to the customer after purchase.

### Key Characteristics

- No weight / no shipping (like Virtual)
- Has a **Links** section (the actual downloadable content)
- Has an optional **Samples** section (preview files)
- Supports shareable vs. non-shareable links

### Downloadable Link Settings

| Setting | Description |
|---|---|
| **Title** | Label shown to customer (e.g., "HD Version") |
| **Price** | Additional price per link (adds to base product price) |
| **Max Downloads** | Number of times link can be used (0 = unlimited) |
| **Is Shareable** | If Yes, no login required to download; If No, customer must be logged in |
| **Link Type** | File (uploaded to server) or URL (external link) |
| **Sample Type** | File or URL for preview |

> **Exam focus:** **Max Downloads = 0** means **unlimited downloads**, not zero downloads. This is a trick question. Also: each downloadable link can have its **own additional price** added on top of the base product price.

### Downloadable Link Access Control

- **There is no time-based link expiry setting** in Magento 2 — no "Links Valid for N Days" field exists in the codebase (verified against EE 2.4.8-p3 `system.xml`)
- Link access is controlled by:
  - **Download count** — Max Downloads per link (0 = unlimited)
  - **Order status** — links become available when the order item reaches the configured status (default: Invoiced)
  - **Refund/cancellation** — links are marked expired when orders are refunded or canceled
- Global defaults are configured at **Stores > Configuration > Catalog > Downloadable Product Options**:
  - Order Item Status to Enable Downloads
  - Default Maximum Number of Downloads
  - Shareable (default)
  - Default Sample Title / Default Link Title
  - Open Links in New Window
  - Use Content-Disposition
  - Disable Guest Checkout if Cart Contains Downloadable Items

> **Exam focus:** Downloadable link availability is governed by download count and order status — not by a time window. The per-product settings are: title, price, max downloads, shareable flag, and file/URL. Global defaults live in Stores > Config > Catalog > Downloadable Product Options.

### Samples vs Links

```
Samples: Preview content (free, shown before purchase)
  - No purchase required
  - Displayed on PDP

Links: Actual product delivery (gated by purchase)
  - Access granted after successful order
  - Sent via Order Confirmation email / My Account > My Downloads
```

---

## 8. Product Type Comparison Matrix

| Feature | Simple | Configurable | Grouped | Bundle | Virtual | Downloadable |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Own SKU | Yes | Yes (parent) | Yes (group) | Yes | Yes | Yes |
| Own Price | Yes | Derived* | No | Yes/Derived | Yes | Yes |
| Own Stock | Yes | No (child) | No (each child) | No (components) | Yes | Yes |
| Weight/Shipping | Yes | Via child | Via each child | Via components | **No** | **No** |
| Child Products | No | Yes (Simples) | Yes (Simples) | Yes (Simples/Virtual) | No | No |
| Configurable Axes | No | Yes | No | No | No | No |
| Downloadable Links | No | No | No | No | No | **Yes** |
| Can be child of... | Config/Group/Bundle | — | — | — | Group/Bundle | — |

*Configurable parent price: typically lowest child, configurable in theme/module

> **Exam focus:** Memorize which product types have **no own price** (Grouped) and **no own stock at parent level** (Configurable, Bundle).

---

## 9. Catalog Configuration: Attributes & Attribute Sets

### Product Attributes

Attributes define the properties of a product (color, size, material, etc.). They live in:

```
Stores > Attributes > Product
```

#### Key Attribute Settings

```
+-- Attribute Code       (unique identifier, snake_case)
+-- Default Label        (shown in admin)
+-- Input Type           (text, textarea, date, yes/no, dropdown,
|                          multiselect, price, media image,
|                          visual swatch, text swatch)
+-- Values Required      (yes/no)
+-- Attribute Scope      (Store View / Website / Global)
+-- Use in Search        (makes attribute searchable in catalog search)
+-- Comparable on Front  (shows in comparison table)
+-- Use in Layered Navigation (faceted filtering)
+-- Use for Promo Rule Conditions
+-- Visible on Catalog Page on Storefront
+-- Used in Product Listing
```

> **Exam focus:** **Attribute Scope** determines whether the value can differ per store view (Store View scope) or must be the same across all stores (Global scope). **Configurable product attributes MUST be Global scope.**

#### Input Type Details

| Input Type | Notes |
|---|---|
| Text Field | Single-line text, no options |
| Text Area | Multi-line text |
| Date | Date picker |
| Yes/No | Boolean toggle |
| Dropdown | Single select from predefined values; **usable as configurable axis** |
| Multiple Select | Multi-value select |
| Price | Numeric, uses store currency |
| Media Image | Image upload |
| Visual Swatch | Color/image swatch; **usable as configurable axis** |
| Text Swatch | Text label swatch; **usable as configurable axis** |

> **Exam focus:** Only **Dropdown**, **Visual Swatch**, and **Text Swatch** input types can be used as configurable product axes.

### Attribute Sets

An **Attribute Set** is a template that groups attributes into **groups** (tabs in the admin form). Every product belongs to exactly one Attribute Set.

```
Attribute Set: "Clothing"
  |
  +-- Group: General
  |     +-- Name, Description, SKU, Price, etc.
  |
  +-- Group: Physical Details
  |     +-- Weight, Dimensions
  |
  +-- Group: Clothing Attributes
        +-- Size (dropdown)
        +-- Color (visual swatch)
        +-- Material (dropdown)
        +-- Gender (dropdown)
```

#### Managing Attribute Sets

```
Path: Stores > Attributes > Attribute Set

Actions:
  - Create new set (from scratch or based on existing set)
  - Drag attributes between groups
  - Create new groups (tabs in admin form)
  - Delete attributes from set (removes from product form, not from system)
```

> **Exam focus:** Changing a product's **Attribute Set** after creation is possible in Admin, but it will **remove attribute values** not present in the new set. This is a destructive operation.

> **Exam focus:** The **Default** attribute set cannot be deleted. Custom attribute sets can be based on the Default set.

#### System vs Custom Attributes

| Type | Description |
|---|---|
| **System Attributes** | Built-in (name, sku, price, status, visibility, etc.) — cannot be deleted |
| **Custom Attributes** | Created by admin/developer — can be deleted if not used by system |

### Attribute Scope: Detailed

```
Store View Scope:
  Value can differ per Store View
  Example: product name in French vs English

Website Scope:
  Value same across all store views in a website
  Example: price per website/currency zone

Global Scope:
  Single value across entire Magento installation
  Example: SKU, weight, attribute used in configurable
```

> **Exam focus:** **Price** is **Website scope** by default (so you can have different prices per website). **SKU** is **Global** scope.

---

## 10. Swatches

### Overview

Swatches replace standard dropdown selects with visual or text representations, improving the shopping UX for attributes like Color and Size.

```
Types:
  1. Visual Swatch — color block or image thumbnail
  2. Text Swatch   — text label (e.g., "XL", "2XG")
```

### Configuring Swatches

```
Path: Stores > Attributes > Product > [Select Color attribute]
  |
  +-- Input Type: Visual Swatch
  +-- Manage Swatch (Values of Your Attribute):
        For each option value:
          - Upload image, OR
          - Choose color (hex picker), OR
          - Enter text label
```

### Swatch Display on PDP

```
Configurable Product PDP:
  +--[ Red ]--[ Blue ]--[ Green ]--+   <-- Visual Swatches (Color)
  +--[ S ]--[ M ]--[ L ]--[ XL ]--+   <-- Text Swatches (Size)

  - Unavailable combos shown as crossed out
  - Hovering swatch may update product image
```

> **Exam focus:** Swatches are an attribute **Input Type** setting, not a separate configuration section. They behave like dropdowns for configurable products but render differently on the frontend.

### Swatch Configuration Options

```
Stores > Configuration > Catalog > Storefront
  |
  +-- Swatches per Product   (max swatches shown before "more" link)
  +-- Show Swatches in Product List (category page)
  +-- Show Swatches Tooltip
```

---

## 11. Inventory Behavior by Product Type

This is one of the most critical and tricky areas for the exam.

### Stock Tracking Summary

```
+----------------+------------------------------------------+
| Product Type   | Where Stock is Tracked                   |
+----------------+------------------------------------------+
| Simple         | On the product itself                    |
| Virtual        | On the product itself                    |
| Downloadable   | On the product itself (or unlimited)     |
| Configurable   | On each CHILD Simple product             |
| Grouped        | On each individual associated product    |
| Bundle         | On each component Simple product         |
+----------------+------------------------------------------+
```

### Configurable Product Inventory Deep Dive

```
Configurable Parent (shirt-configurable)
  qty = 0 (meaningless / ignored)
  stock_status = determined by children
  |
  +-- Child: shirt-red-S  qty=10  stock=In Stock
  +-- Child: shirt-red-M  qty=0   stock=Out of Stock
  +-- Child: shirt-blue-S qty=5   stock=In Stock
  +-- Child: shirt-blue-M qty=2   stock=In Stock

Result:
  Parent shows "In Stock" because at least 1 child is in stock
  Red / M option appears greyed out or unavailable on PDP
```

> **Exam focus:** The Configurable parent product row in `cataloginventory_stock_item` **does** exist, but its `qty` is not used for availability. Availability is determined by **child simples**. Setting the parent's qty does nothing for stock management.

### Bundle Product Inventory

```
Bundle "Gaming Bundle"
  No own stock
  |
  +-- Component: Mouse     qty=50
  +-- Component: Keyboard  qty=30
  +-- Component: Headset   qty=0  (optional)

Bundle is saleable IF:
  - All REQUIRED components have available stock
  - Optional components with 0 stock still allow bundle sale
```

> **Exam focus:** A Bundle product is **out of stock** if any **required** component option has no in-stock selections. Optional components being out of stock does not prevent the bundle from being purchased.

### MSI (Multi-Source Inventory)

Magento 2.3+ ships with **MSI (Multi-Source Inventory)**:

```
Source  = physical location (warehouse, store, etc.)
Stock   = saleable quantity aggregated from sources

Sources --> Stock --> Sales Channel (Website)
```

> **Exam focus:** In MSI, stock status for Configurable products is still derived from child simples, but each child can have quantities split across multiple sources.

---

## 12. Pricing Behavior by Product Type

### Price Display Summary

```
+----------------+-------------------------------------------+
| Product Type   | Price Behavior                            |
+----------------+-------------------------------------------+
| Simple         | Direct product price                      |
| Virtual        | Direct product price                      |
| Downloadable   | Base price + optional per-link price      |
| Configurable   | "As low as $X" (lowest child price)       |
| Grouped        | NO group price — each child has own price |
| Bundle Dynamic | "From $X to $Y" (sum of min/max options)  |
| Bundle Fixed   | Base price + selection adjustments ($/%)  |
+----------------+-------------------------------------------+
```

### Tier Pricing

Available on Simple, Virtual, Downloadable, Configurable (at child level):

```php
// Tier price example:
// Buy 1-4:    $20.00
// Buy 5-9:    $18.00 (10% off)
// Buy 10+:    $15.00 (25% off)
```

### Special Price

```
Simple/Virtual/Downloadable:  Set directly on product
Configurable:                 Set on child simples
Grouped:                      Set on each member simple
Bundle Fixed:                 Set on bundle product
Bundle Dynamic:               Set on component simples
```

> **Exam focus:** For a **Configurable product**, the special price must be set on the **child Simple products**, not on the parent. The parent PDP will then show the discounted "as low as" price.

### Group Price / Customer Group Pricing

Catalog Price Rules and customer group pricing can apply to product types differently:

```
Catalog Price Rule can target:
  - Conditions based on product attributes
  - Applies to: Simple, Virtual, Downloadable
  - For Configurable: applies via children
  - For Grouped: applies to individual members
```

---

## 13. Admin Form Differences: Configurable vs Bundle

Understanding the admin form differences is explicitly called out in the task description.

### Side-by-Side Admin Form Comparison

```
CONFIGURABLE PRODUCT                  BUNDLE PRODUCT
==============================        ==============================
Attribute Set: [Clothing v]           Attribute Set: [Default v]
Name: [Red T-Shirt          ]         Name: [Gaming Bundle         ]
SKU:  [shirt-001            ]         SKU:  [bundle-gaming-001     ]
Price: [19.99               ]         Dynamic Price: [Yes / No]
                                      Price: [grayed if Dynamic=Yes]
                                      Dynamic SKU:  [Yes / No]

[Configuration] Tab                   [Bundle Items] Tab
  "Create Configurations" button        "Add Option" button
  |                                     |
  +-- Select Attributes                 +-- Option Title: [CPU      ]
  |   (Color, Size)                     +-- Input Type: [Radio     ]
  |                                     +-- Required:   [Yes       ]
  +-- Select/Create Values              |
  |   Color: Red, Blue, Green           +-- Add Products to Option
  |   Size: S, M, L, XL                     |
  |                                         +-- Search: [i5 CPU    ]
  +-- Bulk assign:                          +-- Search: [i7 CPU    ]
      Images per child                      +-- Set qty, default,
      Price per child                           user-defined qty
      Qty per child

[No "Bundle Items" tab]               [No "Create Configurations" btn]

Stock tracked: CHILD simples          Stock tracked: COMPONENT simples
Price shown:   "As low as $X"         Price shown:   "From $X to $Y"
                                                      (Dynamic) or
                                                      base $X +/- adjustments (Fixed)
```

### Key Admin Form Sections Unique to Each Type

#### Configurable Only:
- **"Configurations" tab** with the "Create Configurations" workflow
- Attribute selection step with value matrix
- Ability to associate existing simples or auto-generate them

#### Bundle Only:
- **"Bundle Items" tab**
- **Dynamic Price** toggle (affects whether Price field is editable)
- **Dynamic SKU** toggle
- Per-option: title, required flag, input type
- Per-item-in-option: default selection, user-defined qty flag

> **Exam focus:** On a **Bundle product** with Dynamic Price = Yes, the **Price field is disabled** in the admin form because the price is calculated from components. You must set Dynamic Price = No (Fixed) to enter a manual price.

> **Exam focus:** On a **Configurable product**, after clicking "Create Configurations", you cannot change the configurable attribute axes later through the UI (you'd need to delete and recreate, or use a workaround). The axes are locked once set.

---

## 14. Hands-On Walkthroughs

### Creating a Configurable Product — Step by Step

```
1. Navigate to: Catalog > Products > Add Product
   Select: Configurable Product

2. Basic Info:
   - Attribute Set: Clothing (must contain Color + Size)
   - Product Name: "Classic Cotton T-Shirt"
   - SKU: cotton-tshirt
   - Price: 24.99  (placeholder; shown as "as low as")
   - Status: Enabled
   - Visibility: Catalog, Search

3. Click the "Configuration" tab
   Click "Create Configurations" button

4. Step 1 - Select Attributes:
   - Check "Color" ✓
   - Check "Size" ✓
   - Click "Next"

5. Step 2 - Attribute Values:
   Color: [x] Red  [x] Blue  [x] White
   Size:  [x] S    [x] M     [x] L     [x] XL
   Click "Next"

6. Step 3 - Bulk Images, Price, Qty:
   Images: Apply unique images by attribute (Color)
     - Upload red image for Red
     - Upload blue image for Blue
   Price: Apply unique prices by attribute (or keep same)
   Qty:   Apply single quantity to each SKU: 50
   Click "Next"

7. Step 4 - Summary:
   Review 12 child variations (3 colors x 4 sizes)
   Click "Generate Products"

8. Save the parent product.
   Verify:
   - Child simples appear in Products grid
   - Each child has: cotton-tshirt-Red-S, etc.
   - Inventory on parent = not meaningful
```

### Creating a Bundle Product — Step by Step

```
1. Navigate to: Catalog > Products > Add Product
   Select: Bundle Product

2. Basic Info:
   - Product Name: "Home Office Bundle"
   - SKU: home-office-bundle (fixed SKU base)
   - Dynamic Price: No  (Fixed at $399)
   - Price: 399.00
   - Dynamic SKU: No
   - Status: Enabled
   - Visibility: Catalog, Search

3. Scroll to "Bundle Items" section
   Click "Add Option"

   Option 1:
   - Option Title: "Desk Chair"
   - Input Type: Radio Buttons
   - Required: Yes
   - Click "Add Products to Option"
     Search: "Ergonomic Chair A"  -> Add  (qty: 1, default: Yes)
     Search: "Budget Chair B"     -> Add  (qty: 1, default: No)

4. Click "Add Option" again

   Option 2:
   - Option Title: "Desk Lamp"
   - Input Type: Checkbox
   - Required: No
   - Click "Add Products to Option"
     Search: "LED Desk Lamp"       -> Add  (qty: 1, default: Yes)
     Search: "Halogen Desk Lamp"   -> Add  (qty: 1, default: No)

5. Save.
   Verify:
   - PDP shows base price $399
   - If selection price values are $0, total stays $399 regardless of choice
   - If selections have non-zero price values, total = $399 + adjustments
   - Required option (Chair) must be selected to add to cart
   - Optional option (Lamp) can be unchecked
```

---

## 15. Tricky Exam Gotchas

These are the most commonly missed concepts — study these carefully.

### Gotcha 1: Configurable Stock = Child Level

```
Q: You set qty=100 on a Configurable parent product. How many items can be sold?
A: Depends ENTIRELY on the stock of child simples.
   Setting qty on the parent has NO effect.
```

### Gotcha 2: Grouped Product Has No Price

```
Q: A merchant wants all items in a Grouped product to share one price.
   How do you set the group's price?
A: You CANNOT. Grouped products have no group-level price.
   Each associated product has its own price.
   If you want a single price, use a Bundle with Fixed pricing instead.
```

### Gotcha 3: Bundle Dynamic vs Fixed — What Changes

```
Dynamic Price:  Final price = sum of actual product prices of selected options
                Bundle base price = $0 (not editable)
Fixed Price:    Final price = bundle base price + selection price adjustments
                Selections can add fixed $ or % adjustments to the base
                If all adjustments are $0, total = base price regardless of selections

These are INDEPENDENT of Dynamic SKU vs Fixed SKU.
```

### Gotcha 4: Downloadable Max Downloads = 0

```
Max Downloads = 0 --> UNLIMITED downloads
Max Downloads = 1 --> Can be downloaded ONCE
Max Downloads = 5 --> Can be downloaded up to 5 times
```

### Gotcha 5: Virtual Product and Checkout

```
Cart with ONLY Virtual products:
  --> Shipping step SKIPPED in checkout

Cart with Virtual + Simple:
  --> Shipping step SHOWN normally
```

### Gotcha 6: Configurable Attribute Must Be Global + Dropdown-like

```
Text field attributes --> CANNOT be configurable axes
Dropdown (global)     --> CAN be configurable axes
Website-scoped attr   --> CANNOT be configurable axes
Store View-scoped     --> CANNOT be configurable axes
```

### Gotcha 7: Bundle Required vs Optional Options

```
Required option with 0 stock --> Bundle is OUT OF STOCK
Optional option with 0 stock --> Bundle can STILL be purchased
                                 (user just can't select that option)
```

### Gotcha 8: Simple Product as Child vs Standalone

```
A Simple product used as a child of a Configurable CAN also be:
  - Sold standalone (if Visibility = Catalog, Search)
  - Part of multiple Configurable products
  - Part of Grouped products simultaneously

Usually child simples are set to:
  Visibility = "Not Visible Individually"
  so they don't appear as duplicates in catalog
```

> **Exam focus:** Child simples of a Configurable product are typically set to **"Not Visible Individually"** to avoid duplicate listings. However, they can still be ordered directly if the customer knows the direct URL or accesses via the configurable PDP.

### Gotcha 9: Attribute Set Cannot Be Unset

```
Every product MUST belong to an attribute set.
You can CHANGE the attribute set after creation, but
this may cause data loss for attributes not in the new set.
```

### Gotcha 10: Downloadable Product Links vs Samples

```
Samples: Free preview, available before purchase
Links:   Gated content, delivered after successful payment
         Each link can have its own additional price delta
```

---

## Quick-Reference Checklist

### Product Types

- [ ] **Simple** — single SKU, own price, own stock, has weight; building block for other types
- [ ] **Configurable** — parent + child simples; stock tracked at child level ONLY; parent has no own stock
- [ ] **Configurable** — parent price shown as "as low as" lowest child price; price updates on variant selection
- [ ] **Configurable attribute** must be: Dropdown/Visual Swatch/Text Swatch + Global scope + "Use to create configurable" = Yes
- [ ] **Grouped** — collection of simples shown together; NO group price; NO group stock; each child has own price
- [ ] **Grouped** — items added to cart as separate line items, not as one grouped line
- [ ] **Bundle Dynamic** — price = sum of selected option prices; shown as "From $X to $Y"
- [ ] **Bundle Fixed** — base price on bundle + selection price adjustments (fixed $ or %); if all adjustments = $0, total equals base price
- [ ] **Bundle** — has two independent settings: Price Type (Dynamic/Fixed) AND SKU Type (Dynamic/Fixed)
- [ ] **Bundle required option OOS** → bundle is OOS; optional option OOS → bundle still saleable
- [ ] **Virtual** — no weight, no shipping; checkout skips shipping step if all items are virtual
- [ ] **Downloadable** — no shipping; has Links (gated) and Samples (free preview)
- [ ] **Downloadable Max Downloads = 0** → unlimited (not zero!)
- [ ] **Downloadable link access** controlled by download count + order status — no time-based "links valid for N days" setting exists

### Catalog Configuration

- [ ] **Attribute Input Types** usable as configurable axes: Dropdown, Visual Swatch, Text Swatch (NOT text field)
- [ ] **Attribute Scope** must be **Global** for configurable axes
- [ ] **Price attribute** is **Website scope** by default
- [ ] **SKU attribute** is **Global scope**
- [ ] **Attribute Sets** group attributes into tabs in the admin product form
- [ ] **Default attribute set** cannot be deleted
- [ ] Changing a product's attribute set may cause data loss for non-matching attributes
- [ ] **System attributes** cannot be deleted; custom attributes can be if not system-required

### Swatches

- [ ] Swatches are configured as an **Input Type** on the attribute (Visual Swatch / Text Swatch)
- [ ] Work like dropdowns for configurable product axes but render as clickable UI elements
- [ ] Swatch display settings: Stores > Config > Catalog > Storefront

### Inventory

- [ ] Simple, Virtual, Downloadable: stock on the product itself
- [ ] Configurable: stock on child simples; parent qty is irrelevant
- [ ] Grouped: stock on each individual member product
- [ ] Bundle: stock on each component simple; required options must have stock
- [ ] MSI (Magento 2.3+): Sources + Stocks architecture; stock = aggregate from sources

### Pricing

- [ ] Special price on Configurable → set on **child simples**, not parent
- [ ] Grouped → no group price; each member has own price
- [ ] Bundle Dynamic → price = sum of selected options (special prices apply to components)
- [ ] Bundle Fixed → single price on bundle (special prices apply to bundle itself)
- [ ] Tier pricing available on Simple, Virtual, Downloadable, and Configurable (at child level)
- [ ] Downloadable base price + optional additional price per link

### Admin Form Key Differences

- [ ] Configurable has **"Create Configurations" button** under Configurations tab
- [ ] Bundle has **"Bundle Items" section** with Add Option and Dynamic Price toggle
- [ ] Bundle with Dynamic Price = Yes → Price field is **disabled** in admin
- [ ] Configurable axes cannot be changed after creation through standard UI
- [ ] Grouped product admin form has **no Price field** at product level
- [ ] Child simples set to **"Not Visible Individually"** to avoid duplicate catalog listings

flashcards.question: Which three attribute input types can be used as configurable product axes in Magento 2?
flashcards.answer: Dropdown, Visual Swatch, and Text Swatch. These are the only input types that support configurable product variations. Text fields, multiselect, and other types cannot be used.
flashcards.hint: Think about the types that allow single-value selection and can be rendered visually on the PDP.

flashcards.question: Where is inventory tracked for a Configurable product in Magento 2?
flashcards.answer: Inventory is tracked exclusively on the child Simple products. The parent Configurable product's qty field is ignored — setting qty on the parent has no effect on stock availability.
flashcards.hint: The parent is essentially a shell; the real sellable items are its children.

flashcards.question: What happens when a customer adds items from a Grouped product to the cart?
flashcards.answer: Each associated Simple product is added as a separate line item in the cart. There is no single grouped line item — the customer pays for each product at its own price independently.
flashcards.hint: Unlike Bundle products, Grouped products do not create a single combined cart entry.

flashcards.question: What is the difference between Dynamic Pricing and Fixed Pricing on a Bundle product?
flashcards.answer: Dynamic Pricing calculates the final price as the sum of selected component prices (bundle base = $0). Fixed Pricing uses a manually set base price plus optional selection adjustments (fixed $ or % of base). These are independent of the Dynamic/Fixed SKU setting.
flashcards.hint: One derives from children, the other starts with its own base price.

flashcards.question: What does Max Downloads = 0 mean for a Downloadable product in Magento 2?
flashcards.answer: Max Downloads = 0 means unlimited downloads, not zero downloads. The customer can download the file as many times as they want. Setting it to 1 would limit them to a single download.
flashcards.hint: Zero is the 'no limit' value, which is counterintuitive.

flashcards.question: What scope must a product attribute have to be used as a configurable product axis?
flashcards.answer: The attribute must have Global scope. Website-scoped and Store View-scoped attributes cannot be used as configurable axes, even if they have the correct input type (Dropdown/Swatch).
flashcards.hint: Configurable variations must be consistent across the entire installation.

flashcards.question: What happens to checkout when a cart contains only Virtual products?
flashcards.answer: The shipping step is completely skipped during checkout. If even one physical product is added to the cart, the shipping step displays normally for the entire order.
flashcards.hint: No physical goods means no shipping address or method is needed.

flashcards.question: Can a Simple product be a child of multiple Configurable products simultaneously?
flashcards.answer: Yes. A Simple product can be associated as a child of multiple Configurable products and can also be sold standalone. Child simples are typically set to 'Not Visible Individually' to avoid duplicate catalog listings.
flashcards.hint: Visibility settings control whether the child appears independently in search and catalog.

flashcards.question: What happens if you change a product's Attribute Set after creation?
flashcards.answer: Changing a product's Attribute Set is allowed, but it will remove attribute values that are not present in the new set. This is a destructive operation that can cause data loss for non-matching attributes.
flashcards.hint: Attributes exclusive to the old set lose their stored values permanently.

flashcards.question: What is the default price scope for the Price attribute in Magento 2?
flashcards.answer: The Price attribute has Website scope by default, meaning each website can have different product prices. SKU, by contrast, is Global scope. Price scope can be changed to Global in Catalog configuration.
flashcards.hint: This allows multi-currency or region-based pricing across different websites.

flashcards.question: How does Customizable Options differ from Configurable product variations?
flashcards.answer: Customizable Options (e.g., engraving text, file uploads) add a price delta to the base product without creating new SKUs. Configurable product variations use separate child Simple products, each with its own distinct SKU and inventory.
flashcards.hint: One modifies the existing product; the other resolves to a different product entirely.

flashcards.question: What determines whether a Bundle product is in stock or out of stock?
flashcards.answer: A Bundle product is out of stock if any required component option has no in-stock selections available. Optional components being out of stock do not prevent the bundle from being purchased.
flashcards.hint: Required vs optional is the key distinction for bundle availability.

flashcards.question: Does a Grouped product have its own price field in the admin?
flashcards.answer: No. A Grouped product has no group-level price field — it is grayed out or absent in the admin form. Each associated Simple product retains its own individual price. There is no way to set a single group price.
flashcards.hint: If a merchant wants one combined price, they should use a Bundle with Fixed pricing instead.

flashcards.question: How is downloadable link access controlled in Magento 2?
flashcards.answer: Downloadable link access is controlled by download count (Max Downloads per link, 0 = unlimited) and order status (links become available when the order reaches the configured status, default: Invoiced). There is no time-based link expiry setting.
flashcards.hint: There are only two control mechanisms — count and order status — no calendar-based expiration.

flashcards.question: On a Bundle product with Dynamic Price = Yes, what happens to the Price field in the admin?
flashcards.answer: The Price field is disabled (grayed out) because the price is automatically calculated from the sum of selected component prices. You must set Dynamic Price = No (Fixed) to manually enter a base price on the bundle.
flashcards.hint: Dynamic pricing means the system calculates it — manual entry is blocked.

studyNotes.title: Day 2 — Pricing, Promotions & Catalog Price Rules
studyNotes.content:
# Pricing, Promotions & Catalog Price Rules
## Adobe Commerce / Magento 2 Certification Study Notes

---

## Table of Contents

1. [Price Types Overview](#1-price-types-overview)
2. [Special Price](#2-special-price)
3. [Tier Pricing](#3-tier-pricing)
4. [Group Pricing](#4-group-pricing)
5. [Catalog Price Rules](#5-catalog-price-rules)
6. [Cart Price Rules](#6-cart-price-rules)
7. [Price Display: Tax Inclusion/Exclusion](#7-price-display-tax-inclusionexclusion)
8. [Minimum Advertised Price (MAP)](#8-minimum-advertised-price-map)
9. [Price Precedence & Rule Interaction](#9-price-precedence--rule-interaction)
10. [Hands-On Scenarios](#10-hands-on-scenarios)
11. [Quick-Reference Checklist](#quick-reference-checklist)

---

## 1. Price Types Overview

Magento 2 / Adobe Commerce supports several distinct price types that can apply to a product simultaneously. Understanding which price "wins" is critical for exam success.

| Price Type | Where Configured | Scope | Applies To |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Regular Price** | Product > Price field | Website | All customers |
| **Special Price** | Product > Special Price | Website | All customers (date-optional) |
| **Tier Price** | Product > Advanced Pricing | Website | Quantity-based breaks, per customer group |
| **Group Price** | Product > Advanced Pricing | Website | Specific customer groups (qty = 1) |
| **Catalog Price Rule** | Marketing > Catalog Price Rules | Website | Dynamic discount via conditions |

```
Price Resolution Order (simplified):

  Regular Price                                      
       |                                             
       v                                             
  Special Price (if active & dated)  <-- overrides regular
       |                                             
       v                                             
  Tier / Group Price  <-- compared against current price
       |                                             
       v                                             
  Catalog Price Rule  <-- applied to the lowest price so far
       |                                             
       v                                             
  Final Product Price (displayed on storefront)      
```

> **Exam focus:** The system always displays the **lowest applicable price** to the customer. Understanding which price type can override another is a frequent exam topic.

---

## 2. Special Price

### Configuration Path
`Catalog > Products > [Product] > Advanced Pricing > Special Price`

### Key Characteristics

- Can have an optional **From / To date range**
- When active, the Special Price **replaces** (not discounts from) the regular price for storefront display
- The original regular price is shown as a strikethrough
- Applied at the **product level**, not rule-driven

```php
// Magento calculates final price using FinalPriceCalculator
// Special price check happens in:
// vendor/magento/module-catalog/Model/Product/Type/Price.php

public function getFinalPrice($qty, $product)
{
    // Special price is evaluated before catalog rules
    $specialPrice = $product->getSpecialPrice();
    if ($this->_isSpecialPriceEnabled($product, $specialPrice)) {
        // Special price wins if lower than regular
        $finalPrice = min($finalPrice, $specialPrice);
    }
}
```

### Special Price Date Handling

| Field | Behavior |
|---|---|
| `Special Price From Date` | Blank = active immediately |
| `Special Price To Date` | Blank = never expires |
| Time zone | Uses **store time zone** for evaluation |

> **Exam focus:** A Special Price with **no dates** is always active. With dates, it activates/deactivates automatically via cron. Special price takes precedence over a Catalog Price Rule when **both apply** — but verify which is actually lower in your specific scenario.

---

## 3. Tier Pricing

### Configuration Path
`Catalog > Products > [Product] > Advanced Pricing > Tier Price`

### Key Characteristics

- **Quantity-based** discounts (buy 5 or more, get 10% off)
- Can be scoped to:
  - `ALL GROUPS` — applies to all customer groups including guests
  - Specific customer group
- Can be set as:
  - **Fixed price** per unit at that quantity
  - **Discount** (percentage off)
- Multiple tiers can be defined for the same product

### Example Tier Price Table

| Customer Group | Qty | Price Type | Amount |
|---|---|---|---|
| ALL GROUPS | 5 | Fixed | $45.00 |
| ALL GROUPS | 10 | Discount | 15% |
| Wholesale | 1 | Fixed | $38.00 |
| Wholesale | 5 | Fixed | $32.00 |

```xml
<!-- Tier price in product import CSV / XML structure -->
<tier_prices>
    <item>
        <customer_group_id>0</customer_group_id> <!-- ALL GROUPS -->
        <qty>5</qty>
        <value>45.00</value>
        <extension_attributes>
            <website_id>0</website_id>
            <percentage_value>0</percentage_value>
        </extension_attributes>
    </item>
</tier_prices>
```

> **Exam focus:** Tier prices for a specific customer group take priority over `ALL GROUPS` tier prices for that same quantity break. The system picks the **most specific and lowest** applicable tier.

---

## 4. Group Pricing

### Configuration Path
`Catalog > Products > [Product] > Advanced Pricing > Tier Price`
(Group pricing is implemented as a tier price entry with `qty = 1`)

### Key Characteristics

- Effectively a **Tier Price at quantity 1** for a specific customer group
- Used to give a flat per-unit discount to groups like "Retailer" or "Wholesale"
- If a customer belongs to a group with a group price defined, that price replaces the regular price as the baseline

```
Customer Group: Wholesale
Regular Price:  $100.00
Group Price:    $80.00   <-- baseline for this group
Tier (qty=5):  $70.00   <-- applied when cart qty >= 5
```

> **Exam focus:** Group price is stored in the same `tier_price` table as regular tier prices. There is **no separate "group price" database table** in Magento 2 (unlike Magento 1). This is a common trick question.

---

## 5. Catalog Price Rules

Catalog Price Rules are promotional rules applied **before the customer adds to cart**. They modify the displayed product price on category pages, product pages, and search results.

### Navigation
`Marketing > Promotions > Catalog Price Rules`

### Rule Components

```
+------------------+
|   Catalog Rule   |
+------------------+
| 1. General Info  |  --> Name, Status, Websites, Customer Groups
| 2. Conditions    |  --> What products qualify?
| 3. Actions       |  --> How to modify the price?
| 4. Priority      |  --> Order of rule application
+------------------+
```

### 5.1 General Info Settings

| Field | Description |
|---|---|
| **Status** | Active / Inactive |
| **Websites** | Which store views/websites the rule applies to |
| **Customer Groups** | NOT LOGGED IN, General, Wholesale, Retailer |
| **From / To Date** | Optional date range for the rule |
| **Priority** | Integer; **lower number = higher priority** |
| **Stop Further Rules Processing** | Prevents lower-priority rules from applying |

### 5.2 Conditions

Conditions determine **which products** the rule applies to. They use a condition tree similar to cart price rules.

**Available Condition Attributes:**

- Category (product is in category X)
- Attribute Set
- Product attribute values (color, size, brand, etc.)
- Price
- SKU

```
Condition Tree Example:
IF ALL of these conditions are TRUE:
  - Category IS "Summer Sale"
  - Attribute: Color IS "Red" OR "Blue"
  - Price >= 20.00
THEN apply action...
```

> **Exam focus:** Catalog price rule conditions match on **product attributes** and **categories**. They do **not** have access to cart/customer data (use Cart Price Rules for that).

### 5.3 Action Types

| Action | Description | Example |
|---|---|---|
| **By Percentage of the Original Price** | Reduces price by X% | 20% off → $100 becomes $80 |
| **By Fixed Amount** | Reduces price by flat dollar amount | $15 off → $100 becomes $85 |
| **To Percentage of the Original Price** | Sets price to X% of original | Set to 75% → $100 becomes $75 |
| **To Fixed Amount** | Sets price to exact dollar amount | Set to $49.99 |

> **Exam focus:** "By Percentage" vs "To Percentage" is a very common exam trap:
> - **"By Percentage"** = discount *by* that percentage (subtract)
> - **"To Percentage"** = set price *to* that percentage of original (multiply)

### 5.4 Priority and Rule Stacking

```
Rule A:  Priority 1  (highest priority, applies first)
Rule B:  Priority 2
Rule C:  Priority 5
Rule D:  Priority 10 (lowest priority, applies last)

Without "Stop Further Rules Processing":
  All matching rules apply in priority order

With "Stop Further Rules Processing" on Rule A:
  Only Rule A applies; B, C, D are skipped
```

**How stacking works — step by step:**

```
Original Price: $100.00

Rule A (Priority 1): By Percentage 10%
  --> Price after Rule A: $90.00

Rule B (Priority 2): By Fixed Amount $5
  --> Price after Rule B: $85.00   <-- EACH RULE APPLIES TO THE RESULT OF THE PREVIOUS

Rule C (Priority 5): To Fixed Amount $79.99
  --> Price after Rule C: $79.99   <-- "To Fixed" uses min(amount, current price)
  --> If current price were already $75, it would stay $75 (can only lower, never raise)
```

> **Exam focus:** Catalog price rules apply **sequentially** in priority order. **All four action types** operate on the **already-discounted price** from earlier rules, not on the original price. Specifically: `to_fixed` uses min(action amount, current price) — it can only lower the price; `to_percent` calculates a percentage of the current (not original) price.

### 5.5 Applying Catalog Price Rules

After creating or modifying a catalog price rule, you must **apply** the rules to update indexed prices.

```bash
# Manually reindex catalog price rules
bin/magento indexer:reindex catalogrule_rule
bin/magento indexer:reindex catalogrule_product

# Or apply from admin:
# Marketing > Catalog Price Rules > Apply Rules (button)
```

> **Exam focus:** Catalog Price Rules are **index-based**. They require reindexing to take effect. Cart Price Rules are evaluated **at runtime** and do NOT require indexing.

---

## 6. Cart Price Rules

Cart Price Rules apply discounts **in the shopping cart**, after the customer has added items. They can use coupon codes and have access to cart/customer/address data.

### Navigation
`Marketing > Promotions > Cart Price Rules`

### Rule Components

```
+--------------------+
|   Cart Price Rule  |
+--------------------+
| 1. Rule Info       |  --> Name, Status, Websites, Customer Groups, Dates
| 2. Conditions      |  --> Cart/customer conditions
| 3. Actions         |  --> Discount type, coupon, free shipping
| 4. Labels          |  --> What the customer sees in cart
| 5. Related          |  --> Related cart price rules
+--------------------+
```

### 6.1 Rule Info Settings

| Field | Description |
|---|---|
| **Coupon** | No Coupon / Specific Coupon / Auto Generated |
| **Coupon Code** | The actual code customers enter |
| **Uses per Coupon** | Max total uses (0 = unlimited) |
| **Uses per Customer** | Max uses per individual customer (0 = unlimited) |
| **Priority** | Same as catalog rules; lower = higher priority |
| **Stop Further Rules Processing** | Prevents stacking with lower-priority cart rules |

### 6.2 Conditions Tab

Cart price rule conditions have access to richer data than catalog rules:

**Condition Sources:**

| Source | Examples |
|---|---|
| **Cart attributes** | Subtotal, Total Items Qty, Total Weight, Payment Method, Shipping Method |
| **Product attributes** | SKU, Category, Attribute values (per line item) |
| **Customer attributes** | Customer Group (set in Rule Info, not conditions) |
| **Address** | Shipping Country, Region, Postcode |

```
Condition Example:
IF ALL of these conditions are TRUE:
  - Subtotal >= 50.00
  - Shipping Country IS "United States"
  - Product Category IS "Electronics"
THEN apply 10% discount
```

### 6.3 Action Types

| Action | Description |
|---|---|
| **Percent of product price discount** | X% off each qualifying item |
| **Fixed amount discount** | Flat dollar off each qualifying item |
| **Fixed amount discount for whole cart** | Flat dollar off cart total |
| **Buy X get Y free (discount amount is Y)** | BXGY promotion |

#### Buy X Get Y Free (BXGY)

```
Action: Buy X get Y free
Buy (X): 2        <-- Customer must buy this many
Free (Y): 1       <-- This many items are free
Maximum Qty Discount is Applied To: 1
```

> **Exam focus:** In BXGY, the "Discount Amount" field represents **Y** (the number of free items), not a dollar amount or percentage. The cheapest qualifying items are made free.

### 6.4 Free Shipping Action

Cart Price Rules can grant **Free Shipping** in addition to (or instead of) a price discount:

| Free Shipping Option | Behavior |
|---|---|
| **No** | No free shipping applied |
| **For matching items only** | Only cart items matching the conditions get free shipping |
| **For shipment with matching items** | Entire shipment is free if any item matches |

```
Example Rule: "$75+ gets free shipping"
Condition: Subtotal >= 75.00
Discount Amount: 0  (no price discount)
Free Shipping: For shipment with matching items
```

### 6.5 Coupon Codes

```
Coupon Type Options:
  - No Coupon        --> Rule applies automatically (auto-applied)
  - Specific Coupon  --> Customer must enter a code
  - Auto Generated   --> System generates unique codes (bulk)
```

```bash
# Generate coupon codes via CLI (Magento 2.4+)
# Not natively available - typically done via Admin UI or custom script
# Admin path: Marketing > Cart Price Rules > [Rule] > Manage Coupon Codes
```

> **Exam focus:** Rules with **"No Coupon"** apply automatically to qualifying carts. Rules with **"Specific Coupon"** only apply when the code is entered. Auto-applied rules still respect priority and Stop Further Rules Processing.

### 6.6 Cart Rule Stacking

```
Without "Stop Further Rules Processing":

  Cart Rule 1 (Priority 1, No Coupon): 10% off
    --> Applied automatically

  Cart Rule 2 (Priority 2, Coupon: SAVE5): $5 off
    --> Applied when coupon entered
    --> STACKS with Rule 1

  Cart Rule 3 (Priority 3, No Coupon): 5% off
    --> Also auto-applied
    --> STACKS with Rules 1 and 2

Result: All three discounts apply
```

```
With "Stop Further Rules Processing" on Cart Rule 1:

  Cart Rule 1 (Priority 1): 10% off  --> Applies
  Cart Rule 2 (Priority 2): $5 off   --> SKIPPED
  Cart Rule 3 (Priority 3): 5% off   --> SKIPPED

Result: Only Rule 1 discount applies
```

> **Exam focus:** **Cart rules stack by default.** The "Stop Further Rules Processing" flag on a cart rule stops ALL lower-priority cart rules, including coupon-based ones. If a customer enters a coupon code but a higher-priority rule has "Stop Further Rules" checked, their coupon **will not apply**.

---

## 7. Price Display: Tax Inclusion/Exclusion

### Configuration Path
`Stores > Configuration > Sales > Tax > Price Display Settings`

### 7.1 Display Settings by Context

| Context | Config Option | Values |
|---|---|---|
| **Catalog (category/product pages)** | Display Product Prices In Catalog | Excluding Tax / Including Tax / Including and Excluding Tax |
| **Shopping Cart** | Display Prices In Shopping Cart | Excluding Tax / Including Tax / Including and Excluding Tax |
| **Orders, Invoices, Credit Memos** | Display Prices In Orders, Invoices, Credit Memos | Excluding Tax / Including Tax / Including and Excluding Tax |

### 7.2 Tax Calculation vs. Display

> **Important distinction:** Tax **calculation** settings (how tax is computed) are separate from **display** settings (how prices are shown).

```
Example:
  Product Price:    $100.00 (excluding tax)
  Tax Rate:         10%

  Display: "Including Tax"  --> Customer sees $110.00
  Display: "Excluding Tax"  --> Customer sees $100.00
  Display: "Including and Excluding Tax" --> Customer sees both:
    $110.00 (Incl. Tax) / $100.00 (Excl. Tax)
```

### 7.3 Cross-Border Tax Display

When the shipping destination changes the tax rate, prices can appear to change. This is controlled by:
- `Stores > Configuration > Sales > Tax > Calculation Settings > Catalog Prices`
- Options: **Excluding Tax** or **Including Tax**

> **Exam focus:** Setting "Catalog Prices" to "Including Tax" means the system **back-calculates** the base price when tax is applied. This is the EU/Australian pricing model. Mixing this with "Display: Excluding Tax" can cause price display confusion — a classic exam scenario.

---

## 8. Minimum Advertised Price (MAP)

### Configuration Path
`Stores > Configuration > Sales > Minimum Advertised Price`

### What is MAP?

MAP (Minimum Advertised Price) is a manufacturer's policy that prevents retailers from publicly advertising a product below a certain price. Magento supports this by allowing products to be sold at the MAP price but **hiding** the actual selling price on catalog pages.

### 8.1 Global MAP Settings

| Setting | Description |
|---|---|
| **Enable MAP** | Yes / No |
| **Display Actual Price** | On Gesture / In Cart / Before Order Confirmation |
| **Default Popup Text Message** | Text shown to customers about the actual price |
| **Default "What's This?" Text** | Link text that triggers the price popup |

### 8.2 Product-Level MAP

On each product, you can set:
- `Advanced Pricing > Manufacturer's Suggested Retail Price (MSRP)` — the displayed/advertised price
- `Advanced Pricing > Display Actual Price` — override the global display setting per product

### 8.3 MAP Display Behavior

```
MAP Enabled + Product has MSRP set:

  Category Page:     Shows "Add to Cart" button only, NO price displayed
  Product Page:      Shows MSRP with "Click for price" link (or popup)
  Cart:              Shows actual (sale) price

  Customer journey:
  [Category] --> Add to Cart (no price)
              --> [Cart] Actual price revealed
```

| Display Actual Price Setting | Where Actual Price Shows |
|---|---|
| **On Gesture** | Only when customer clicks "What's This?" popup |
| **In Cart** | Only in the shopping cart |
| **Before Order Confirmation** | In cart and on order review page |

> **Exam focus:** When MAP is enabled and a product has an MSRP, the **"Add to Cart" button is shown instead of the price** on catalog pages. The actual price is only revealed based on the "Display Actual Price" setting. Catalog Price Rules and Special Prices still apply to the actual selling price — MAP only controls **display**.

---

## 9. Price Precedence & Rule Interaction

This is the most **exam-critical** section. Understanding exactly which price wins in each scenario is essential.

### 9.1 Catalog Price: What Wins?

```
Scenario: Product has Regular Price, Special Price, AND a Catalog Rule

Step 1: Start with Regular Price ($100)
Step 2: Check Special Price
        - If active: use Special Price ($85) as current price
Step 3: Check Catalog Rule
        - Rule: 20% off = $100 * 0.80 = $80
        - Compare: Special Price ($85) vs Catalog Rule ($80)
        - LOWER wins: $80 (Catalog Rule wins here)

BUT: 
Step 3 (alternate): Rule: 10% off = $100 * 0.90 = $90
        - Compare: Special Price ($85) vs Catalog Rule ($90)
        - LOWER wins: $85 (Special Price wins here)
```

> **Exam focus:** The common statement is "Special Price takes precedence over Catalog Rules" — but this is **NOT always true**. The system applies **both** and shows the **lower** of the two. The question is which one is numerically lower in the scenario given.

### 9.2 The Actual Magento Algorithm

```php
// Simplified from vendor/magento/module-catalog-rule/
// Model/ResourceModel/Rule/Product/Price.php

// Catalog rule price is stored after indexing
// At runtime, FinalPriceCalculator compares:

$priceOptions = [
    $regularPrice,
    $specialPrice,      // if active
    $tierPrice,         // best applicable tier
    $catalogRulePrice,  // from index
];

$finalPrice = min(array_filter($priceOptions, 'is_numeric'));
```

### 9.3 Priority and Precedence Summary

```
Price Type Interaction Matrix:

+------------------+------------------+--------------------+
|  Price Type      |  Beats           |  Loses To          |
+------------------+------------------+--------------------+
| Regular Price    | Nothing          | Everything         |
| Special Price    | Regular Price    | Lower-priced Rule  |
| Group Price      | Regular Price    | Special if lower   |
| Tier Price       | Group Price      | Special if lower   |
| Catalog Rule     | Regular Price    | Special if lower   |
+------------------+------------------+--------------------+

RULE: The LOWEST applicable price always wins for display.
```

### 9.4 Cart Rules vs. Catalog Rules

| Aspect | Catalog Price Rule | Cart Price Rule |
|---|---|---|
| **When applied** | Before add to cart (product price) | In shopping cart |
| **Requires indexing** | YES | NO (runtime) |
| **Coupon codes** | NO | YES |
| **Conditions on cart** | NO | YES |
| **Free shipping** | NO | YES |
| **BXGY** | NO | YES |
| **Stacks by default** | YES | YES |
| **Stop further rules** | YES | YES |
| **Visible on** | Product/Category pages | Cart/Checkout |

> **Exam focus:** Catalog price rules require **reindexing**. Cart price rules do **not**. This is a frequent differentiator question.

### 9.5 Cart Rule Stacking Scenarios

```
Scenario A: Two auto-applied rules, no "Stop Further Rules"

  Rule 1 (Priority 1): 10% off subtotal
  Rule 2 (Priority 2): $10 off subtotal

  Cart subtotal: $100
  After Rule 1:  $90
  After Rule 2:  $80
  Final:         $80 (both rules stacked)

---

Scenario B: Rule 1 has "Stop Further Rules Processing" = YES

  Rule 1 (Priority 1): 10% off, STOP = YES
  Rule 2 (Priority 2): $10 off

  Cart subtotal: $100
  After Rule 1:  $90 (Rule 2 is skipped)
  Final:         $90

---

Scenario C: Customer enters a coupon for Rule 2, Rule 1 has STOP

  Rule 1 (Priority 1): 10% off, STOP = YES (auto-applied)
  Rule 2 (Priority 2): COUPON "SAVE10" = $10 off

  Cart subtotal: $100
  After Rule 1:  $90 (Rule 2 is SKIPPED even with valid coupon)
  Final:         $90
  Coupon message: Coupon code is not valid or not applicable
```

> **Exam focus:** Scenario C above is a **classic exam trap**. A customer entering a valid coupon code may see it rejected because a higher-priority auto-applied rule has "Stop Further Rules Processing" enabled. This is expected Magento behavior, not a bug.

---

## 10. Hands-On Scenarios

### 10.1 Creating a Catalog Price Rule

```
Step 1: Navigate to Marketing > Promotions > Catalog Price Rules
Step 2: Click "Add New Rule"

--- Rule Information Tab ---
Rule Name:       Summer Sale 20% Off
Status:          Active
Websites:        Main Website
Customer Groups: NOT LOGGED IN, General, Wholesale, Retailer
From Date:       06/01/2024
To Date:         06/30/2024
Priority:        1
Stop Further Rules Processing: No

--- Conditions Tab ---
Conditions: (leave blank to apply to ALL products)
  OR
If ALL of these conditions are TRUE:
  Category IS 4 (Summer Collection)

--- Actions Tab ---
Apply:           By Percentage of the Original Price
Discount Amount: 20

Step 3: Save
Step 4: Click "Apply Rules" (or run bin/magento indexer:reindex)
```

### 10.2 Creating a Cart Price Rule with Coupon

```
Step 1: Navigate to Marketing > Promotions > Cart Price Rules
Step 2: Click "Add New Rule"

--- Rule Information Tab ---
Rule Name:       SUMMER10 - $10 Off $50+
Status:          Active
Websites:        Main Website
Customer Groups: NOT LOGGED IN, General
Coupon:          Specific Coupon
Coupon Code:     SUMMER10
Uses per Coupon: 100
Uses per Customer: 1
From Date:       06/01/2024
To Date:         06/30/2024
Priority:        5
Stop Further Rules Processing: No

--- Conditions Tab ---
Conditions:
  Cart Subtotal >= 50.00

--- Actions Tab ---
Apply:                               Fixed amount discount for whole cart
Discount Amount:                     10
Maximum Qty Discount is Applied To:  0
Apply to Shipping Amount:            No
Free Shipping:                       No

Step 3: Save (no reindexing needed)
```

### 10.3 Testing Rule Interaction

```
Test Matrix:

Setup:
  Product A: Regular $100, Special Price $85 (active)
  Catalog Rule: 20% off all products (Priority 1)
  Cart Rule:    SUMMER10 coupon, $10 off $50+ (Priority 5)

Test 1: View product on category page
  Expected: min($85 special, $100*0.80=$80 catalog rule) = $80
  Displayed: $80.00

Test 2: Add to cart (no coupon)
  Expected: $80 (from catalog rule / special price lower calculation)
  Subtotal:  $80

Test 3: Add coupon SUMMER10
  Condition check: $80 >= $50 --> TRUE
  Cart rule applies: $80 - $10 = $70
  Final cart total: $70

Test 4: Add "Stop Further Rules Processing" to Catalog Rule (cart rule)
  - Catalog rules and cart rules are INDEPENDENT systems
  - "Stop Further Rules" on catalog rule only stops OTHER catalog rules
  - Cart rules are unaffected
  Note: "Stop Further Rules" on CART RULE would stop other cart rules
```

### 10.4 Verifying Prices in Database

```sql
-- Check catalog rule prices in index
SELECT * FROM catalogrule_product_price
WHERE product_id = 123
AND rule_date = CURDATE();

-- Check tier/special prices
SELECT value, qty, customer_group_id, website_id
FROM catalog_product_entity_tier_price
WHERE entity_id = 123;

-- Check special price
SELECT value
FROM catalog_product_entity_decimal
WHERE attribute_id = (
  SELECT attribute_id FROM eav_attribute
  WHERE attribute_code = 'special_price'
  AND entity_type_id = 4
)
AND entity_id = 123;
```

---

## Quick-Reference Checklist

### Price Types
- [ ] **Regular Price** = base product price; everything else discounts from this
- [ ] **Special Price** = absolute price override; uses From/To date optional; always active if no dates set
- [ ] **Tier Price** = quantity-based breaks; can be fixed or percentage; scoped to customer group or ALL GROUPS
- [ ] **Group Price** = tier price at qty=1 for a specific customer group; same database table as tier prices
- [ ] The system displays the **lowest applicable price** — no single type "always wins"
- [ ] Special Price does NOT always beat Catalog Rule — whichever is **lower** wins

### Catalog Price Rules
- [ ] Path: `Marketing > Promotions > Catalog Price Rules`
- [ ] **Lower priority number = higher priority** (Priority 1 runs before Priority 10)
- [ ] 4 action types: By Percentage, By Fixed Amount, To Percentage, To Fixed Amount
- [ ] **"By Percentage"** = subtract that % | **"To Percentage"** = multiply to get that % of original
- [ ] Rules apply **sequentially**; each rule discounts from the already-discounted price
- [ ] Catalog rules require **reindexing** to take effect
- [ ] **No coupon codes** in catalog rules
- [ ] "Stop Further Rules Processing" stops lower-priority **catalog** rules only
- [ ] Conditions match **product attributes and categories** only (no cart data)

### Cart Price Rules
- [ ] Path: `Marketing > Promotions > Cart Price Rules`
- [ ] **No reindexing required** — evaluated at runtime
- [ ] Coupon types: No Coupon (auto), Specific Coupon, Auto Generated
- [ ] Rules **stack by default** unless "Stop Further Rules Processing" is enabled
- [ ] "Stop Further Rules Processing" blocks ALL lower-priority cart rules, including coupon-based ones
- [ ] Free Shipping options: No / For matching items only / For shipment with matching items
- [ ] BXGY: "Discount Amount" = Y (number of free items), not a dollar/percent value
- [ ] Cart rule conditions can use: subtotal, qty, weight, shipping method, payment method, product attributes, address fields

### Price Display & Tax
- [ ] 3 display contexts: Catalog pages / Cart / Orders+Invoices
- [ ] Each context independently set to: Excl. Tax / Incl. Tax / Both
- [ ] "Catalog Prices" base setting (excl. vs. incl.) affects tax back-calculation — EU model uses "Including Tax"

### Minimum Advertised Price (MAP)
- [ ] Requires: Enable MAP = Yes AND product has MSRP value set
- [ ] On catalog pages: **price is hidden**, only "Add to Cart" button shown
- [ ] "Display Actual Price" controls WHERE actual price is revealed: On Gesture / In Cart / Before Order Confirmation (3 options only)
- [ ] Discounts (special price, catalog rules) still apply to actual selling price — MAP only affects **display**

### Critical Exam Traps
- [ ] Special Price does NOT unconditionally win over Catalog Rules — **lower of the two wins**
- [ ] Catalog rules need indexing; cart rules do NOT
- [ ] "Stop Further Rules" on a HIGH-priority cart rule can silently block a customer's valid coupon
- [ ] Group price is stored in the **tier_price table**, not a separate table
- [ ] "By Percentage 20%" ≠ "To Percentage 20%" — "By" subtracts from current price; "To" sets current price to that % of current price
- [ ] All 4 catalog rule action types operate on the **current (already-discounted) price**, not the original — `to_fixed` uses min(amount, current)
- [ ] BXGY "Discount Amount" = number of free items (Y), not a monetary value
- [ ] MAP shows "Add to Cart" but **no price** on category pages — the selling price is still discounted normally
- [ ] Cart rules apply to the cart; catalog rules change the product's displayed price — they are **independent systems** that both contribute to what the customer ultimately pays

flashcards.question: What is the difference between 'By Percentage of the Original Price' and 'To Percentage of the Original Price' in Catalog Price Rules?
flashcards.answer: 'By Percentage' subtracts that percentage from the price (20% off $100 = $80). 'To Percentage' sets the price to that percentage of the original (75% of $100 = $75). This is a common exam trap.
flashcards.hint: 'By' means discount by that amount; 'To' means set the price to that fraction.

flashcards.question: Do Catalog Price Rules require reindexing to take effect?
flashcards.answer: Yes. Catalog Price Rules are index-based and require reindexing (catalogrule_rule and catalogrule_product indexers) or clicking 'Apply Rules' in admin. Cart Price Rules, by contrast, are evaluated at runtime and do NOT require reindexing.
flashcards.hint: One is pre-computed and stored; the other is calculated on the fly.

flashcards.question: What happens when a higher-priority Cart Price Rule has 'Stop Further Rules Processing' enabled and a customer enters a valid coupon for a lower-priority rule?
flashcards.answer: The customer's coupon will NOT apply. 'Stop Further Rules Processing' on a higher-priority rule blocks ALL lower-priority cart rules, including coupon-based ones. The coupon may show as 'not valid or not applicable.'
flashcards.hint: Priority takes precedence over coupon validity — it is a hard stop.

flashcards.question: In a Cart Price Rule with 'Buy X Get Y Free' action, what does the 'Discount Amount' field represent?
flashcards.answer: The Discount Amount field represents Y — the number of free items the customer receives, not a dollar amount or percentage. The cheapest qualifying items in the cart are made free.
flashcards.hint: It is a quantity of free items, not a monetary value.

flashcards.question: Does Special Price always take precedence over Catalog Price Rules?
flashcards.answer: No. The system applies both and displays the lower of the two. If a Catalog Price Rule produces a price of $80 and the Special Price is $85, the Catalog Rule price of $80 wins. The lowest applicable price always prevails.
flashcards.hint: It is not about precedence hierarchy but about which number is actually smaller.

flashcards.question: Where is Group Price stored in Magento 2's database?
flashcards.answer: Group Price is stored in the same tier_price table as regular tier prices, as a tier price entry with qty = 1 for a specific customer group. There is no separate 'group_price' database table in Magento 2 (unlike Magento 1).
flashcards.hint: It is technically just a tier price at quantity one.

flashcards.question: What does 'lower priority number' mean for Catalog Price Rules?
flashcards.answer: A lower priority number means higher priority — the rule runs first. Priority 1 applies before Priority 10. Rules apply sequentially, and each rule operates on the already-discounted price from earlier rules, not the original price.
flashcards.hint: Think of it like first place: number 1 goes first.

flashcards.question: What is the key difference between Catalog Price Rule conditions and Cart Price Rule conditions?
flashcards.answer: Catalog Price Rule conditions can only match product attributes and categories. Cart Price Rule conditions have access to richer data including cart subtotal, total qty, shipping method, payment method, address fields, and product attributes.
flashcards.hint: Catalog rules know about products; cart rules know about the entire shopping session.

flashcards.question: When MAP (Minimum Advertised Price) is enabled and a product has an MSRP set, what appears on catalog/category pages?
flashcards.answer: The 'Add to Cart' button is shown instead of the price on catalog pages. The actual selling price is only revealed based on the 'Display Actual Price' setting (On Gesture, In Cart, or Before Order Confirmation). Discounts still apply to the actual price — MAP only controls display.
flashcards.hint: MAP hides the price from public view but does not change the actual selling price.

flashcards.question: What happens to a Special Price when no From/To dates are set?
flashcards.answer: A Special Price with no dates is always active — it applies immediately and indefinitely. The From Date blank means active now; the To Date blank means it never expires. Time zone evaluation uses the store's configured time zone.
flashcards.hint: Blank dates mean no time restriction at all.

flashcards.question: How do multiple Catalog Price Rules stack when applied sequentially?
flashcards.answer: Each rule operates on the already-discounted price from the previous rule, not the original price. For example, Rule A (10% off $100 = $90) then Rule B ($5 off $90 = $85). The 'To Fixed Amount' action uses min(amount, current price) — it can only lower, never raise.
flashcards.hint: Each rule sees the result of the prior rule as its starting point.

flashcards.question: Can coupon codes be used with Catalog Price Rules?
flashcards.answer: No. Coupon codes are only available in Cart Price Rules. Catalog Price Rules apply automatically to all qualifying products based on conditions — they have no coupon code mechanism. Cart Price Rules support No Coupon (auto-applied), Specific Coupon, or Auto Generated codes.
flashcards.hint: Catalog rules affect displayed prices before add-to-cart; coupons are a cart-level concept.

flashcards.question: What are the three options for the Free Shipping field in a Cart Price Rule?
flashcards.answer: No (no free shipping), For matching items only (only items matching the conditions get free shipping), and For shipment with matching items (entire shipment is free if any item matches the conditions).
flashcards.hint: The scope ranges from none, to per-item, to the entire shipment.
