studyNotes.content:
# Magento 2 Customer Journey & Order Lifecycle
### Comprehensive Study Notes — Week 1: Core Features

---

## Table of Contents

1. [Customer Journey Overview](#1-customer-journey-overview)
2. [Product Detail Page (PDP) & Add to Cart](#2-product-detail-page-pdp--add-to-cart)
3. [Cart & Checkout Flow](#3-cart--checkout-flow)
4. [Order Confirmation & Transactional Email](#4-order-confirmation--transactional-email)
5. [Customer Account Features](#5-customer-account-features)
6. [Guest Checkout vs Required Login](#6-guest-checkout-vs-required-login)
7. [Order Lifecycle & Statuses](#7-order-lifecycle--statuses)
8. [Invoice: Payment Capture Record](#8-invoice-payment-capture-record)
9. [Shipment: Physical Delivery Tracking](#9-shipment-physical-delivery-tracking)
10. [Credit Memo: Refunds & Returns](#10-credit-memo-refunds--returns)
11. [Store Scope Hierarchy](#11-store-scope-hierarchy)
12. [Hands-On Admin Walkthrough](#12-hands-on-admin-walkthrough)
13. [Quick-Reference Checklist](#quick-reference-checklist)

---

## 1. Customer Journey Overview

The Magento 2 customer journey follows a well-defined funnel from discovery to post-purchase. Understanding each stage is essential for both exam questions and real-world implementation.

```
Browse/Land
    |
    v
Search / Category Browse
    |
    v
Product Detail Page (PDP)
    |
    v
Add to Cart
    |
    v
Cart Review
    |
    v
Checkout
    |--- Step 1: Shipping Address + Method
    |--- Step 2: Payment Method + Order Review
    |
    v
Order Placed (Order ID generated)
    |
    v
Confirmation Email Sent
    |
    v
Admin: Invoice -> Shipment -> (optionally) Credit Memo
```

### 1.1 Stage-by-Stage Breakdown

| Stage | Key Actions | Magento Entities Involved |
|---|---|---|
| **Browse** | View homepage, categories, promotions | CMS Pages, Categories, Banners |
| **Search** | Keyword or layered nav filtering | Elasticsearch, Search Config |
| **PDP** | View product, select options, read reviews | Product Entity, Reviews, Related Products |
| **Add to Cart** | Qty selection, custom options, grouped/bundle config | Quote Item, Cart (Quote) |
| **Cart** | Apply coupon, estimate shipping, update qty | Quote, CartPriceRule |
| **Checkout** | Enter shipping + payment | Address, Shipping Method, Payment Method |
| **Order Placed** | Submit payment | Order Entity (sales_order table) |
| **Confirmation** | Email sent, account updated | Email Template, Order History |

- **Exam focus:** The shopping cart in Magento 2 is technically a **Quote** object. It only becomes an **Order** after successful checkout submission.
- **Exam focus:** Layered navigation (faceted search) is powered by **Elasticsearch** in Magento 2.4+. MySQL search was deprecated.

---

## 2. Product Detail Page (PDP) & Add to Cart

### 2.1 PDP Key Components

- **Product images gallery** — multiple images, zoom, video support
- **Price display** — includes tier pricing, special prices, customer group pricing
- **Options selection** — configurable attributes (size/color), custom options, bundle selects
- **Qty selector** — minimum/maximum qty can be enforced via product settings
- **Add to Cart / Wishlist / Compare** buttons
- **Reviews & Ratings** block
- **Related / Up-sell / Cross-sell** products

### 2.2 Product Types & Add-to-Cart Behavior

| Product Type | Add to Cart Behavior |
|---|---|
| Simple | Direct add, no additional selection needed |
| Configurable | Must select all attribute options first |
| Grouped | Set qty for each child product |
| Bundle | Select components and qty |
| Virtual | No shipping required; still has checkout |
| Downloadable | No shipping; download link generated post-purchase |

- **Exam focus:** A **Virtual** product does not trigger the shipping step in checkout. A **Downloadable** product also skips shipping but generates a secure download link after invoice creation.

### 2.3 The Quote (Cart) Lifecycle

```
Empty Quote
    |
    v
addProduct() called
    |
    v
Quote Item(s) created (quote_item table)
    |
    v
Price Totals Collected
    |
    v
Checkout initiated
    |
    v
Quote converted to Order (sales_order table)
    |
    v
Quote marked as inactive
```

---

## 3. Cart & Checkout Flow

### 3.1 Cart Page Features

- **Mini-cart** (header) — quick view, quick remove
- **Full cart page** — qty edit, coupon code field, remove items
- **Estimate Shipping & Tax** widget
- **Proceed to Checkout** button

```
Cart Page
+------------------------------------------+
| Item | Qty | Price | Subtotal            |
|------|-----|-------|---------------------|
| SKU1 |  2  | $10   | $20                 |
| SKU2 |  1  | $25   | $25                 |
+------------------------------------------+
| Coupon Code: [________] [Apply]          |
| Estimate Shipping: [Country] [ZIP]       |
| Subtotal:  $45                           |
| Shipping:  $5.00                         |
| Tax:       $3.60                         |
| Grand Total: $53.60                      |
| [Proceed to Checkout]                    |
+------------------------------------------+
```

### 3.2 One-Page Checkout (OPC) Steps

Magento 2 introduced the **One-Page Checkout** — two visible steps on a single page using JavaScript/Ajax:

**Step 1: Shipping**
- Customer enters or selects shipping address
- Available shipping methods load dynamically
- Guest enters email (triggers "already have an account?" check)

**Step 2: Review & Payment**
- Select payment method
- Order summary sidebar
- Place Order button

- **Exam focus:** In Magento 2, checkout is **two steps** (Shipping → Review & Payment), not the legacy Magento 1 six-step process.
- **Exam focus:** The email field at checkout step 1 is used for both guest identification and the **order confirmation email**. It also determines if the email already exists (account merge prompt).

### 3.3 Shipping Methods Available by Default

| Method | Config Path |
|---|---|
| Flat Rate | Stores > Config > Sales > Shipping Methods > Flat Rate |
| Free Shipping | Stores > Config > Sales > Shipping Methods > Free Shipping |
| Table Rate | CSV-based; weight/price/destination rules |
| UPS / FedEx / USPS / DHL | Live carrier APIs — require API credentials |

### 3.4 Payment Methods Available by Default

| Method | Notes |
|---|---|
| Check / Money Order | Offline; no capture until manual invoice |
| Bank Transfer | Offline |
| Cash on Delivery | Offline |
| Zero Subtotal | Used when order total = $0 (e.g., 100% coupon) |
| PayPal Express | Popular online method; redirects to PayPal |

- **Exam focus:** **Offline payment methods** (Check/Money Order, Bank Transfer) do **not** capture payment automatically. An admin must manually create an Invoice to record payment.
- **Exam focus:** **Online payment methods** (PayPal, Braintree) can be configured for **Authorize Only** or **Authorize & Capture** (immediate).

---

## 4. Order Confirmation & Transactional Email

### 4.1 What Triggers the Confirmation Email

After the customer clicks **Place Order**:

1. Order entity is persisted to `sales_order` table
2. Magento dispatches `checkout_onepage_controller_success_action` event
3. Order confirmation email is queued/sent to customer
4. If guest checkout — email contains a "track order" link only (no account)
5. If logged in — order appears in **My Account > My Orders**

### 4.2 Transactional Emails in Admin

- **Location:** `Marketing > Communications > Email Templates`
- **Config:** `Stores > Configuration > Sales > Sales Emails`
- **Default templates:** New Order, New Order (Guest), Order Comment, Invoice, Shipment, Credit Memo

```
Sales Emails Config (Stores > Config > Sales > Sales Emails)
+------------------------------------------+
| Orders                                   |
|  Enabled:         Yes                    |
|  New Order Confirmation Email: [To]      |
|  New Order Email Template: [Template]    |
|  New Order Email Template for Guest      |
|  Send Order Email Copy To: [email]       |
|  Send Order Email Copy Method: BCC/Copy  |
+------------------------------------------+
```

- **Exam focus:** Separate email templates exist for **logged-in customers** and **guests**. The guest template does not include account-specific links.
- **Exam focus:** The **"Send Copy To"** field accepts a comma-separated list of email addresses that receive a copy (BCC or separate copy) of every transactional email of that type.

---

## 5. Customer Account Features

### 5.1 My Account Dashboard

```
My Account
+---------------------------+
| Dashboard                 |
| My Orders                 |
| My Downloadable Products  |
| My Wish List              |
| Address Book              |
| Account Information       |
| Stored Payment Methods    |
| My Product Reviews        |
+---------------------------+
```

### 5.2 Address Book

- Customer can store **multiple addresses**
- Designate a **default billing** and **default shipping** address
- Addresses pre-populate checkout fields
- Admin can also manage customer addresses: `Customers > All Customers > [Customer] > Addresses`

- **Exam focus:** A customer can have **one default billing** and **one default shipping** address, but can store unlimited additional addresses in the address book.

### 5.3 Order History

- Lists all orders placed by the customer
- Customer can:
  - **View** order details
  - **Reorder** (adds same items back to cart)
  - **Print order**
  - **Track shipment** (if tracking number added)
  - **Return** (if RMA enabled — Commerce only)
- Guest orders are **not visible** in order history (no account link)

- **Exam focus:** The **Reorder** function does NOT re-place the order — it simply populates the shopping cart with the previous order's items. Stock and price are re-evaluated at the time of reorder.

### 5.4 Downloadable Products

- After a downloadable product is **invoiced**, download links become available
- Located in: **My Account > My Downloadable Products**
- Downloads can be limited by:
  - Number of downloads allowed (Max Downloads; 0 = unlimited)
  - Order status / refund status (no time-based "expiry period" exists in Magento 2.4.8-p3)
- Link type: **File** (stored on server) or **URL** (external link)

- **Exam focus:** Download links are only activated **after the order is invoiced** — NOT just after order placement.

### 5.5 Wishlist

- Customers can save products for later
- Wishlist is **account-specific** — requires login
- Admin config: `Stores > Config > Customers > Wish List`
- Can **share wishlist** via email to others
- Items moved from wishlist to cart when "Add to Cart" clicked from wishlist

- **Exam focus:** Wishlist requires a **customer account** — guests cannot use the wishlist. This is a common reason stores may choose to encourage account creation.

### 5.6 Customer Groups

| Group | Default Use |
|---|---|
| NOT LOGGED IN | Guest / unauthenticated users |
| General | Default registered customers |
| Wholesale | Custom group (example) |
| Retailer | Custom group (example) |

- Groups affect: catalog price rules, cart price rules, tax classes, shipping restrictions

## 6. Guest Checkout vs Required Login

### 6.1 Configuration Options

**Location:** `Stores > Configuration > Sales > Checkout`

```
Checkout Options
+--------------------------------------------+
| Allow Guest Checkout:  [Yes / No]          |
| Enable Terms & Conditions: [Yes / No]      |
+--------------------------------------------+
```

**Location:** `Stores > Configuration > Customers > Customer Configuration > Create New Account Options`

```
Create New Account Options
+----------------------------------------------------+
| Allow Customers to Create Account: [Yes / No]     |
| Enable Automatic Assignment to Customer Group      |
| Default Group: [General]                           |
+----------------------------------------------------+
```

### 6.2 Comparison Table

| Feature | Guest Checkout | Required Login |
|---|---|---|
| Checkout speed | Faster (no registration) | Slightly slower |
| Order history visibility | No (email only) | Yes (My Account) |
| Wishlist access | No | Yes |
| Address book | No | Yes |
| Reorder capability | No | Yes |
| Abandoned cart recovery | Harder (no account) | Easier |
| Downloadable products | Via email link only | Via My Account |
| Conversion impact | Higher conversion typically | May reduce conversion |

- **Exam focus:** When **guest checkout is disabled**, customers are **forced to log in or create an account** before reaching the checkout. This setting is at `Sales > Checkout > Allow Guest Checkout`.
- **Exam focus:** A guest order can later be **associated with an account** if the customer registers with the same email address — Magento will link historical guest orders to the account.

### 6.3 Account Creation After Checkout

After a guest completes checkout, the order success page displays a **"Create an Account"** link. This is built into the checkout success page layout (`Magento\Checkout\Block\Registration`) and does not require a separate config toggle — it appears automatically when guest checkout is used and no account exists for that email.

## 7. Order Lifecycle & Statuses

### 7.1 Order States vs Order Statuses

Understanding the difference between **State** and **Status** is critical:

| Concept | Description |
|---|---|
| **State** | System-level code — fixed set, hard-coded in Magento |
| **Status** | Admin-customizable label that maps to a State |

- Multiple **statuses** can map to a single **state**
- Example: State `processing` could have statuses `Processing`, `Fraud Review`, `Awaiting Payment`
- Admin can create custom statuses at: `Stores > Order Status`

### 7.2 Core Order States

```
ORDER STATE FLOW
================
Note: `pending` is a STATUS (label), not a state. The state code is `new`.

                    [new]  (status: "Pending")
                      |
          +-----------+-----------+
          |                       |
    (awaiting payment)     (payment captured)
          |                       |
          v                       v
  [pending_payment]        [processing]
          |                       |
          |               +-------+-------+
          |               |               |
          v               v               v
      [canceled]    [complete]        [holded]
                          |
                     (credit memo)
                          |
                          v
                       [closed]
```

**Detailed State Descriptions:**

| State | Code | Description |
|---|---|---|
| **New** | `new` | Order placed, payment not yet captured (offline methods); default status label is "Pending" |
| **Pending Payment** | `pending_payment` | Waiting for payment gateway response |
| **Payment Review** | `payment_review` | Payment needs manual review (e.g., PayPal IPN) |
| **Processing** | `processing` | Payment captured (invoiced); awaiting shipment |
| **Complete** | `complete` | Fully invoiced AND fully shipped |
| **Closed** | `closed` | Credit memo has been created against this order |
| **Canceled** | `canceled` | Order was canceled — irreversible |
| **On Hold** | `holded` | Manually placed on hold by admin |

- **Exam focus:** **"Complete"** = the order has been **fully invoiced AND fully shipped**. Both actions must occur.
- **Exam focus:** **"Closed"** = a **credit memo has been created** on the order (refund issued). This is NOT the same as Complete.
- **Exam focus:** **"Canceled"** is **irreversible** — you **cannot un-cancel** an order. If an order is accidentally canceled, you must create a **new order**.
- **Exam focus:** **"On Hold"** is the only status that can be manually toggled. Use the **"Hold"** and **"Unhold"** buttons in Admin.

### 7.3 Visual State Machine

```
NEW ORDER PLACED
      |
      v
  [new] <------------- Offline payment methods
      |                (Check/Money Order)
      |                (default status label = "Pending")
      |
  INVOICE CREATED
      |
      v
  [processing] <------ Online payment captured
      |
      +---> [on_hold]  (admin manually holds)
      |          |
      |     [processing] (admin unholds)
      |
  SHIPMENT CREATED
  (all items shipped)
      |
      v
  [complete]
      |
  CREDIT MEMO CREATED
      |
      v
  [closed]

  OR at any eligible point:

  [canceled] <-------- Cannot return from here
```

### 7.4 State vs Status Mapping (Default)

| State | Default Status Label |
|---|---|
| `new` | Pending |
| `pending_payment` | Pending Payment |
| `payment_review` | Payment Review |
| `processing` | Processing |
| `complete` | Complete |
| `closed` | Closed |
| `canceled` | Canceled |
| `holded` | On Hold |

### 7.5 Cancellation Rules

An order **can be canceled** when:
- It is NOT in `complete`, `closed`, or `canceled` state
- It is NOT fully invoiced (not all items have been invoiced)
- Common cancelable states: `new`, `pending_payment`, and `processing` (if not fully invoiced)

An order **cannot be canceled** when:
- It has been **fully invoiced** (all items invoiced / payment captured)
- It is already in `complete`, `closed`, or `canceled` state
- To refund a processing/complete order: create a **Credit Memo** instead

```bash
# Magento CLI — example of checking order status
bin/magento info:adminuri
# Orders managed via Admin UI or API
```

## 8. Invoice: Payment Capture Record

### 8.1 What Is an Invoice?

An **Invoice** in Magento 2 is:
- A **financial document** confirming payment was received
- The action that moves an order from `pending` → `processing`
- Required before **downloadable links** are activated
- Note: shipments do NOT require an invoice first — they can be created independently (see Section 9)

> An Invoice is NOT a PDF bill sent to the customer (though a PDF can be generated). It is primarily a **payment capture event** in the system.

### 8.2 Invoice Creation

**In Admin:** `Sales > Orders > [Order] > Invoice`

```
Create Invoice
+----------------------------------------------+
| Items to Invoice                             |
| SKU001 - Product Name    Qty: [2]  of 2     |
| SKU002 - Product Name    Qty: [1]  of 1     |
+----------------------------------------------+
| Invoice Totals                               |
| Subtotal: $45.00                             |
| Shipping: $5.00                              |
| Tax:      $3.60                              |
| Grand Total: $53.60                          |
+----------------------------------------------+
| Payment Action:                              |
|  [o] Capture Online  (charges card now)     |
|  [o] Capture Offline (manual payment noted) |
|  [o] Not Capture                            |
+----------------------------------------------+
| [ ] Send Email Notification                  |
| [Submit Invoice]                             |
+----------------------------------------------+
```

### 8.3 Invoice Capture Modes

| Mode | Behavior |
|---|---|
| **Capture Online** | Sends capture request to payment gateway in real time |
| **Capture Offline** | Records payment as received without contacting gateway |
| **Not Capture** | Creates invoice record but marks payment as pending |

- **Exam focus:** **Capture Online** is only available when the payment method supports it (online methods like PayPal, Braintree). Offline methods (Check/Money Order) only support **Capture Offline**.
- **Exam focus:** Creating an invoice **triggers the invoice confirmation email** to the customer (if configured).
- **Exam focus:** You can create a **partial invoice** — invoice only some items from an order, leaving the rest uninvoiced.

### 8.4 Invoice Impact on Order State

```
Before Invoice:  State = [new]
                 Status = "Pending"

After Invoice:   State = [processing]
                 Status = "Processing"
                 Downloadable links = ACTIVE
```

## 9. Shipment: Physical Delivery Tracking

### 9.1 What Is a Shipment?

A **Shipment** in Magento 2:
- Tracks the **physical dispatch** of goods to the customer
- Records **carrier** and **tracking number**
- Triggers the **shipment confirmation email**
- When all items are shipped → order moves to `complete`

### 9.2 Shipment Creation

**In Admin:** `Sales > Orders > [Order] > Ship`

```
Create Shipment
+----------------------------------------------+
| Items to Ship                                |
| SKU001 - Product Name    Qty: [2]  of 2     |
| SKU002 - Product Name    Qty: [1]  of 1     |
+----------------------------------------------+
| Shipping Information                         |
|  Carrier: [Custom / UPS / FedEx / USPS]     |
|  Title:   [_________________]               |
|  Number:  [1Z999AA10123456784]              |
|           [+ Add Tracking Number]           |
+----------------------------------------------+
| [ ] Send Tracking Information Email          |
| [Submit Shipment]                            |
+----------------------------------------------+
```

### 9.3 Partial Shipments

- You can ship **some items** from an order and leave the rest
- Order stays in `processing` until **all items** are shipped and invoiced
- Each partial shipment generates its own shipment record with its own tracking

```
Order: 2 items
  |
  +-- Shipment #1: Item A (tracking: 1Z123...)
  |   Status: Processing (still has unshipped items)
  |
  +-- Shipment #2: Item B (tracking: 1Z456...)
      Status: Complete (all items now shipped)
```

- **Exam focus:** An order only reaches **"Complete"** state when it is **both fully invoiced AND fully shipped** — partial shipments alone do not complete the order.
- **Exam focus:** Shipments **can be created independently of invoices** — there is no code requiring an invoice before shipping. The `canShip()` method checks item quantities, hold status, and virtual status, but NOT invoice existence.

### 9.4 Tracking Information

- Tracking numbers appear in:
  - Admin Shipment detail page
  - Customer's **My Account > My Orders > View > Track Order**
  - Shipment confirmation email (clickable tracking link for major carriers)

## 10. Credit Memo: Refunds & Returns

### 10.1 What Is a Credit Memo?

A **Credit Memo** in Magento 2:
- Is the mechanism for issuing a **refund** to the customer
- Optionally returns items **back to stock**
- Changes the order state to **"Closed"**
- Can be partial (partial items/amounts) or full

### 10.2 Credit Memo Creation

**In Admin:** `Sales > Orders > [Order] > Credit Memo`

> **Prerequisite:** Order must be **invoiced** before a credit memo can be created.

```
Create Credit Memo
+----------------------------------------------+
| Items to Refund                              |
| SKU001 Qty to Refund: [2]  Return to Stock  |
| SKU002 Qty to Refund: [1]  Return to Stock  |
+----------------------------------------------+
| Refund Totals                                |
|  Subtotal:          $45.00                  |
|  Shipping Refund:   $5.00  [Adjust]         |
|  Adjustment Refund: $0.00  [+/-]            |
|  Adjustment Fee:    $0.00  [+/-]            |
|  Grand Total:       $53.60                  |
+----------------------------------------------+
| Payment Method:                              |
|  [o] Refund Online  (sends to gateway)      |
|  [o] Refund Offline (records only)          |
+----------------------------------------------+
| [ ] Send Email Notification                  |
| [Submit Credit Memo]                         |
+----------------------------------------------+
```

### 10.3 Credit Memo Options

| Field | Description |
|---|---|
| **Qty to Refund** | How many units to refund (can be less than ordered) |
| **Return to Stock** | Checkbox — adds qty back to inventory |
| **Adjustment Refund** | Additional amount to refund beyond item cost |
| **Adjustment Fee** | Amount to deduct from refund (restocking fee) |
| **Shipping Refund** | Amount of original shipping to refund |
| **Refund Online** | Sends refund request to payment gateway |
| **Refund Offline** | Records refund without contacting gateway |

- **Exam focus:** After creating a credit memo, the order state changes to **"Closed"** — this is permanent. You can add more credit memos but the state remains `closed`.
- **Exam focus:** **"Return to Stock"** must be manually checked — it is **not automatic**. If unchecked, inventory is NOT restored.
- **Exam focus:** **Adjustment Fee** is a **deduction** from the refund (like a restocking fee). **Adjustment Refund** is an **addition** to the refund amount.
- **Exam focus:** A credit memo requires the order to be **invoiced** — you cannot create a credit memo on an uninvoiced order.

### 10.4 Refund Flow

```
Order State: [processing] or [complete]
      |
      v
Admin creates Credit Memo
      |
      +---> Refund Online:  Gateway processes refund
      |     Refund Offline: Admin records manually
      |
      +---> Return to Stock: YES -> qty added back
      |     Return to Stock: NO  -> qty stays consumed
      |
      v
Order State: [closed]
Credit Memo PDF available in Admin + Customer email
```

## 11. Store Scope Hierarchy

### 11.1 The Four Scope Levels

```
SCOPE HIERARCHY (Broadest to Most Specific)
============================================

+-----------------------------------+
|         GLOBAL (Default)          |
|  Applies to all stores unless     |
|  overridden at lower level        |
+-----------------------------------+
              |
    +---------+---------+
    |                   |
+-------+           +-------+
|Website|           |Website|
|  (A)  |           |  (B)  |
+-------+           +-------+
    |
+---+---+
|       |
+-----+ +-----+
|Store| |Store|
| (1) | | (2) |
+-----+ +-----+
    |
+---+---+
|       |
+------+ +------+
| View | | View |
| (EN) | | (FR) |
+------+ +------+
```

### 11.2 Scope Level Definitions

| Scope Level | Also Called | Key Characteristics |
|---|---|---|
| **Global** | Default Config | Fallback for all settings; one per installation |
| **Website** | Website | Groups stores; shares customer accounts by default; separate base URLs possible |
| **Store** | Store (Root Category) | Each store has one root category; groups store views |
| **Store View** | Store View | Language/locale specific; where customers interact |

### 11.3 What Each Scope Controls

#### Global (Default) Scope
- Tax configuration (usually)
- Payment method availability defaults
- Shipping method defaults
- System-level settings (admin, cron, indexing)

#### Website Scope
- **Customer accounts** — customers belong to a website
- **Base currency** — each website can have different currency
- **Price scope** — can be set to Global or Website in catalog settings
- **Payment methods** — can be enabled/disabled per website
- **Shipping methods** — same

#### Store Scope
- **Root Category** — each store has exactly one root category tree
- **Default language** (though store views override this)

#### Store View Scope
- **Locale / Language** — `en_US`, `fr_FR`, etc.
- **Product names, descriptions** — translatable at store view level
- **CMS page content** — localized content
- **Timezone display**
- **Email logos** per store view

### 11.4 Configuration Scope in Admin

```
Stores > Configuration
+------------------------------------------+
| Scope Selector (top left dropdown):      |
|  [Default Config]     <- Global          |
|  Main Website                            |
|    Main Website Store                    |
|      Default Store View                  |
|      French Store View                   |
+------------------------------------------+
```

When a setting has a **"Use Default"** checkbox:
- Checked = inherits from the scope above
- Unchecked = override at this scope level

- **Exam focus:** **Catalog Price Scope** (`Stores > Config > Catalog > Catalog > Price`) can be set to **Global** or **Website** — determines if a product can have different prices per website.
- **Exam focus:** **Customer accounts are scoped to Website** — a customer who registers on Website A cannot log in to Website B (unless account sharing is configured).
- **Exam focus:** **Product attributes** can have scope: **Global**, **Website**, or **Store View**. For example, `name` and `description` are typically Store View scope (translatable), while `price` is Website or Global scope.

### 11.5 Attribute Scope vs Configuration Scope

| Concept | Scope Options | Example |
|---|---|---|
| Product Attribute Values | Global / Website / Store View | `description` = Store View (translatable) |
| System Configuration | Global / Website / Store / Store View | Payment methods = Website |
| Customer Accounts | Website-scoped | Login valid for one website |
| Price Rules | Website-scoped | Cart rules apply per website |

## 12. Hands-On Admin Walkthrough

### 12.1 Complete Order Lifecycle in Admin

Follow this sequence to walk through a full order lifecycle:

#### Step 1: Find or Place an Order

```
Admin > Sales > Orders
  - Find an existing order in "Pending" or "Processing" state
  - OR: Place a new order via Admin > Sales > Orders > Create New Order
```

**Create Order via Admin:**
```
Sales > Orders > [+ Create New Order]
  1. Select Customer (or Create Guest)
  2. Select Store
  3. Add Products (by SKU or search)
  4. Set Qty
  5. Apply Coupon (optional)
  6. Enter Billing Address
  7. Enter Shipping Address
  8. Select Shipping Method
  9. Select Payment Method (offline recommended for test)
  10. Submit Order
```

#### Step 2: View the New Order

```
Sales > Orders > [Order #]
  Observe:
  - Status: "Pending" (if offline payment)
  - State: new/pending
  - No Invoice tab visible yet for offline payments
  - Buttons: Cancel, Hold, Send Email, Invoice
```

#### Step 3: Create an Invoice

```
Sales > Orders > [Order #] > [Invoice] button
  1. Review items and quantities
  2. Select "Capture Offline" (for Check/Money Order)
  3. Check "Send Email Notification"
  4. Click [Submit Invoice]

  Observe after:
  - Order Status: "Processing"
  - Invoice tab now shows Invoice #
  - "Ship" button now available
```

#### Step 4: Create a Shipment

```
Sales > Orders > [Order #] > [Ship] button
  1. Confirm quantities to ship
  2. Add Carrier: Custom
  3. Add Tracking Number: TEST123456
  4. Check "Send Tracking Information"
  5. Click [Submit Shipment]

  Observe after:
  - Shipment tab shows Shipment # and tracking
  - If all items shipped: Order Status = "Complete"
  - Customer can now see tracking in My Account
```

#### Step 5: Create a Credit Memo (Refund)

```
Sales > Orders > [Order #] > [Credit Memo] button
  (Only available if order is invoiced)
  1. Set qty to refund for each item
  2. Check "Return to Stock" (important!)
  3. Optionally adjust shipping refund amount
  4. Select "Refund Offline"
  5. Check "Send Email Notification"
  6. Click [Submit Credit Memo]

  Observe after:
  - Order Status: "Closed"
  - Credit Memos tab shows Credit Memo #
  - Inventory restored (if Return to Stock checked)
```

## Quick-Reference Checklist

### Customer Journey
- [ ] Journey sequence: Browse → Search → PDP → Add to Cart → Cart → Checkout (Shipping + Payment) → Order Placed → Confirmation Email
- [ ] Magento 2 checkout = **two steps** (Shipping + Review & Payment), not six steps
- [ ] Cart = **Quote object** in database; becomes Order after successful checkout
- [ ] Guest email at checkout used for order confirmation and account existence check

### Product Types
- [ ] Virtual products = no shipping step in checkout
- [ ] Downloadable products = no shipping; links activate after **invoice**
- [ ] Configurable = must select all attribute options before adding to cart

### Customer Account
- [ ] One **default billing** + one **default shipping** address; unlimited stored addresses
- [ ] **Reorder** = adds items to cart only; does NOT re-place the order
- [ ] Wishlist requires **customer account** (login required; guests cannot use wishlist)
- [ ] Download links activate **after invoice**, NOT after order placement
- [ ] Guest orders linked to account if customer registers with same email

### Guest vs. Required Login
- [ ] Config: `Stores > Config > Sales > Checkout > Allow Guest Checkout`
- [ ] Separate email templates for logged-in customers vs. guests
- [ ] Guest orders NOT visible in order history

### Order States (CRITICAL)
- [ ] **Complete** = fully invoiced **AND** fully shipped (both required)
- [ ] **Closed** = credit memo created (refund issued)
- [ ] **Canceled** = **irreversible** — cannot un-cancel; must create new order
- [ ] **On Hold** = only manually toggled state; use Hold/Unhold buttons
- [ ] **Processing** = payment captured (invoiced); not yet fully shipped
- [ ] **New** (status "Pending") = order placed with offline payment; not yet invoiced — state code is `new`, NOT `pending`

### Invoice
- [ ] Invoice = **payment capture record** (not just a PDF)
- [ ] Creates invoice → order moves `new` → `processing`
- [ ] **Capture Online** = real-time gateway request
- [ ] **Capture Offline** = manual record (no gateway call)
- [ ] Partial invoices are possible
- [ ] Downloadable links activate upon invoicing
- [ ] Shipments can be created independently — NO invoice prerequisite

### Shipment
- [ ] Shipments do NOT require a prior invoice — can be created independently
- [ ] Partial shipments allowed; order stays `processing` until **all** items shipped
- [ ] Order reaches **Complete** only when fully invoiced AND fully shipped
- [ ] Tracking number visible in customer My Account and confirmation email

### Credit Memo
- [ ] Requires order to be **invoiced** before creation
- [ ] Changes order state to **Closed** (permanent)
- [ ] **Return to Stock** is manual (checkbox) — not automatic
- [ ] **Adjustment Fee** = deducted from refund (restocking fee)
- [ ] **Adjustment Refund** = added to refund amount
- [ ] **Refund Online** = gateway; **Refund Offline** = record only

### Store Scope Hierarchy
- [ ] 4 levels: **Global → Website → Store → Store View**
- [ ] Global = installation-wide default/fallback
- [ ] Website = customer accounts scope; base currency; payment/shipping methods
- [ ] Store = root category assignment
- [ ] Store View = locale/language; product name/description translations; CMS content
- [ ] **Catalog Price Scope**: Global or Website (set in Catalog config)
- [ ] **Customer accounts are Website-scoped** by default (cannot log in across websites)
- [ ] Product attribute values can be scoped: Global / Website / Store View
- [ ] "Use Default" checkbox = inherit from parent scope

### Tricky Distinctions (High Exam Value)
- [ ] **Complete ≠ Closed**: Complete = shipped+invoiced; Closed = refunded
- [ ] **Closed ≠ Canceled**: Closed = had credit memo; Canceled = voided before processing
- [ ] **Cancel vs Credit Memo**: Cancel if not fully invoiced (any state except complete/closed/canceled); Credit Memo if invoiced
- [ ] **Invoice ≠ PDF receipt**: It's a system payment capture event
- [ ] **Shipment ≠ Complete**: Partial shipment does not complete an order
- [ ] **Hold ≠ Cancel**: Hold is reversible; Cancel is not

flashcards.question: What is a Quote in Magento 2 and when does it become an Order?
flashcards.answer: The shopping cart is technically a Quote object in the database. It only becomes an Order after the customer successfully completes checkout and clicks Place Order. At that point, the Quote is converted to a sales_order record and marked inactive.
flashcards.hint: The database entity behind the cart has a different name than what customers see.

flashcards.question: What two conditions must both be met for an order to reach the 'Complete' state?
flashcards.answer: The order must be fully invoiced AND fully shipped. Both actions are required — a partial shipment or partial invoice alone will not move the order to Complete. It remains in Processing until both are fully done.
flashcards.hint: Payment captured plus goods dispatched — both must cover all items.

flashcards.question: What is the difference between the 'Closed' and 'Canceled' order states?
flashcards.answer: Closed means a credit memo (refund) was issued against the order. Canceled means the order was voided before fulfillment. Canceled is irreversible — you cannot un-cancel an order. To handle a completed order, you must use a Credit Memo, not cancellation.
flashcards.hint: One involves money going back; the other means the order never proceeded.

flashcards.question: Can a shipment be created before an invoice in Magento 2?
flashcards.answer: Yes. Shipments can be created independently of invoices — there is no code requiring an invoice before shipping. The canShip() method checks item quantities, hold status, and virtual status, but NOT invoice existence.
flashcards.hint: Invoicing and shipping are parallel workflows, not sequential dependencies.

flashcards.question: What prerequisite must exist before a Credit Memo can be created?
flashcards.answer: The order must be invoiced (payment captured) before a credit memo can be created. You cannot create a credit memo on an uninvoiced order because canCreditmemo() checks getTotalPaid(). The credit memo changes the order state to Closed.
flashcards.hint: You cannot refund money that was never captured.

flashcards.question: What is the difference between Order State and Order Status in Magento 2?
flashcards.answer: State is a system-level, hard-coded code that drives business logic (e.g., 'new', 'processing', 'complete'). Status is an admin-customizable display label mapped to a State. Multiple statuses can map to one state. You can create new statuses but cannot create new states.
flashcards.hint: One is fixed in code; the other is a configurable label.

flashcards.question: What does the 'Return to Stock' checkbox do on a Credit Memo, and is it automatic?
flashcards.answer: The 'Return to Stock' checkbox adds refunded item quantities back to inventory. It is NOT automatic — it must be manually checked by the admin. If left unchecked, the inventory quantity is not restored even though the refund is processed.
flashcards.hint: Refunding money and restoring stock are two separate actions.

flashcards.question: At which scope level are customer accounts managed in Magento 2?
flashcards.answer: Customer accounts are scoped to the Website level. A customer who registers on Website A cannot log in to Website B unless account sharing is specifically configured. This also means base currency and pricing are Website-scoped.
flashcards.hint: The second level in the Global > Website > Store > Store View hierarchy.

flashcards.question: What happens when a guest completes checkout and later registers with the same email?
flashcards.answer: Magento will link the historical guest orders to the newly created account. The guest order can be associated with the account, making it visible in the customer's My Account > My Orders section.
flashcards.hint: Email address is the linking key between guest orders and accounts.

flashcards.question: What does the Reorder function do in Magento 2?
flashcards.answer: The Reorder function adds the same items from a previous order back to the shopping cart. It does NOT re-place the order. Stock availability and current prices are re-evaluated at the time of reorder, so quantities or prices may differ from the original.
flashcards.hint: It is a cart population shortcut, not an order duplication.

flashcards.question: When do downloadable product links become available to the customer?
flashcards.answer: Download links are activated after the order is invoiced (payment captured), not just after order placement. They appear in My Account > My Downloadable Products. The order must reach the configured status (default: Invoiced) for links to become accessible.
flashcards.hint: Payment must be confirmed before digital goods are delivered.

flashcards.question: How many checkout steps does Magento 2 use, and what are they?
flashcards.answer: Magento 2 uses a two-step One-Page Checkout: Step 1 is Shipping (address and method selection), and Step 2 is Review & Payment (payment method and order placement). This replaced the six-step process from Magento 1.
flashcards.hint: It looks like one page but has two distinct stages.

flashcards.question: What are the three Invoice capture modes and when is each available?
flashcards.answer: Capture Online sends a real-time capture request to the payment gateway (only for online methods). Capture Offline records payment without contacting the gateway (for offline methods like Check/Money Order). Not Capture creates an invoice record but marks payment as pending.
flashcards.hint: Online methods talk to the gateway; offline methods just record locally.

flashcards.question: What is the difference between Adjustment Fee and Adjustment Refund on a Credit Memo?
flashcards.answer: Adjustment Fee is a deduction from the refund amount (like a restocking fee — reduces what the customer gets back). Adjustment Refund is an addition to the refund amount (increases what the customer gets back beyond the item cost).
flashcards.hint: Fee takes away from the refund; Refund adds to it.
