  - [1.1 How Layered Navigation Works](#11-how-layered-navigation-works)
  - [1.2 Anchor vs Non-Anchor Categories](#12-anchor-vs-non-anchor-categories)
  - [1.3 Attribute Configuration for Layered Navigation](#13-attribute-configuration-for-layered-navigation)
  - [1.4 Price Ranges: Automatic vs Manual Steps](#14-price-ranges-automatic-vs-manual-steps)
- [2. Search Configuration](#2-search-configuration)
  - [2.1 Catalog Search Engine](#21-catalog-search-engine)
  - [2.2 Search Suggestions & Autocomplete](#22-search-suggestions--autocomplete)
  - [2.3 Popular Search Terms](#23-popular-search-terms)
  - [2.4 Search Term Synonyms](#24-search-term-synonyms)
  - [2.5 Search Results & Layered Navigation](#25-search-results--layered-navigation)
- [3. Customer Management](#3-customer-management)
  - [3.1 Customer Groups](#31-customer-groups)
  - [3.2 Customer Accounts & Address Book](#32-customer-accounts--address-book)
  - [3.3 Customer Grid: Filtering & Segmentation](#33-customer-grid-filtering--segmentation)
- [4. Wishlist](#4-wishlist)
  - [4.1 Single Wishlist (CE)](#41-single-wishlist-ce)
  - [4.2 Multiple Wishlists (EE)](#42-multiple-wishlists-ee)
- [5. Newsletter Subscription Management](#5-newsletter-subscription-management)
- [6. Hands-On: Adding a Filterable Attribute](#6-hands-on-adding-a-filterable-attribute)
- [7. Tricky Exam Concepts Summary](#7-tricky-exam-concepts-summary)
- [Quick-Reference Checklist](#quick-reference-checklist)

---

## 1. Layered Navigation

### 1.1 How Layered Navigation Works

Layered navigation (also called **faceted navigation**) allows shoppers to progressively narrow down product listings using filters. It appears as a sidebar panel on:

- **Category pages** (only on **anchor** categories — see below)
- **Search results pages**

Each active filter adds a constraint to the product query, and multiple filters can be applied simultaneously.

```
Storefront Category Page (Anchor)
+-----------------------------+----------------------------------+
|  Layered Navigation Panel   |  Product Grid                    |
|-----------------------------|----------------------------------|
|  Shopping Options           |  [Product] [Product] [Product]  |
|                             |                                  |
|  Price                      |  [Product] [Product] [Product]  |
|    $0.00 - $99.99  (12)     |                                  |
|    $100.00 - $199.99 (8)    |  [Product] [Product] [Product]  |
|    $200.00 and above (4)    |                                  |
|                             |                                  |
|  Color                      |                                  |
|    Red    (5)               |                                  |
|    Blue   (7)               |                                  |
|    Green  (3)               |                                  |
|                             |                                  |
|  Size                       |                                  |
|    S (4) M (8) L (6)        |                                  |
+-----------------------------+----------------------------------+
```

**Exam focus:**
- Layered navigation appears **only on anchor categories** and **search results pages**
- Non-anchor categories do **not** display the layered navigation sidebar
- The filter panel is powered by the search index (OpenSearch/Elasticsearch), not SQL queries

---

### 1.2 Anchor vs Non-Anchor Categories

This is one of the most commonly tested concepts in the exam.

| Property | Anchor Category | Non-Anchor Category |
|---|---|---|
| Shows layered nav filters | **Yes** | **No** |
| Shows products from subcategories | **Yes** (recursively) | No (own products only) |
| Typical use | Broad parent categories | Leaf/specific categories |
| Setting location | Catalog > Categories > Display Settings | Same |

**How to set a category as Anchor:**

```
Admin > Catalog > Categories
  > [Select Category]
    > Display Settings tab
      > Is Anchor = Yes
```

**Exam focus:**
- Setting **Is Anchor = Yes** on a category enables layered navigation **and** causes it to display products from all child/subcategories
- A common mistake is enabling filterable attributes but forgetting to set the category as an anchor — filters will not appear

---

### 1.3 Attribute Configuration for Layered Navigation

To appear in layered navigation, a product attribute must be configured correctly.

**Path:** `Admin > Stores > Attributes > Product > [Select Attribute] > Storefront Properties`

| Setting | Options | Behavior |
|---|---|---|
| Use in Layered Navigation | No | Never appears in layered nav |
| Use in Layered Navigation | Filterable (with results) | Only shows filter option if ≥1 product matches |
| Use in Layered Navigation | Filterable (no results) | Shows filter option even if 0 products match |
| Use in Search Results Layered Navigation | Yes / No | Controls appearance on search results page |
| Use in Search | Yes / No | Makes attribute values searchable via full-text |

**Attribute requirements for layered navigation:**
- Input type must be **Dropdown**, **Multiple Select**, **Price**, or **Yes/No**
- Text fields (e.g., Text Field, Text Area) **cannot** be used in layered navigation
- Attribute scope must allow indexing

```
Attribute Storefront Properties
+------------------------------------------+
| Use in Layered Navigation:               |
|   [Filterable (with results)         v]  |
|                                          |
| Use in Search Results Layered Nav:       |
|   [Yes                               v]  |
|                                          |
| Use in Search: [Yes v]                   |
| Comparable on Storefront: [Yes v]        |
| Visible on Catalog Pages: [Yes v]        |
+------------------------------------------+
```

**Exam focus:**
- **Filterable (with results)** = most common, hides filter if no products qualify — better UX
- **Filterable (no results)** = always shows filter — useful for consistency but can confuse shoppers
- After changing attribute settings, you must **reindex** (`bin/magento indexer:reindex`) for changes to appear on the frontend

---

### 1.4 Price Ranges: Automatic vs Manual Steps

Price is a special layered navigation filter with two configuration modes.

**Path:** `Admin > Stores > Configuration > Catalog > Catalog > Layered Navigation`

#### Automatic (Equalize Product Counts)

Magento automatically calculates price bucket ranges so that each bucket contains roughly the same number of products.

- No manual input needed
- Range sizes vary based on product distribution
- Best for stores with uneven price distributions

#### Automatic (Equalize Price Ranges)

Magento creates equal-width price buckets across the entire price spectrum.

- Range sizes are equal (e.g., $0–$50, $50–$100, $100–$150)
- Bucket counts may be unequal
- Best for stores with predictable pricing

#### Manual

Admin defines fixed step sizes.

```
Path: Stores > Configuration > Catalog > Catalog > Layered Navigation
  Price Navigation Step Calculation: Manual
  Default Price Navigation Step: 100
```

This creates ranges like: `$0-$100`, `$100-$200`, `$200-$300`, etc.

```
Comparison of Price Range Modes
+---------------------------------+--------------------+-----------------------+
| Mode                            | Range Width        | Product Count/Bucket  |
|---------------------------------|--------------------|------------------------|
| Automatic (Equalize Prod Counts)| Varies             | Roughly equal         |
| Automatic (Equalize Price Range)| Equal              | Varies                |
| Manual                          | Fixed (admin-set)  | Varies                |
+---------------------------------+--------------------+-----------------------+
```

**Exam focus:**
- **Manual** mode requires setting a specific step value (e.g., 100 = $100 increments)
- Automatic modes do **not** require a step value
- Price ranges are always displayed as currency ranges in the layered navigation sidebar

---

## 2. Search Configuration

### 2.1 Catalog Search Engine

Magento 2.4+ requires an external full-text search engine. MySQL search was removed.

**Path:** `Admin > Stores > Configuration > Catalog > Catalog > Catalog Search`

| Engine | Version Support | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| **OpenSearch** | Magento 2.4.6+ (preferred) | Open-source fork of Elasticsearch |
| **Elasticsearch 7** | Magento 2.4.x | Still supported but being phased out |
| ~~MySQL~~ | ~~Magento 2.3 and below~~ | Removed in 2.4 |

**Configuration fields:**

```
Catalog Search Configuration
+------------------------------------------------+
| Search Engine: [OpenSearch               v]    |
| OpenSearch Server Hostname: [localhost      ]  |
| OpenSearch Server Port:     [9200           ]  |
| OpenSearch Index Prefix:    [magento2        ]  |
| Enable OpenSearch HTTP Auth: [No          v]   |
| Minimum Terms to Match:     [1              ]  |
+------------------------------------------------+
```

**Exam focus:**
- As of Magento **2.4.6**, OpenSearch is the **recommended** search engine
- Elasticsearch support is maintained but deprecated in newer versions
- The **index prefix** allows multiple Magento instances to share one search cluster
- After changing the search engine, run: `bin/magento indexer:reindex catalogsearch_fulltext`

---

### 2.2 Search Suggestions & Autocomplete

**Path:** `Stores > Configuration > Catalog > Catalog > Catalog Search`

| Setting | Description |
|---|---|
| Autocomplete Limit | Number of autocomplete suggestions shown in the search dropdown |
| Search Suggestions Enabled | Shows "Did you mean...?" suggestions for misspelled queries |
| Search Suggestions Count | Max number of "did you mean" suggestions |
| Show Results Count for Suggestions | Displays product count next to each suggestion |
| Search Recommendations Enabled | Shows popular/related search terms below the search box |
| Search Recommendations Count | Max number of recommendations |

```
Storefront Search Dropdown Example
+-----------------------------------------------+
| [ search query: "blak shoes"                ] |
|-----------------------------------------------|
| Did you mean:                                 |
|   black shoes (24 results)                    |
|   black boots (12 results)                    |
|-----------------------------------------------|
| Suggestions:                                  |
|   Black Running Shoes                         |
|   Black Leather Shoes                         |
+-----------------------------------------------+
```

**Exam focus:**
- **Search Suggestions** = "did you mean" (corrects misspellings)
- **Search Recommendations** = related/popular terms (not spelling corrections)
- These are distinct features with separate enable/count controls

---

### 2.3 Popular Search Terms

Popular search terms are collected from actual customer searches and can be displayed as a tag cloud.

**Path (Admin):** `Marketing > SEO & Search > Search Terms`

**Path (Config):** `Stores > Configuration > Catalog > Catalog > Catalog Search > Popular Search Terms`

- When **enabled**, popular terms appear as a **tag cloud** in the storefront footer (or as a widget)
- Terms with more searches appear **larger** in the cloud
- Admin can manually **add, edit, or redirect** search terms
- A search term can be configured with a **redirect URL** — searching for that term sends the user to a specific page

```
Popular Search Terms Tag Cloud (Storefront)
+------------------------------------------+
|  shoes   BOOTS   jacket   t-shirt        |
|     DENIM    accessories   SALE          |
|  bags   WATCHES   sunglasses             |
+------------------------------------------+
(Larger font = more searches)
```

**Exam focus:**
- Popular search terms can be **redirected** to any URL (useful for promotions)
- The tag cloud is a storefront feature; disabling it does not delete the terms
- Search terms are **store-view specific**

---

### 2.4 Search Term Synonyms

Synonyms allow you to group alternative terms so they return the same search results, improving search relevance without changing product data.

**Path:** `Admin > Marketing > SEO & Search > Search Synonyms`

**Synonym groups (two-way only):**

Magento supports **two-way (grouped) synonyms only**. All terms in a group are treated as equivalent — searching for any one of them returns results matching any of the others.

| Type | Example | Behavior |
|---|---|---|
| Two-way (grouped) | "coat, jacket, blazer" | All three terms return the same results |

> **Note:** Magento does **not** support one-way synonyms in the admin. The `SynonymGroupInterface` only stores a comma-separated group of equivalent terms — there is no directional mapping. If you need one-way behavior, it must be configured directly in OpenSearch/Elasticsearch.

```bash
# Two-way synonym example
# Synonyms group: "tv, television, telly"
# Searching any of the three returns products matching all three terms
```

**Creating a synonym group:**
```
Admin > Marketing > SEO & Search > Search Synonyms
  > Add Synonym Group button
    > Synonyms field: "tv, television, telly"
    > Scope: [Store View]
    > Save
```

**Exam focus:**
- Synonyms are configured at **store-view level**, not global
- Path: **Marketing > SEO & Search > Search Synonyms** (not under Catalog)
- Synonyms are processed by the search engine (OpenSearch/Elasticsearch) — they require the search index to be rebuilt after changes

---

### 2.5 Search Results & Layered Navigation

Search results pages also support layered navigation — the same filterable attributes configured for category pages appear here, controlled by the **"Use in Search Results Layered Navigation"** attribute setting.

```
Search Results Page for "jacket"
+-----------------------------+----------------------------------+
|  Filter By                  |  Search Results: "jacket"        |
|-----------------------------|----------------------------------|
|  Price                      |  [Jacket 1]  [Jacket 2]          |
|    $50-$100 (6)             |  [Jacket 3]  [Jacket 4]          |
|    $100-$200 (4)            |                                  |
|  Color                      |  Showing 10 of 24 results        |
|    Black (8) Blue (2)       |                                  |
|  Material                   |                                  |
|    Leather (3) Wool (7)     |                                  |
+-----------------------------+----------------------------------+
```

---

## 3. Customer Management

### 3.1 Customer Groups

Customer groups are fundamental to Magento's pricing, tax, and access control system.

**Path:** `Admin > Customers > Customer Groups`

#### Default Customer Groups

| Group ID | Group Name | Description |
|---|---|---|
| **0** | **NOT LOGGED IN** | Guest visitors — not authenticated |
| **1** | General | Default for new registered customers |
| **2** | Wholesale | Pre-configured group for wholesale buyers |
| **3** | Retailer | Pre-configured group for retail businesses |

> **Critical:** Group **0 — "NOT LOGGED IN"** is a real customer group. It applies to all **guest/unauthenticated** visitors and is used for:
> - Guest pricing rules
> - Tax class assignments for guests
> - Cart price rules targeting guests

```
Customer Group Impacts
+--------------------+-------------------------------+
| Customer Group     | Affects                       |
|--------------------|-------------------------------|
| NOT LOGGED IN (0)  | Guest pricing, guest tax      |
| General (1)        | Default registered customer   |
| Wholesale (2)      | Wholesale-specific pricing    |
| Retailer (3)       | Retailer-specific pricing     |
| [Custom Groups]    | Any custom pricing/rules      |
+--------------------+-------------------------------+
```

**Where customer groups are used:**
- **Tier Pricing / Group Pricing** — different prices per group
- **Cart Price Rules** — target specific groups
- **Catalog Price Rules** — apply discounts per group
- **Tax Rules** — different tax rates per group
- **Shipping Rules** — free shipping thresholds per group
- **Customer Segments (EE only)** — more granular segmentation

**Exam focus:**
- **"NOT LOGGED IN" is Group 0** — it is a customer group, not an absence of a group
- You cannot delete the four default groups
- A customer can belong to **only one group** at a time
- Changing a customer's group immediately affects their pricing and tax treatment

---

### 3.2 Customer Accounts & Address Book

**Customer Account features (storefront):**

| Feature | Description |
|---|---|
| My Account Dashboard | Overview of recent orders, account info |
| Address Book | Save multiple billing/shipping addresses |
| Order History | View, reorder, create returns |
| Account Information | Update name, email, password |
| Newsletter Subscriptions | Manage subscriptions |
| Wishlist | Save products for later |
| Store Credit (EE) | View and apply store credit |
| Reward Points (EE) | View reward point balance |

**Address Book:**
- Customers can save multiple addresses
- One address is set as the **default billing** address
- One address is set as the **default shipping** address
- During checkout, saved addresses appear in a dropdown

**Admin customer management path:** `Admin > Customers > All Customers`

```
Customer Edit Page (Admin)
+----------------------------------------------------+
| Customer Information                               |
|   Account Information tab                         |
|   Addresses tab                                   |
|   Orders tab                                      |
|   Shopping cart tab                               |
|   Wishlist tab                                    |
|   Newsletter tab                                  |
|   Product Reviews tab                             |
|   Billing Agreements tab                          |
|   Store Credit tab (EE)                           |
|   Reward Points tab (EE)                          |
+----------------------------------------------------+
```

**Exam focus:**
- The **Address Book** can store unlimited addresses (no built-in cap)
- Default billing and default shipping addresses are separate designations
- Admins can **create orders on behalf of customers** from the customer edit page (Create Order button)

---

### 3.3 Customer Grid: Filtering & Segmentation

**Path:** `Admin > Customers > All Customers`

The customer grid supports:
- **Column filtering** — filter by email, name, group, website, etc.
- **Full-text search** within the grid
- **Export** to CSV or XML
- **Bulk actions** — Subscribe to newsletter, Unsubscribe from newsletter, Assign customer group, Delete

#### Customer Segments (EE Only)

Customer Segments allow much more granular targeting than customer groups.

**Path:** `Admin > Customers > Segments`

| Feature | Customer Groups (CE+EE) | Customer Segments (EE only) |
|---|---|---|
| Assignment | Manual, rule-based at account creation | Dynamic, real-time rule evaluation |
| Criteria | Single group assignment | Complex rules (order history, cart contents, demographics) |
| Use in promotions | Yes | Yes (more granular) |
| Real-time evaluation | No | Yes |

**Segment rule examples (EE):**
- "Customers who have purchased more than $500 in the last 30 days"
- "Customers with items from category X in cart"
- "Customers in ZIP code 10001"

**Exam focus:**
- Customer Segments are **EE only** — do not confuse with Customer Groups
- Segments are evaluated **dynamically/in real-time**; groups require manual assignment
- Both can be used in cart price rules and catalog price rules

---

## 4. Wishlist

### 4.1 Single Wishlist (CE)

**Path:** `Admin > Stores > Configuration > Customers > Wish List`

| Setting | Description |
|---|---|
| Enabled | Enables/disables wishlist feature |
| Share Wishlist Email Sender | Sender identity for wishlist share emails |
| Share Wishlist Email Template | Email template used |
| Max Emails Allowed to be Sent | Limit per share action |
| Email Text Length Limit | Max characters in share message |
| Display Wish List Summary | Show count on storefront |

**CE wishlist behavior:**
- Each customer has **exactly one** wishlist
- Products can be moved from wishlist to cart
- Wishlists can be **shared** via email (generates a public URL)
- Quantity can be set per wishlist item
- Items stay in the wishlist after being added to cart (must be manually removed)

```
Wishlist Flow (CE)
+------------+     Add to     +------------+     Move to    +---------+
|  Product   |  ---------->  |  Wishlist  |  ----------->  |  Cart   |
|   Page     |   Wishlist    | (single)   |                |         |
+------------+               +------------+                +---------+
                                  |
                             Share via email
                                  |
                             +----------+
                             | Shareable|
                             |   URL    |
                             +----------+
```

**Exam focus:**
- CE = **one wishlist per customer**
- Wishlist sharing creates a **public URL** — anyone with the link can view it (but not edit)
- Wishlist is **not available** to guests (requires login)

---

### 4.2 Multiple Wishlists (EE)

**Path:** `Admin > Stores > Configuration > Customers > Wish List > General Options > Enable Multiple Wish Lists`

**EE wishlist enhancements:**
- Customers can create **multiple named wishlists** (e.g., "Birthday Ideas", "Work Equipment", "Home Office")
- Each wishlist can be shared independently
- Products can be moved or copied between wishlists
- All wishlists can be managed from the customer's account dashboard

```
Multiple Wishlist Example (EE)
+------------------+
|  My Wishlists    |
|------------------|
|  Birthday Ideas  |  (5 items)
|  Work Equipment  |  (3 items)
|  Home Office     |  (8 items)
|  [+ Create New]  |
+------------------+
```

**Exam focus:**
- Multiple wishlists = **EE only** feature
- CE customers have exactly **1** wishlist; EE customers can have **many**
- The feature must be explicitly enabled in configuration (not on by default even in EE)

---

## 5. Newsletter Subscription Management

**Path (Config):** `Admin > Stores > Configuration > Customers > Newsletter`

**Path (Subscribers):** `Admin > Marketing > Communications > Newsletter Subscribers`

### Subscription Settings

| Setting | Description |
|---|---|
| Allow Guest Subscription | Guests can subscribe without an account |
| Need to Confirm | Requires email confirmation (double opt-in) |
| Confirmation Email Sender | Sender identity for confirmation emails |
| Confirmation Email Template | Template for double opt-in email |
| Success Email Sender | Sender for successful subscription confirmation |
| Success Email Template | Template for subscription success |
| Unsubscription Email Sender | Sender for unsubscribe confirmation |
| Unsubscription Email Template | Template for unsubscribe email |

### Newsletter Subscriber Grid

```
Admin > Marketing > Communications > Newsletter Subscribers
+--------------------------------------------------+
| Filter by: Status | Customer | Email | Website   |
|--------------------------------------------------|
| Email              | Status      | Subscribed On |
| john@example.com   | Subscribed  | Jan 1, 2024   |
| jane@example.com   | Unsubscribed| Feb 5, 2024   |
| guest@example.com  | Subscribed  | Mar 10, 2024  |
+--------------------------------------------------+
| Bulk Actions: Unsubscribe | Delete | Export      |
+--------------------------------------------------+
```

**Subscription statuses:**

| Status | Meaning |
|---|---|
| Subscribed | Active subscriber |
| Unsubscribed | Previously subscribed, opted out |
| Not Activated | Signed up but has not confirmed (double opt-in pending) |
| Unconfirmed | Customer account itself requires confirmation — newsletter subscription waits until account is confirmed (distinct from "Not Activated", which is for newsletter double opt-in) |

**Exam focus:**
- **Double opt-in** = "Need to Confirm" setting — sends a confirmation email before activating subscription
- Guests **can** subscribe if "Allow Guest Subscription" is enabled
- Newsletter subscriptions are **store-view specific**
- Admin can **manually subscribe or unsubscribe** customers from the customer edit page

---

## 6. Hands-On: Adding a Filterable Attribute

This walkthrough covers the complete process of making a product attribute appear in layered navigation.

### Step 1: Create or Edit the Attribute

```
Admin > Stores > Attributes > Product
  > Add New Attribute (or select existing)
```

**Required attribute settings for layered navigation:**

```
Properties Tab:
+------------------------------------------+
| Default Label:    [Color               ] |
| Catalog Input Type: [Dropdown         v] |
| Values Required:    [No               v] |
+------------------------------------------+
```

> Note: Input type **must be** Dropdown, Multiple Select, Yes/No, or Price.

### Step 2: Configure Storefront Properties

```
Storefront Properties Tab:
+--------------------------------------------------+
| Use in Search:                      [Yes      v] |
| Use in Layered Navigation:                       |
|   [Filterable (with results)               v]    |
| Use in Search Results Layered Navigation:        |
|   [Yes                                     v]    |
| Position:                           [0        ]  |
| Use for Promo Rule Conditions:      [Yes      v] |
| Allow HTML Tags on Storefront:      [No       v] |
| Visible on Catalog Pages:           [Yes      v] |
| Used in Product Listing:            [Yes      v] |
| Used for Sorting in Product Listing:[No       v] |
+--------------------------------------------------+
```

### Step 3: Add Attribute to Attribute Set

```
Admin > Stores > Attributes > Attribute Sets
  > [Select your attribute set, e.g., "Default"]
  > Drag attribute from "Unassigned Attributes" 
    to the appropriate group
  > Save
```

### Step 4: Assign Values to Products

Edit products and assign values for the attribute (e.g., Color = Red, Blue, Green).

### Step 5: Ensure Category is Anchor

```
Admin > Catalog > Categories
  > [Select your test category]
    > Display Settings tab
      > Is Anchor: [Yes v]
  > Save
```

### Step 6: Reindex

```bash
# Reindex all indexes
bin/magento indexer:reindex

# Or reindex specific indexes
bin/magento indexer:reindex catalog_product_attribute
bin/magento indexer:reindex catalogsearch_fulltext

# Check index status
bin/magento indexer:status
```

### Step 7: Clear Cache

```bash
bin/magento cache:flush
# or
bin/magento cache:clean
```

### Step 8: Verify on Frontend

Navigate to your anchor category in the storefront. The new filter should appear in the layered navigation sidebar.

```
Troubleshooting Checklist
+-------------------------------------------+
| Attribute input type is Dropdown/Select?  |
| "Use in Layered Navigation" != No?        |
| Category "Is Anchor" = Yes?               |
| Attribute added to product attribute set? |
| Products have values for this attribute?  |
| Index has been rerun after changes?       |
| Cache has been cleared?                   |
+-------------------------------------------+
```

**Exam focus:**
- **All of these steps must be complete** for layered navigation to work
- The most common exam scenario: attribute is configured correctly, but the category is not set to anchor → filters do not appear
- Reindexing is **required** after attribute changes; cache flush alone is not sufficient

---

## 7. Tricky Exam Concepts Summary

This section consolidates the "gotcha" items that frequently appear on exams.

### "NOT LOGGED IN" is Customer Group 0

```
Common Misconception vs. Reality
+---------------------------------+--------------------------------+
| Wrong Assumption                | Correct Behavior               |
|---------------------------------|--------------------------------|
| Guests have no customer group   | Guests = Group 0 (NOT LOGGED IN)|
| Pricing rules skip guests       | Group 0 rules APPLY to guests  |
| Tax rules don't affect guests   | Group 0 tax class applies      |
| Cart rules require login        | Group 0 rules fire for guests  |
+---------------------------------+--------------------------------+
```

**Exam focus:**
- When creating a **catalog price rule** or **cart price rule** that should apply to guests, target **"NOT LOGGED IN"** customer group
- Tax rules assign a **customer tax class** — guest customers use the class assigned to Group 0

---

### Anchor Category Requirement

```
Category Anchor Setting Impact
+-------------------+------------------+-----------------------------+
| Is Anchor         | Layered Nav      | Shows Subcategory Products  |
|-------------------|------------------|-----------------------------|
| Yes               | Shows filters    | Yes (recursive)             |
| No                | No filters       | No                          |
+-------------------+------------------+-----------------------------+
```

---

### Search Synonyms Location

A very commonly tested navigation path:

```
WRONG paths (common distractors):
  - Stores > Configuration > Catalog > Search > Synonyms  [WRONG]
  - Catalog > Search Terms > Synonyms                     [WRONG]

CORRECT path:
  Admin > Marketing > SEO & Search > Search Synonyms      [CORRECT]
```

---

### Filterable (With Results) vs Filterable (No Results)

```
Scenario: Color filter, no "Purple" products exist

Filterable (with results):  Purple does NOT appear in filter list
Filterable (no results):    Purple STILL appears in filter list (with 0 count)
```

---

### CE vs EE Feature Matrix

| Feature | CE | EE |
|---|---|---|
| Layered Navigation | Yes | Yes |
| Single Wishlist | Yes | Yes |
| Multiple Wishlists | **No** | **Yes** |
| Customer Segments | **No** | **Yes** |
| Customer Groups | Yes | Yes |
| Store Credit | No | Yes |
| Reward Points | No | Yes |
| Gift Registry | No | Yes |

---

### Attribute Input Types & Layered Navigation Compatibility

| Input Type | Can Use in Layered Nav? |
|---|---|
| Dropdown | Yes |
| Multiple Select | Yes |
| Yes/No | Yes |
| Price | Yes (automatic) |
| Text Field | **No** |
| Text Area | **No** |
| Date | **No** |
| Media Image | **No** |

---

## Quick-Reference Checklist

### Layered Navigation
- [ ] Layered navigation appears **only on anchor categories** and **search results pages**
- [ ] Set category **Is Anchor = Yes** under `Catalog > Categories > Display Settings`
- [ ] Non-anchor categories **do not show** layered navigation filters
- [ ] Only **Dropdown, Multiple Select, Yes/No, and Price** attribute types support layered navigation
- [ ] "Filterable (with results)" hides options with 0 matching products
- [ ] "Filterable (no results)" shows all options regardless of match count
- [ ] After attribute changes, **reindex** (`bin/magento indexer:reindex`) and **clear cache**

### Price Ranges
- [ ] Three modes: **Automatic (Equalize Product Counts)**, **Automatic (Equalize Price Ranges)**, **Manual**
- [ ] Manual mode requires setting a **step value** (e.g., 100 = $100 increments)
- [ ] Path: `Stores > Configuration > Catalog > Catalog > Layered Navigation`

### Search Configuration
- [ ] Magento 2.4+ requires **OpenSearch** or **Elasticsearch** (MySQL search removed)
- [ ] OpenSearch is preferred/recommended from Magento **2.4.6+**
- [ ] **Search Suggestions** = "did you mean?" (spelling corrections)
- [ ] **Search Recommendations** = popular/related terms (not corrections)
- [ ] **Popular Search Terms** can be **redirected** to any URL
- [ ] **Search Synonyms path: Marketing > SEO & Search > Search Synonyms** (NOT under Catalog)
- [ ] Synonyms are **store-view scoped**
- [ ] Magento supports **two-way (grouped) synonyms only** — no one-way synonym support in the admin

### Customer Groups
- [ ] Group **0 = "NOT LOGGED IN"** = all guest/unauthenticated visitors
- [ ] Default groups: 0-NOT LOGGED IN, 1-General, 2-Wholesale, 3-Retailer
- [ ] Default groups **cannot be deleted**
- [ ] Customer groups affect: pricing, tax, shipping rules, promotions
- [ ] A customer belongs to **only one group** at a time
- [ ] Group 0 (NOT LOGGED IN) must be targeted in rules meant to apply to **guests**

### Customer Accounts
- [ ] Address book supports **multiple addresses** (separate default billing and shipping)
- [ ] Admin can create orders on behalf of customers from the customer edit page
- [ ] Customer edit page tabs: Account, Addresses, Orders, Cart, Wishlist, Newsletter, Reviews

### Customer Segments (EE Only)
- [ ] Customer Segments = **EE only** (Customer Groups = CE + EE)
- [ ] Segments evaluated **dynamically in real-time**; groups require manual assignment
- [ ] Segments support complex rules (order history, cart contents, demographics)

### Wishlist
- [ ] CE: **one wishlist per customer**
- [ ] EE: **multiple named wishlists** per customer (must be enabled in config)
- [ ] Wishlist sharing creates a **public read-only URL**
- [ ] Guests **cannot** use wishlists (login required)
- [ ] Items remain in wishlist after being added to cart (manual removal required)

### Newsletter
- [ ] Double opt-in = enable **"Need to Confirm"** setting
- [ ] Guests can subscribe if **"Allow Guest Subscription"** is enabled
- [ ] Subscriber path: `Marketing > Communications > Newsletter Subscribers`
- [ ] Statuses: Subscribed, Unsubscribed, Not Activated, Unconfirmed
- [ ] Newsletter subscriptions are **store-view specific**

### Hands-On Steps (Filterable Attribute)
1. [ ] Create attribute with correct input type (Dropdown, etc.)
2. [ ] Set "Use in Layered Navigation" = Filterable (with results)
3. [ ] Add attribute to attribute set
4. [ ] Assign values to products
5. [ ] Set target category **Is Anchor = Yes**
6. [ ] Run `bin/magento indexer:reindex`
7. [ ] Run `bin/magento cache:flush`
8. [ ] Verify filter appears on category page

flashcards.question: What is an Anchor category and what two things does it enable?
flashcards.answer: An Anchor category (Is Anchor = Yes in Display Settings) enables layered navigation filters on the category page AND causes the category to display products from all its child/subcategories. Non-anchor categories show no layered nav and only display their directly assigned products.
flashcards.hint: It pulls subcategory products up and adds filter sidebar panels.

flashcards.question: What is the difference between 'Filterable (with results)' and 'Filterable (no results)' for layered navigation?
flashcards.answer: 'Filterable (with results)' only shows a filter option if at least one product matches — better UX. 'Filterable (no results)' shows all filter options even if zero products match that value, which provides consistency but can confuse shoppers.
flashcards.hint: One hides empty options; the other always shows everything.

flashcards.question: Which attribute input types can be used in layered navigation?
flashcards.answer: Only Dropdown, Multiple Select, Yes/No, and Price attribute types support layered navigation. Text Field, Text Area, Date, and Media Image types cannot be used in layered navigation filters.
flashcards.hint: It needs discrete, selectable values — not free-form text.

flashcards.question: What is the correct admin path for Search Synonyms in Magento 2?
flashcards.answer: Marketing > SEO & Search > Search Synonyms. A common exam distractor places it under Stores > Configuration > Catalog or Catalog > Search Terms, but those are incorrect. Synonyms are store-view scoped and support only two-way (grouped) synonyms in the admin.
flashcards.hint: It is under Marketing, not Catalog or Stores.

flashcards.question: What is the significance of Customer Group 0 (NOT LOGGED IN) in Magento 2?
flashcards.answer: Group 0 — NOT LOGGED IN — is a real customer group that applies to all guest/unauthenticated visitors. It is used for guest pricing rules, tax class assignments for guests, and cart price rules targeting guests. It is not the absence of a group.
flashcards.hint: Guests are not ungrouped; they belong to a specific group with ID zero.

flashcards.question: What is the difference between Search Suggestions and Search Recommendations in Magento 2?
flashcards.answer: Search Suggestions provide 'did you mean?' spelling corrections for misspelled queries. Search Recommendations show popular or related search terms based on search history. They are distinct features with separate enable/count controls in Catalog Search configuration.
flashcards.hint: One corrects typos; the other suggests trending terms.

flashcards.question: Can a customer belong to more than one Customer Group at a time?
flashcards.answer: No. A customer can belong to only one customer group at a time. Changing a customer's group immediately affects their pricing, tax treatment, and which promotional rules apply to them. For more granular targeting, Adobe Commerce EE offers Customer Segments.
flashcards.hint: It is a one-to-one relationship, unlike segments which are many-to-many.

flashcards.question: What search engine does Magento 2.4.6+ recommend, and what happened to MySQL search?
flashcards.answer: OpenSearch is the recommended search engine from Magento 2.4.6+. MySQL search was completely removed in Magento 2.4. Elasticsearch 7 is still supported but being phased out. An external search engine is now required.
flashcards.hint: The open-source fork of Elasticsearch became the preferred option.

flashcards.question: Is Multiple Wishlists available in Magento Open Source?
flashcards.answer: No. Multiple Wishlists is an Adobe Commerce (EE) only feature that must be explicitly enabled in configuration. Magento Open Source supports exactly one wishlist per customer. In both editions, wishlists require a customer account — guests cannot use them.
flashcards.hint: CE gets one; EE can have many named lists per customer.

flashcards.question: What does enabling 'Need to Confirm' do for newsletter subscriptions?
flashcards.answer: It enables double opt-in — when a visitor subscribes, a confirmation email is sent and the subscription is not activated until they click the confirmation link. The subscriber status shows as 'Not Activated' until confirmed. This is important for GDPR compliance.
flashcards.hint: The subscriber must take an additional action after signing up.

flashcards.question: What three price range calculation modes are available for layered navigation?
flashcards.answer: Automatic (Equalize Product Counts) creates variable-width buckets with roughly equal products per bucket. Automatic (Equalize Price Ranges) creates equal-width buckets regardless of product distribution. Manual allows the admin to set a fixed step value (e.g., $100 increments).
flashcards.hint: Equal products per bucket, equal price width per bucket, or admin-defined fixed steps.

flashcards.question: Can popular search terms be redirected to a specific URL?
flashcards.answer: Yes. In Marketing > SEO & Search > Search Terms, admin can configure a search term with a redirect URL, sending customers who search for that term to a specific page. This is useful for promotions or directing searches to curated landing pages.
flashcards.hint: Search terms can be mapped to any destination, not just search results.

---

## 2. Core Features — Catalog Deep Dive

### Catalog Hierarchy

```
Magento Catalog
|
+-- Websites
    |
    +-- Store (Store Group)
        |
        +-- Store View
```

- A **Website** is the top-level scope for pricing, customer accounts
- A **Store** shares a root category and a group of store views
- A **Store View** typically controls language/locale

> **Exam focus:** Customer accounts belong to **Website** scope. Base currency is set at **Website** scope. Display currency is set at **Store View** scope.

### Root Categories & Category Trees

- Each **Store** must have exactly one **Root Category**
- Products can belong to multiple categories
- Category URL keys must be unique per store view
- **Anchor categories** pull products from all child categories via layered navigation

```php
// Retrieving the root category ID programmatically
$storeManager = $this->storeManagerInterface->getStore();
$rootCategoryId = $storeManager->getRootCategoryId();
```

> **Exam focus:** Anchor = YES on a category makes the **Layered Navigation** show subcategory products. Default is Anchor = YES for new categories.

### Attributes & Attribute Sets

| Concept | Detail |
|---|---|
| **Attribute Set** | Template of attributes grouped for a product type |
| **Attribute Group** | Visual tab grouping within an attribute set |
| **Default Attribute Set** | "Default" — every new attribute is added here unless specified |
| **Scope** | Global / Website / Store View |

Attribute scope rules:

```
Global  → same value across all websites and store views
Website → different per website
Store View → different per store view (e.g., Name, Description, URL Key)
```

> **Exam focus:** **Price** attribute is scoped at **Website** level by default. **Name** and **Description** are **Store View** scoped. Changing attribute scope affects ALL existing data.

### Configurable Product Attributes

- Only `select` (dropdown) and `swatch` type attributes can be used as configurable product options
- The attribute must have **Use to Create Configurable Product** = YES
- Attribute values create the child simple products (variations)

## 3. Product Type Edge Cases

This is one of the **most heavily tested** topics on the exam. Know every product type's behavior, limitations, and inventory impact.

### Product Type Comparison Table

| Product Type | Stock Tracked | Child Products | Cart Behavior | Price |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Simple | Yes | No | Adds directly | Fixed |
| Virtual | Yes | No | Adds directly, no shipping | Fixed |
| Downloadable | Yes | No | Adds directly, no shipping | Fixed |
| Configurable | No (parent) | Yes (simple) | Parent selected, child added | Range or child price |
| Grouped | No (parent) | Yes (simple/virtual) | Each child added separately | Sum of chosen children |
| Bundle | Optional | Yes (simple/virtual) | Bundle added as one unit | Dynamic or fixed |

> **Exam focus:** **Configurable** products do NOT hold inventory — only their child **simple** products do. A configurable product with no children cannot be added to cart.

### Simple Product

- Most basic product type
- Must have SKU, Name, Price, Visibility, Status
- Can be a standalone product or a child of Configurable/Grouped/Bundle

### Virtual Product

- No shipping required (services, memberships, warranties)
- **No weight** attribute — shipping step skipped if cart contains ONLY virtual products
- Still tracked in inventory

> **Exam focus:** If a cart contains **only virtual products**, the shipping step is **skipped** during checkout. This is a common exam trap question.

### Downloadable Product

- Links and samples defined on product
- Links can be purchased and downloaded multiple times (configurable)
- **Shareable** link setting: if YES, no login required to download; if NO, customer must be logged in
- Can still have weight if physical component exists alongside download

> **Exam focus:** **Shareable = No** requires the customer to be **logged in** to access the download link. Know the difference between shareable and non-shareable download behavior.

### Configurable Product — Edge Cases

```
Parent Configurable (SKU: shirt-configurable)
    |
    +-- Child Simple (SKU: shirt-red-sm, Stock: 5)
    +-- Child Simple (SKU: shirt-red-md, Stock: 0)   <-- Out of stock
    +-- Child Simple (SKU: shirt-blue-sm, Stock: 3)
```

- Out-of-stock child options are **greyed out** but still visible by default
- The **parent** configurable product price can be set but is typically overridden by child price
- Configurable product itself has **no direct inventory** — MSI tracks child SKUs

> **Exam focus:** When a configurable product's child simple is out of stock, the option is greyed out on the frontend, NOT hidden (unless specifically configured via "Display Out of Stock Products" setting).

### Grouped Product — Edge Cases

- Groups related but separately purchasable products
- Customer sets **quantity for each child** individually
- The grouped product itself has **no price** — prices come from associated simple/virtual products
- If all children are out of stock, the grouped product shows as out of stock

> **Exam focus:** A **Grouped** product has **no price of its own**. The customer pays for each associated product at its own price. There is no "bundle discount" concept in grouped products.

### Bundle Product — Edge Cases

Bundle with **Dynamic Price**:

```
Bundle Options:
  Option 1 (Required, Radio): 
      - Processor A (+$100)
      - Processor B (+$150)
  Option 2 (Optional, Checkbox):
      - Extra RAM (+$50)
      - More RAM (+$75)

Total = Base Bundle Price + Sum of Selected Options
```

Bundle with **Fixed Price**:
- Price is set on the bundle itself, not derived from children
- Tier prices and special prices apply to fixed price bundles

| Bundle Attribute | Dynamic Price | Fixed Price |
|---|---|---|
| Special Price | No | Yes |
| Tier Price | No | Yes |
| Catalog Price Rule | No | Yes |
| Customer Group Price | No | Yes |

> **Exam focus:** **Dynamic Price bundles** do NOT support special prices, tier prices, or catalog price rules — these apply only to **Fixed Price** bundles. This is a very common exam question.

### Gift Card Product (Adobe Commerce Only — not Magento Open Source)

- Types: Virtual, Physical, Combined
- Amount: Fixed amounts or Open amount (customer defined within min/max range)
- Gift card codes are generated automatically

> **Exam focus:** **Gift Card** product type is **Adobe Commerce (Enterprise) only**, not available in Magento Open Source. Know which features are EE-only vs CE.

## 4. Pricing Hierarchy

Understanding the pricing waterfall is critical. The system evaluates prices in a specific order and picks the **lowest applicable price**.

### Price Hierarchy (Waterfall)

```
1. Regular Price (Base Price on product)
         |
         v
2. Special Price (date-bound override)
         |
         v
3. Tier Price / Customer Group Price
         |
         v
4. Catalog Price Rule (matches first applicable rule by priority)
         |
         v
5. Cart Price Rule (applied at checkout, not catalog level)
```

> **Exam focus:** The **lowest price wins** among Special Price and Tier Price. Catalog Price Rules apply to the catalog (product detail/listing pages). Cart Price Rules apply at checkout. They are evaluated at DIFFERENT stages.

### Special Price

- Set directly on a product
- Has **From Date** and **To Date** — if no dates set, it applies immediately and indefinitely
- Overrides regular price when active

```php
// Special price is stored as special_price attribute
// Active when: special_price < price AND today is within from_date/to_date
```

### Tier Pricing

Tier prices define price breaks by **quantity** and optionally by **customer group**:

| Qty | Customer Group | Price |
|---|---|---|
| 5 | All Groups | $9.00 |
| 10 | All Groups | $8.00 |
| 5 | Wholesale | $7.50 |

- Tier price can be expressed as a **fixed price** or a **percentage discount**
- The customer sees the lowest applicable tier price for their group and quantity

> **Exam focus:** Tier prices are evaluated per **customer group AND quantity**. The most specific and lowest price wins. A customer in "Wholesale" group buying 5 gets $7.50, not $9.00.

### Customer Group Pricing

- Customer Groups: NOT LOGGED IN, General, Wholesale, Retailer (default groups)
- "NOT LOGGED IN" = Guest customers
- Tier price with qty = 1 effectively becomes a **customer group price**

```
Tier Price: Qty=1, Group=Wholesale, Price=$45
= This is a "customer group price" — no quantity break needed
```

### Catalog Price Rules

- Applied to **product prices in the catalog** (before adding to cart)
- Priority: lower number = higher priority (1 runs before 2)
- **Stop Further Rules Processing**: if checked, no lower-priority rules run after this one matches

Rule structure:
```
Conditions (AND/OR logic):
  - Category is [Electronics]
  - Attribute Set is [Laptop]

Actions:
  - Apply: By Percentage of Original Price
  - Discount Amount: 10
  - Stop Further Rules: No
```

> **Exam focus:** Catalog Price Rules have **Priority** (lower = higher priority). If "Stop Further Rules Processing" is YES, subsequent rules do not apply. Cart Price Rules have **Sort Order** with same logic.

### Cart Price Rules

- Applied **during checkout** on cart/quote level
- Can generate **coupon codes** (auto or manual)
- Can apply to specific **products, shipping, entire cart**
- Conditions checked against cart items

Actions available in Cart Price Rules:

| Action | Description |
|---|---|
| Percent of product price discount | X% off qualifying items |
| Fixed amount discount | $X off qualifying items |
| Fixed amount discount for whole cart | $X off entire cart |
| Buy X get Y free | BXGY promotions |
| No discount | Used with "Free Shipping" only |

> **Exam focus:** **"Buy X Get Y Free"** is a **Cart Price Rule** action, not a Catalog Price Rule. Coupon codes are only available in **Cart Price Rules**, not Catalog Price Rules.

### MAP (Minimum Advertised Price)

- Available in **Magento Open Source** (not EE-only — `module-msrp` has OSL-3.0 license)
- Prevents displaying actual price on catalog pages
- Shows "Click for price" or adds to cart to reveal price
- The **actual price** is shown in the cart

## 5. Order State vs Status

This is a guaranteed exam topic. The distinction between **State** and **Status** is architectural.

### Conceptual Difference

```
STATE = System-level, hard-coded, controls business logic
STATUS = Admin-defined label, maps TO a state, human-readable display
```

```
State (fixed)          Status (configurable examples)
-----------            --------------------------
new                --> Pending, Pending Payment
pending_payment    --> Pending PayPal, Awaiting Payment
processing         --> Processing, Fraud Review
complete           --> Complete
closed             --> Closed
canceled           --> Canceled
holded             --> On Hold
payment_review     --> Payment Review
```

> **Exam focus:** States are **hard-coded** in the system and drive workflow logic. Statuses are **configurable in Admin** (Stores > Order Statuses) and are purely display labels. You can create new statuses and assign them to existing states, but you **cannot create new states**.

### Order State Flow Diagram

```
[Cart / Quote]
      |
      v
[new] <-- Order placed, payment method captured / awaiting capture
      |
      v
[pending_payment] <-- Payment gateway redirect (e.g., PayPal redirect)
      |
      v
[processing] <-- Payment captured, invoice created
      |
      v
[complete] <-- All items shipped + invoiced
      |
      v
[closed] <-- Fully refunded via Credit Memo
      |
[canceled] <-- Order canceled (from new or processing, before shipment)
      |
[holded] <-- Manually placed on hold by admin
```

### Key State Transition Rules

| Rule | Detail |
|---|---|
| An order moves to `complete` when... | All items are **invoiced AND shipped** |
| An order moves to `closed` when... | A **credit memo** is created for the full order |
| `canceled` is only possible when... | Order is in `new` or `processing` state (no shipment yet) |
| `holded` can be applied from... | Most active states |
| `pending_payment` occurs when... | Customer is redirected to payment gateway (no response yet) |

> **Exam focus:** `closed` ≠ `canceled`. **Closed** means a refund (credit memo) was issued. **Canceled** means the order was canceled before fulfillment. An order that has been shipped **cannot be canceled** — it must be refunded to move to `closed`.

### Invoice, Shipment, Credit Memo Relationship

```
Order
  |
  +-- Invoice (captures payment, triggers processing state)
  |
  +-- Shipment (ships items, triggers complete state when all shipped+invoiced)
  |
  +-- Credit Memo (refund document, triggers closed state if full refund)
```

> **Exam focus:** Shipments do **not** require a prior invoice — `canShip()` checks item qty, hold status, and other conditions but does **not** check invoice existence. You can ship before invoicing. However, you must have payment captured (typically via an **Invoice**) before you can create a **Credit Memo**, since `canCreditmemo()` checks `getTotalPaid()`.

### Custom Order Statuses

```
Admin > Stores > Settings > Order Status

Steps to create a custom status:
1. Create status with a label (e.g., "Awaiting Warehouse Pickup")
2. Assign it to an existing State (e.g., "Processing")
3. Optionally set as default for that state
```

## 6. CMS Block vs Page vs Widget

This is a commonly missed distinction on the exam. Each has a specific purpose and different scope behavior.

### Comparison Table

| Feature | CMS Block | CMS Page | Widget |
|---|---|---|---|
| Has URL | No | Yes | No |
| Can be placed via Layout XML | Yes | No | Yes |
| Has meta title/description | No | Yes | No |
| Store View scoped | Yes | Yes | Yes |
| Reusable | Yes | N/A | Yes |
| Contains HTML/CSS | Yes | Yes | No (uses template) |
| Requires unique identifier | Yes (Block ID) | Yes (URL Key) | No |
| Can insert into CMS content | Yes (directive) | No | Yes (via admin UI) |

### CMS Block (Static Block)

- Pure HTML/CSS/JS content fragment
- Identified by **Block Identifier** (programmatic key, lowercase, underscores)
- Inserted into other pages/blocks using a **directive**:

```html
{{block class="Magento\Cms\Block\Block" block_id="my_block_identifier"}}
```

Or in WYSIWYG via the Insert Widget button (which generates the directive).

- No routing — cannot be visited as a URL
- Can be assigned to **specific store views** or all store views

> **Exam focus:** CMS Blocks do NOT have URLs. They are **embedded** in pages or layouts. The Block Identifier is case-sensitive and must be unique.

### CMS Page

- Has its own **URL Key** (routed as `/url-key`)
- Has **Page Title**, **Meta Title**, **Meta Keywords**, **Meta Description** for SEO
- Has a **Content Heading** (H1 equivalent on page)
- Can use **Page Layout** (1 column, 2 columns left/right, 3 columns)
- Can be set as the **Home Page** (configured in Stores > Configuration > Web > Default Pages)

```
Special CMS Pages:
- Home Page (default: "home")
- 404 Not Found Page (default: "no-route")
- Cookie Restriction Notice Page
- Enable Cookies Page
```

> **Exam focus:** The **404 page** in Magento is a **CMS page** with URL key `no-route`. The home page URL key is configurable in Stores > Configuration > General > Web > Default Pages > CMS Home Page.

### Widget

- Dynamic, data-driven component inserted into the layout or CMS content
- **Not raw HTML** — it uses a PHP class and template to render
- Configured through Admin UI: Content > Widgets
- Can be placed on **specific pages, categories, products, or all pages**
- Placement defined by **Container** (a layout container name, e.g., `content`, `sidebar.main`)

Common widget types:

| Widget Type | What It Renders |
|---|---|
| CMS Static Block | Embeds a CMS Block |
| CMS Page Link | Link to a CMS page |
| Catalog Category Link | Link to a category |
| Catalog Product Link | Link to a product |
| Catalog New Products List | Dynamic list of new products |
| Orders and Returns | Order search form |
| Recently Compared Products | Recently compared list |
| Recently Viewed Products | Recently viewed list |

> **Exam focus:** The **"CMS Static Block" widget type** is used to insert a CMS Block via the widget system. Know that a widget has **Page Layouts** and **Widget Options** configured in the Admin. A widget references a PHP class; a CMS block is pure content.

### Insertion Methods Summary

```
Method 1 — Layout XML (blocks and widgets):
<block class="Magento\Cms\Block\Block" name="my.block">
    <arguments>
        <argument name="block_id" xsi:type="string">my_identifier</argument>
    </arguments>
</block>

Method 2 — CMS Content Directive (blocks only):
{{block class="Magento\Cms\Block\Block" block_id="my_identifier"}}

Method 3 — Admin Widget UI (widgets only):
Content > Widgets > Add Widget
Select Type, Theme, Store Views, Layout Updates, Widget Options

Method 4 — WYSIWYG Insert Widget Button:
Generates the directive automatically in page/block content
```

### Template Directives in CMS Content

```html
<!-- Insert a static block -->
{{block class="Magento\Cms\Block\Block" block_id="footer_links_block"}}

<!-- Insert a widget -->
{{widget type="Magento\Cms\Block\Widget\Page\Link" 
         anchor_text="Contact Us" 
         page_id="4"}}

<!-- Store variable -->
{{store url="contact"}}

<!-- Media URL -->
{{media url="wysiwyg/banner.jpg"}}
```

> **Exam focus:** `{{block ...}}` directive inserts a CMS static block. `{{widget ...}}` inserts a widget. These directives are processed by the **template engine** before HTML is sent to the browser.

## 7. Customer Journey Fundamentals

### Guest vs Registered Customer Checkout

| Feature | Guest | Registered |
|---|---|---|
| Address book | No | Yes |
| Saved payment methods | No | Yes (vault) |
| Order history | No (email only) | Yes |
| Wishlist | No | Yes |
| Reorder | No | Yes |
| Cart persistence | Session only | Configurable (persistent cart) |

> **Exam focus:** **Persistent Shopping Cart** is a feature that saves a registered customer's cart across sessions using a cookie. Guests do not benefit from persistent cart.

### Checkout Steps

```
Step 1: Shipping (address + method)
    |
    v
Step 2: Payment (+ optional coupon code)
    |
    v
Step 3: Order Review & Place Order
    |
    v
Order Confirmation Page + Email
```

Checkout is **skipped steps** in these scenarios:
- Only virtual products → Shipping step skipped
- Free order ($0) → Payment step may be simplified

### Customer Groups

Default customer groups:

| Group ID | Group Name | Description |
|---|---|---|
| 0 | NOT LOGGED IN | Guest customers |
| 1 | General | Default registered customers |
| 2 | Wholesale | Higher-volume buyers |
| 3 | Retailer | Resellers |

- Customer groups control: **tier prices, catalog rules, cart rules, tax classes**
- New customers are assigned to **General** by default
- Group can be changed manually or via **auto-assignment** based on VAT ID validation

> **Exam focus:** Group ID **0 = NOT LOGGED IN** (guests). Group ID **1 = General** (default registered). Customer group affects pricing rules and tax calculation.

### Wishlist

- Available to **logged-in customers only**
- Items can be moved or copied from wishlist to cart
- Wishlists can be shared via email (generates a unique shareable URL)
- **Multiple Wishlists** is an **Adobe Commerce** (EE) feature only

> **Exam focus:** Multiple Wishlists is **Adobe Commerce only**. Magento Open Source supports only **one wishlist per customer**.

### Compare Products

- Compares up to **4 products** by default (configurable)
- Uses a **session-based** comparison list
- Compare list is **not** saved across sessions by default
- A **Recently Compared** widget can show previous comparisons

### Customer Account Sections

```
My Account
  |
  +-- My Orders
  +-- My Downloadable Products
  +-- My Wish List
  +-- Address Book (default billing + shipping)
  +-- Account Information (name, email, password)
  +-- Stored Payment Methods (vault)
  +-- My Product Reviews
  +-- Newsletter Subscriptions
```

## 8. Commerce Basics Section Review

### Store Configuration Scope

```
Default Config (Global)
    |
    +-- Website Level Config
            |
            +-- Store Level Config
                    |
                    +-- Store View Level Config
```

- More specific scope **overrides** less specific
- "Use Default" checkbox returns to parent scope value

### Indexers

Indexers pre-compute data for fast frontend retrieval:

| Indexer | What It Does |
|---|---|
| Category Products | Maps products to categories |
| Product Categories | Maps categories to products |
| Product Price | Computes final prices (tier, special, rules) |
| Product EAV | Denormalizes EAV attribute data |
| Stock | Computes stock status |
| Catalog Search | Builds search index |
| Catalog Rule Product Price | Applies catalog price rules |

Indexer modes:

```bash
# Update on Save (default) - re-indexes when entity is saved
bin/magento indexer:set-mode realtime [indexer]

# Update by Schedule - uses cron, batched updates
bin/magento indexer:set-mode schedule [indexer]

# Manual reindex
bin/magento indexer:reindex

# Check status
bin/magento indexer:status
```

> **Exam focus:** **Update by Schedule** mode uses **Mview** (Materialized View) to track changes via database changelog tables and processes them via **cron**. This is more performant for large catalogs.

### Cache Types

```bash
# List all cache types
bin/magento cache:status

# Flush specific type
bin/magento cache:flush full_page

# Common types:
config          - Merged XML config files
layout          - Layout XML compilation results
block_html      - Rendered block HTML
collections     - Database query collections
full_page       - Full page cache (FPC)
translate       - Translation strings
eav             - EAV attribute metadata
```

> **Exam focus:** **Full Page Cache (FPC)** stores complete rendered HTML. It can use the **built-in** cache (Magento's own cache storage) or **Varnish** (external). Enabling FPC dramatically reduces server load.

### Tax Configuration

Tax calculation based on:
- **Customer Tax Class** (from customer group)
- **Product Tax Class** (assigned to product)
- **Tax Zone/Rate** (defined by country/state/zip)

Tax Rules combine all three:
```
Tax Rule = Customer Tax Class + Product Tax Class + Tax Zone/Rate
```

Tax display options:
- Including Tax
- Excluding Tax  
- Including and Excluding Tax

> **Exam focus:** Tax is calculated based on **Tax Rules** that intersect Customer Tax Class, Product Tax Class, and Tax Zone/Rate. All three must match for a tax rule to apply.

Catalog URLs:

### Related Products, Up-sells, Cross-sells

## 10. Compliance Section Review

### Cookie Law / GDPR Compliance Features

Built-in Magento compliance features:

```
Stores > Config > General > Web > Default Cookie Settings:
- Cookie Lifetime (seconds)
- Cookie Path
- Cookie Domain
- Use HTTP Only (Yes recommended)
- Cookie Restriction Mode: Yes/No
```

**Cookie Restriction Mode:**
- When enabled, a banner is shown
- Magento does not store non-essential cookies until user accepts
- After acceptance, a `user_allowed_save_cookie` cookie is set (defined as `IS_USER_ALLOWED_SAVE_COOKIE` in `Magento\Cookie\Helper\Cookie`)

> **Exam focus:** **Cookie Restriction Mode** prevents Magento from setting **non-essential cookies** until the customer consents. This is the built-in GDPR cookie consent mechanism.

### Privacy Policy

- CMS page with URL key `privacy-policy-cookie-restriction-mode` (for cookie notice link)
- Regular privacy policy is a separate CMS page
- Footer links managed via CMS blocks

### PCI Compliance Considerations

- Magento itself does not store raw credit card numbers (uses tokenization)
- **Payment vault** stores tokens, not card numbers
- **3D Secure** support for card verification
- Admin access logs, CAPTCHA features

> **Exam focus:** Magento does not store full credit card numbers. Payment tokens (references to stored card data at the payment gateway) are stored in the **vault** (`vault_payment_token` table).

### Customer Data Privacy

```
Admin > Customers > Now Online
Admin > System > Action Logs (EE only)

GDPR-related features (Adobe Commerce):
- Customer data deletion requests
- Data export (portability)
- Consent management
```

> **Exam focus:** **Data deletion** and **data export** for GDPR are **Adobe Commerce (EE) only** features, not available in Magento Open Source.

### Security Features

| Feature | Location |
|---|---|
| Admin Two-Factor Auth (2FA) | Admin > Stores > Config > Security |
| CAPTCHA (admin) | Admin > Stores > Config > Admin > CAPTCHA |
| CAPTCHA (storefront) | Admin > Stores > Config > Customers > CAPTCHA |
| Admin URL customization | env.php `backend/frontName` |
| reCAPTCHA | Admin > Stores > Config > Security |
| Password Policy | Min length, required character classes |

> **Exam focus:** The **Admin URL** should be changed from the default `/admin` for security. It is configured in `app/etc/env.php` under `backend > frontName` or during installation.
