```
| 3 |                                  |        |                                         |
| 4 |                                  |        |                                         |
| 5 |                                  |        |                                         |
+---+----------------------------------+--------+-----------------------------------------+
```

### Predicted High-Risk Topics (Based on Exam Blueprint)

These are statistically most-tested and most-missed based on the AD0-E712 blueprint:

| Rank | Topic | Why It's Hard | Study Action |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | **Pricing Hierarchy** | Multiple overlapping rules with priority logic | Draw the waterfall, practice scenarios |
| 2 | **Product Type Differences** | Many similar types with subtle differences | Build comparison table from memory |
| 3 | **Order State vs Status** | Architectural concept, not UI-obvious | Memorize state machine diagram |
| 4 | **Configurable Attribute Rules** | Specific requirements often forgotten | List all 3 requirements from memory |
| 5 | **CMS Block vs Widget** | Abstract distinction, similar use cases | Identify each by "Does it have PHP class?" |

### Bonus Watch Topics

- **EE vs Open Source feature split** (Gift Cards, Multiple Wishlists, GDPR tools)
- **Scope rules** for attributes (Global/Website/Store View)
- **Indexer modes** (Realtime vs Schedule)
- **Virtual product checkout flow** (shipping step skip)
- **Bundle Dynamic vs Fixed price** (which promotions apply)

---

## Quick-Reference Checklist

### Exam Logistics
- [ ] AD0-E712 — 50 questions, 110 minutes, 68% passing score
- [ ] Domain weights: Core Features 49%, Commerce Basics 14%, Digital Marketing 24%, Compliance 13%
- [ ] Score each domain separately during practice tests

### Product Types
- [ ] Simple — basic, tracks stock directly
- [ ] Virtual — no shipping, no weight, skips shipping step if cart is all-virtual
- [ ] Downloadable — shareable=No requires login to download
- [ ] Configurable — NO inventory at parent level, only children track stock
- [ ] Grouped — no price of its own, customer sets qty per child separately
- [ ] Bundle Dynamic Price — NO special price, tier price, or catalog rules
- [ ] Bundle Fixed Price — supports special price, tier price, catalog rules
- [ ] Gift Card — Adobe Commerce ONLY (not Open Source)
- [ ] Out-of-stock configurable child options are greyed out, not hidden

### Pricing Hierarchy
- [ ] Order: Regular > Special > Tier/Group > Catalog Rule (lowest wins)
- [ ] Cart Price Rules apply at checkout, NOT on catalog pages
- [ ] Catalog Price Rules apply to displayed product prices
- [ ] Lower priority number = runs first in Catalog/Cart Price Rules
- [ ] "Stop Further Rules Processing" halts lower-priority rules
- [ ] Tier price qty=1 = customer group price
- [ ] Guest = "NOT LOGGED IN" group (ID 0), General = default registered (ID 1)
- [ ] Coupon codes only exist in Cart Price Rules, not Catalog Price Rules
- [ ] MAP (Minimum Advertised Price) = available in Open Source (`module-msrp` has OSL-3.0 license)

### Order States vs Statuses
- [ ] States are hard-coded; statuses are admin-configurable labels
- [ ] Cannot create new states, only new statuses assigned to existing states
- [ ] `new` → payment placed, awaiting processing
- [ ] `pending_payment` → customer redirected to gateway, awaiting response
- [ ] `processing` → invoice created, payment captured
- [ ] `complete` → all items invoiced AND shipped
- [ ] `closed` → full credit memo issued (refund)
- [ ] `canceled` → order canceled before shipment
- [ ] `holded` → manually placed on hold
- [ ] Closed ≠ Canceled — closed = refunded, canceled = voided before fulfillment
- [ ] Shipments do NOT require a prior invoice — you can ship before invoicing
- [ ] Credit memos require payment captured (typically via invoice) — `canCreditmemo()` checks `getTotalPaid()`

### CMS Content Types
- [ ] CMS Block — no URL, no meta tags, embedded via directive or layout XML
- [ ] CMS Page — has URL key, has meta tags, can be home page or 404
- [ ] Widget — has PHP class, configured in Admin, placed in containers
- [ ] 404 page = CMS page with URL key `no-route`
- [ ] `{{block class="..." block_id="..."}}` = insert CMS block
- [ ] `{{widget type="..."}}` = insert widget
- [ ] Widget type "CMS Static Block" embeds a CMS block via the widget system
- [ ] Multiple Wishlists = Adobe Commerce only

### Customer Journey
- [ ] Cart with only virtual products = shipping step skipped
- [ ] Persistent Cart = registered customers only
- [ ] Cross-sells appear on CART page; Up-sells and Related appear on PRODUCT page
- [ ] Compare Products: up to 4 by default, session-based
- [ ] Wishlist = logged in only; Multiple wishlists = EE only

### Catalog Architecture
- [ ] Price attribute scope = Website level by default
- [ ] Name, Description, URL Key = Store View scope
- [ ] Changing attribute scope affects ALL existing data
- [ ] Only `select`/`swatch` type attributes can be configurable product options
- [ ] Anchor category = YES pulls products from subcategories into layered nav
- [ ] Root Category is assigned per Store (not Store View, not Website)

### Indexers & Cache
- [ ] Update on Save (realtime) vs Update by Schedule (Mview + cron)
- [ ] Full Page Cache (FPC) = built-in or Varnish
- [ ] `bin/magento indexer:reindex` for manual reindex
- [ ] `bin/magento cache:flush full_page` to flush FPC

### SEO & Digital Marketing
- [ ] XML Sitemap generated by cron, submitted to search engines
- [ ] URL rewrites auto-created when URL key changes (301 redirect preserved)
- [ ] Cross-sells on cart page, up-sells on product page
- [ ] Email templates use `{{var ...}}` for variables, `{{trans "..."}}` for translation

### Compliance & Security
- [ ] Cookie Restriction Mode = built-in GDPR cookie consent mechanism
- [ ] Magento stores payment TOKENS not card numbers (PCI)
- [ ] GDPR data deletion + data export = Adobe Commerce ONLY
- [ ] Admin URL should be customized (configured in env.php)
- [ ] 2FA available for Admin logins

### EE vs Open Source — Know the Difference
- [ ] Gift Cards → EE only
- [ ] Multiple Wishlists → EE only
- [ ] GDPR data tools → EE only
- [ ] MAP (Minimum Advertised Price) → Open Source (NOT EE-only)
- [ ] Action Logs (Admin audit log) → EE only
- [ ] Customer Segments → EE only
- [ ] Reward Points → EE only
- [ ] Return Merchandise Authorization (RMA) → EE only

---

*Study notes compiled for AD0-E712 Adobe Commerce Business Practitioner Professional — Week 1 Review / Practice Test #1*

*Next: Flag top 5 weak topics → Week 2 deep-dive modules*

flashcards.question: What CMS page URL key serves as the 404 Not Found page in Magento 2?
flashcards.answer: The 404 page is a CMS page with the URL key 'no-route'. The home page URL key is configurable in Stores > Configuration > General > Web > Default Pages > CMS Home Page (default: 'home').
flashcards.hint: It is not called '404' — it uses a routing-related name.

flashcards.question: What are the four domain sections tested on the AD0-E712 exam and their approximate weights?
flashcards.answer: Magento Open Source Core Features (49%, ~25 questions), Digital Marketing & eCommerce Fundamentals (24%, ~12 questions), Adobe Commerce Basics (14%, ~7 questions), and Compliance/Security Basics (13%, ~6 questions). Core Features is by far the heaviest section.
flashcards.hint: Nearly half the exam focuses on one domain.

flashcards.question: What is the passing score for the AD0-E712 exam?
flashcards.answer: The passing score is 68%, which means 34 correct answers out of 50 questions. The exam allows 110 minutes and costs $180 USD.
flashcards.hint: Just over two-thirds correct is the threshold.

flashcards.question: Why can Dynamic Price bundle products NOT support special prices, tier prices, or catalog price rules?
flashcards.answer: Dynamic Price bundles derive their total from the sum of selected component prices — the bundle itself has no editable base price. Since special prices, tier prices, and catalog rules need to apply to a product's own price field, they only work on Fixed Price bundles which have a manually set base price.
flashcards.hint: No base price to discount means no place for these pricing features to attach.

flashcards.question: Where do cross-sell products appear versus up-sell products in Magento 2?
flashcards.answer: Cross-sell products appear on the shopping cart page as complementary items. Up-sell products appear on the product detail page (PDP) as more expensive alternatives. Related Products also appear on the PDP as alternative options.
flashcards.hint: Cross-sells suggest additions at cart time; up-sells suggest upgrades while browsing.

flashcards.question: What is Cookie Restriction Mode and what does it do?
flashcards.answer: Cookie Restriction Mode is Magento's built-in GDPR cookie consent mechanism. When enabled, Magento does not store non-essential cookies until the customer accepts. A banner is shown, and only after acceptance is the user_allowed_save_cookie cookie set.
flashcards.hint: It prevents tracking cookies until explicit consent is given.

flashcards.question: Does Magento store full credit card numbers?
flashcards.answer: No. Magento uses tokenization — payment tokens (references to card data stored at the payment gateway) are saved in the vault_payment_token table. Full card numbers are never stored in the Magento database, which helps with PCI compliance.
flashcards.hint: Tokens are safe references, not the actual sensitive data.

flashcards.question: What is the difference between an HTML sitemap and an XML sitemap?
flashcards.answer: An HTML sitemap is a frontend page designed for human navigation, helping visitors find content. An XML sitemap is a file (typically /sitemap.xml) generated by cron for search engine bots, containing URLs with frequency and priority metadata for indexing.
flashcards.hint: One is for people clicking links; the other is for search crawlers.

flashcards.question: What is the Persistent Shopping Cart feature and who can use it?
flashcards.answer: Persistent Shopping Cart saves a registered customer's cart contents across browser sessions using a cookie, so items are not lost when the session expires. It is only available to registered (logged-in) customers — guests do not benefit from cart persistence.
flashcards.hint: Logged-in users get their cart remembered; guests start fresh each session.

flashcards.question: Where is the custom Admin URL configured in Magento 2?
flashcards.answer: The Admin URL is configured in app/etc/env.php under the 'backend' > 'frontName' key, or during installation. It should be changed from the default /admin for security purposes. This is not configurable through the Admin UI.
flashcards.hint: It is a server-side configuration file, not an admin panel setting.

flashcards.question: How is a Tax Rule constructed in Magento 2?
flashcards.answer: A Tax Rule combines three components: Customer Tax Class (from customer group), Product Tax Class (assigned to the product), and Tax Zone/Rate (defined by country, state, and ZIP code). All three must match for the tax rule to apply to a transaction.
flashcards.hint: Three dimensions intersect: who is buying, what they are buying, and where it is going.

flashcards.question: Are GDPR data deletion and data export features available in Magento Open Source?
flashcards.answer: No. GDPR data deletion requests and data export (portability) features are Adobe Commerce (EE) only. Magento Open Source does not include these built-in compliance tools, though custom extensions could add similar functionality.
flashcards.hint: Privacy compliance tools are a premium feature.

flashcards.question: What does the 'Use to Create Configurable Product' attribute setting do?
flashcards.answer: When set to Yes on a Dropdown, Visual Swatch, or Text Swatch attribute with Global scope, it allows that attribute to be used as a configurable product axis for creating product variations. Without this setting enabled, the attribute cannot be selected during the 'Create Configurations' workflow.
flashcards.hint: It is the third requirement alongside input type and scope.

flashcards.question: What is the Mview (Materialized View) system used for in Magento indexing?
flashcards.answer: Mview is the change-tracking mechanism used by the 'Update by Schedule' indexer mode. It tracks entity changes in database changelog tables and processes them in batches via cron, rather than reindexing immediately on every save. This is more performant for large catalogs.
flashcards.hint: It is the engine behind scheduled indexing that watches for changes between cron runs.

flashcards.question: What is the maximum number of products that can be compared by default in Magento 2?
flashcards.answer: Up to 4 products can be compared by default (configurable). The comparison list is session-based and not saved across sessions by default. A Recently Compared widget can show previous comparisons.
flashcards.hint: A small number that fits in a side-by-side table layout.

studyNotes.title: Day 8 — Shipping Methods & Carriers
studyNotes.content:
# Magento 2 Shipping Methods & Carriers — Complete Study Notes

---

## Table of Contents

1. [Shipping Architecture Overview](#1-shipping-architecture-overview)
2. [Origin Address Configuration](#2-origin-address-configuration)
3. [Shipping Zones & Restrictions](#3-shipping-zones--restrictions)
4. [Flat Rate Shipping](#4-flat-rate-shipping)
5. [Free Shipping Method](#5-free-shipping-method)
6. [Table Rate Shipping](#6-table-rate-shipping)
7. [Carrier Integrations (UPS / FedEx / USPS / DHL)](#7-carrier-integrations-ups--fedex--usps--dhl)
8. [In-Store Delivery / Store Pickup](#8-in-store-delivery--store-pickup)
9. [Multi-Address Checkout (Commerce/EE)](#9-multi-address-checkout-commerceee)
10. [Free Shipping — Cart Rule vs Method Trigger](#10-free-shipping--cart-rule-vs-method-trigger)
11. [Hands-On Configuration Lab](#11-hands-on-configuration-lab)
12. [Common Pitfalls & Tricky Exam Scenarios](#12-common-pitfalls--tricky-exam-scenarios)
13. [Quick-Reference Checklist](#quick-reference-checklist)

---

## 1. Shipping Architecture Overview

Magento 2 separates **shipping methods** into two broad categories:

```
+-------------------------------+----------------------------------+
|   OFFLINE CARRIERS            |   ONLINE / REAL-TIME CARRIERS    |
+-------------------------------+----------------------------------+
| Flat Rate                     | UPS                              |
| Free Shipping                 | FedEx                            |
| Table Rate                    | USPS                             |
| In-Store Pickup               | DHL                              |
+-------------------------------+----------------------------------+
         |                                  |
         v                                  v
  Configured locally              Calls external APIs
  No account needed               Account credentials required
  Rates are static                Rates are dynamic/live
```

### How Shipping Rate Collection Works

```
Customer Checkout
      |
      v
  Cart / Quote Object
      |
      v
  Magento calls each active carrier's collectRates()
      |
      +---> Offline carriers: calculate locally
      |
      +---> Online carriers: send HTTP request to API
      |
      v
  Rates returned -> displayed to customer
```

**Exam focus:**
- Offline carriers never contact external APIs — rates are pre-configured in Admin
- Online carriers require valid account credentials; failures fall back gracefully (or show error)
- Every carrier extends `\Magento\Shipping\Model\Carrier\AbstractCarrier`

---

## 2. Origin Address Configuration

The **origin (shipping) address** is the base from which all carrier rate calculations begin. It is configurable at **Default and Website** scope (showInDefault=1, showInWebsite=1, NO showInStore) — so different websites can have different origin addresses.

### Admin Path

```
Stores > Configuration > Sales > Shipping Settings > Origin
```

### Fields Configured

| Field | Description | Impact |
|-------|-------------|--------|
| Country | Sender country | Mandatory for all carriers |
| Region / State | Sender state or province | Required for US-based carriers |
| ZIP / Postal Code | Origin ZIP code | Distance-based rate calculations |
| City | Sender city | Some carriers use for zone lookup |
| Street Address | Full street | Used on shipping labels |

**Exam focus:**
- The origin address affects **all** carrier rate calculations — both offline (Table Rate zones) and online (UPS/FedEx distance-based pricing)
- Incorrect or missing origin ZIP can cause real-time carriers to return **no rates**
- Origin is configurable at **Default and Website** scope — different websites can have different origin addresses (but NOT different per store view)

---

## 3. Shipping Zones & Restrictions

Each shipping method can be restricted to specific **countries** or **regions**, forming a logical "shipping zone."

### Admin Path (per carrier)

```
Stores > Configuration > Sales > Delivery Methods > [Carrier Name]
  > Ship to Applicable Countries
  > Ship to Specific Countries (multi-select)
```

### Options

| Setting | Behaviour |
|---------|-----------|
| All Allowed Countries | Method shows for any country in the allowed-countries list |
| Specific Countries | Only shows for the selected countries |

### Restriction Logic Flow

```
Customer enters shipping address
          |
          v
  Magento checks: Is this carrier active?
          |
          v
  Magento checks: Does destination country match
                  allowed country/region for this method?
          |
      YES |                  NO |
          v                     v
  Rate is calculated       Method hidden from
  and offered              checkout entirely
```

**Exam focus:**
- Country restrictions are *per carrier/method*, not global
- A customer whose country is NOT in the allowed list will simply **not see** that shipping method — no error message
- "Allowed Countries" (General config) is different from "Ship to Specific Countries" (per carrier)

---

## 4. Flat Rate Shipping

The simplest offline carrier — charges a **fixed price** that does not change based on weight, destination, or cart total.

### Admin Path

```
Stores > Configuration > Sales > Delivery Methods > Flat Rate
```

### Key Configuration Fields

| Field | Options / Notes |
|-------|-----------------|
| Enabled | Yes / No |
| Title | Label shown at checkout (e.g., "Standard Shipping") |
| Method Name | Sub-label (e.g., "Fixed") |
| Type | **Per Order** or **Per Item** |
| Price | Dollar amount charged |
| Calculate Handling Fee | Fixed or Percent |
| Handling Fee | Additional fee on top of rate |
| Displayed Error Message | Shown when method is unavailable |
| Ship to Applicable Countries | All / Specific |
| Sort Order | Display priority at checkout |

### Per Order vs Per Item — Critical Difference

```
Cart: 3 items, Flat Rate = $5.00

Per ORDER:
  Shipping = $5.00 (flat, regardless of quantity)

Per ITEM:
  Shipping = 3 x $5.00 = $15.00
```

**Exam focus:**
- **Per Item** multiplies the rate by the total number of items in the cart — not unique products
- The Handling Fee is *added on top* of the calculated rate and can be Fixed or a Percentage
- Flat Rate **ignores** weight, dimensions, and destination entirely
- If two products have different flat rates configured at the product level, Magento uses the **highest** rate in certain configurations — but standard Flat Rate method uses the global config price

---

## 5. Free Shipping Method

A dedicated shipping method that offers **$0.00** shipping, optionally gated behind a minimum order amount.

### Admin Path

```
Stores > Configuration > Sales > Delivery Methods > Free Shipping
```

### Key Configuration Fields

| Field | Options / Notes |
|-------|-----------------|
| Enabled | Yes / No |
| Title | Label (e.g., "Free Shipping") |
| Method Name | Sub-label (e.g., "Free") |
| Minimum Order Amount | Subtotal threshold to unlock free shipping |
| Include Tax to Amount | Whether tax is included when checking threshold |
| Displayed Error Message | Shown when below threshold |
| Ship to Applicable Countries | All / Specific |
| Sort Order | Display priority |

### Minimum Order Amount — CRITICAL BEHAVIOUR

```
Cart subtotal (before discount): $95.00
Coupon discount applied:         -$10.00
Cart subtotal (after discount):  $85.00

Free Shipping minimum set to:    $90.00

RESULT: Free Shipping is NOT available
(Magento checks AFTER discounts are applied)
```

**Exam focus:**
- The minimum order amount is checked **after discounts are applied** — this is a very common exam trap
- This applies to both the **Free Shipping method** minimum AND to cart rules with free shipping action
- The "Include Tax to Amount" setting determines if tax is counted toward the threshold
- Free Shipping method offers free shipping for the **entire order** — all items

---

## 6. Table Rate Shipping

The most powerful offline carrier — allows defining complex rate tables based on combinations of **weight**, **price**, and **destination** using a CSV file.

### Admin Path

```
Stores > Configuration > Sales > Delivery Methods > Table Rates
```

### Condition Options (choose ONE per table)

| Condition | Description |
|-----------|-------------|
| Weight vs. Destination | Rate based on total cart weight + destination |
| Price vs. Destination | Rate based on cart subtotal + destination |
| # of Items vs. Destination | Rate based on item count + destination |

### CSV Format — EXACT COLUMN HEADERS REQUIRED

```csv
Country,Region/State,Zip/Postal Code,Weight (and above),Shipping Price
US,*,*,0,5.00
US,*,*,5,8.00
US,*,*,10,12.00
US,CA,*,0,6.00
US,CA,*,5,9.00
CA,*,*,0,10.00
*,*,*,0,15.00
```

> **Note:** The third column is **Zip/Postal Code** (NOT City). This is defined in `ColumnResolver.php` as `COLUMN_ZIP = 'Zip/Postal Code'`. Using "City" as a header will cause a silent failure with no rates returned.

> **For Price vs. Destination condition:**

```csv
Country,Region/State,Zip/Postal Code,Order Subtotal (and above),Shipping Price
US,*,*,0,8.00
US,*,*,50,5.00
US,*,*,100,0.00
```

### Column Header Reference

| Column | Valid Values | Notes |
|--------|-------------|-------|
| Country | ISO 2-letter code or `*` | `*` = wildcard (any country) |
| Region/State | State code or `*` | `*` = any region |
| Zip/Postal Code | ZIP/postal code or `*` | `*` = any ZIP code |
| Weight/Price/Items (and above) | Numeric | "and above" means >= this value |
| Shipping Price | Numeric (dollars) | The rate charged |

### Wildcard Resolution — Specificity Rules

```
Magento matches rows from MOST specific to LEAST specific:

Most specific:   Country + Region + Zip/Postal Code match
    |
    v
    Country + Region + * (any ZIP)
    |
    v
    Country + * (any region) + * (any ZIP)
    |
    v
Least specific:  * + * + * (catch-all)
```

### Table Rate CSV Import

```
Admin Path:
  Stores > Configuration > Sales > Delivery Methods > Table Rates
    > Export CSV (download current rates)
    > Import CSV (upload new rates)
    > [Save Config to apply]
```

### CRITICAL — Silent Failure Behaviour

```
Common CSV Mistakes That Cause Silent Failure:
+------------------------------------------+----------------------------------+
| Mistake                                  | Symptom                          |
+------------------------------------------+----------------------------------+
| Wrong column header name                 | No products shown / no rates     |
| Extra spaces in headers                  | Silent failure                   |
| BOM character at start of file           | First column not parsed          |
| Wrong condition vs. column headers       | All rows ignored                 |
| Missing wildcard catch-all row           | Some destinations show no rate   |
| Decimal separator wrong (comma vs dot)   | Rates import as $0.00            |
+------------------------------------------+----------------------------------+
```

**Exam focus:**
- Table Rate CSV format is **strict** — wrong headers = silent failure with no rates shown to customer
- Always export the existing CSV as a template before creating a new one
- The condition selected in Admin config **must match** the column headers in the CSV
- Wildcard `*` is used for "any" — not blank
- Table Rates must be **enabled per website** — they are website-scoped in config
- You must **Save Config** after importing the CSV for changes to take effect

---

## 7. Carrier Integrations (UPS / FedEx / USPS / DHL)

Real-time carriers query external APIs to return live shipping rates based on weight, dimensions, origin, and destination.

### Common Requirements for All Real-Time Carriers

```
Prerequisites for Real-Time Carrier Rates:
  1. Valid account credentials (Account Number, API Key, etc.)
  2. Products must have WEIGHT configured
  3. Origin address must be fully configured
  4. Sandbox vs. Production URL correctly set
  5. Store's currency must match carrier account currency
```

### UPS Configuration

**Admin Path:** `Stores > Configuration > Sales > Delivery Methods > UPS`

| Setting | Description |
|---------|-------------|
| Enabled for Checkout | Show rates to customers |
| UPS Type | UPS XML (legacy) or REST API |
| Gateway URL | Production or sandbox endpoint |
| Access License Number | API access key |
| User ID (Username) | API username |
| Password | API password |
| Shipper Number | 6-character UPS account number (required for negotiated rates) |
| Allowed Methods | Check/uncheck individual service levels (Ground, 2-Day Air, etc.) |
| Free Method | Which UPS method becomes free when free shipping is triggered |
| Free Shipping Amount Threshold | Minimum to trigger free UPS method |
| Destination Type | Residential or Commercial (affects pricing) |
| Negotiated Rates | Use account-specific negotiated rates (requires account agreement) |

**Exam focus:**
- UPS requires **Access License Number**, **User ID**, **Password**, and **Shipper Number** (for negotiated rates)
- Negotiated Rates must be enabled in *both* UPS account settings AND Magento config
- Setting Destination Type to **Residential** typically costs more than Commercial

### FedEx Configuration

**Admin Path:** `Stores > Configuration > Sales > Delivery Methods > FedEx`

| Setting | Description |
|---------|-------------|
| Account ID | FedEx account number |
| Meter Number | Unique identifier for rate requests |
| Key | API authentication key |
| Password | API password |
| Sandbox Mode | Yes/No — test vs. live |
| Allowed Methods | FedEx Ground, Express, Overnight, etc. |
| Hub ID | Required for SmartPost |
| Free Method | Method to make free when threshold met |
| Smart Post Hub ID | SmartPost specific |
| Packaging | Default box type |
| Dropoff | Regular pickup, drop box, etc. |

**Exam focus:**
- FedEx requires **4 credentials**: Account ID, Meter Number, Key, Password
- FedEx Sandbox mode exists natively in Admin — useful for testing without real charges

### USPS Configuration

**Admin Path:** `Stores > Configuration > Sales > Delivery Methods > USPS`

| Setting | Description |
|---------|-------------|
| Gateway URL | USPS Web Tools URL |
| Secure Gateway URL | HTTPS endpoint |
| Username | USPS Web Tools User ID |
| Password | USPS Web Tools password |
| Allowed Methods | Priority Mail, First Class, Media Mail, etc. |
| Free Method | Method to make free |
| Size | Regular or Large |
| Container | Package type |
| Machinable | Affects letter-rate eligibility |

**Exam focus:**
- USPS uses **Username** (User ID) from the USPS Web Tools registration
- USPS is US-origin only for domestic rates; international rates are a separate API endpoint
- USPS does not support **negotiated rates** the way UPS/FedEx do

### DHL Configuration

**Admin Path:** `Stores > Configuration > Sales > Delivery Methods > DHL`

| Setting | Description |
|---------|-------------|
| Gateway URL | DHL XML API endpoint |
| Access ID | DHL account identifier |
| Password | API password |
| Account Number | DHL account number |
| Content Type | Documents or Non-Documents |
| Handling Fee | Additional fee |
| Allowed Methods | Express Worldwide, etc. |

**Exam focus:**
- DHL in Magento core is primarily configured for **international** shipments
- DHL Express and DHL eCommerce are different products requiring different integrations

### Real-Time Carrier Fallback

```
If API call fails or returns no rates:

Option 1: Show error message to customer
Option 2: Show a fallback rate (configured as "Specific Error Message")

Config setting: "Displayed Error Message" per carrier
```

---

## 8. In-Store Delivery / Store Pickup

Allows customers to pick up orders at a physical location instead of having them shipped.

### Magento Open Source vs Commerce

| Feature | Open Source | Commerce (EE) |
|---------|-------------|---------------|
| Basic In-Store Delivery method | Yes | Yes |
| Multi-source Inventory (MSI) Store Pickup | Yes (all MSI pickup modules have OSL license) | Yes |
| Source-based pickup locations | Yes | Yes |

> **Note:** All `module-inventory-in-store-pickup-*` modules have OSL-3.0 license, meaning the full MSI store pickup experience is available in Open Source.

### Admin Path (Basic)

```
Stores > Configuration > Sales > Delivery Methods > In-Store Delivery
```

| Setting | Description |
|---------|-------------|
| Enabled | Yes / No |
| Method Name | Label at checkout (e.g., "Store Pickup") |
| Price | Cost (usually $0.00) |
| Search Radius | Radius for store search (MSI) |
| Displayed Error Message | When unavailable |

### MSI Store Pickup (Commerce)

```
Sources (physical locations) are configured with:
  - Latitude / Longitude
  - Pickup contact info
  - Is Pickup Location: Yes/No

Customer flow at checkout:
  1. Select "In-Store Pickup"
  2. Search for nearby store by ZIP or city
  3. Select store
  4. Order is assigned to that Source
```

**Exam focus:**
- In-Store Delivery with MSI store pickup (including location search) is available in **both Open Source and Commerce** — all related modules have OSL license
- Store Pickup orders still go through order management (not instant pickup)

---

## 9. Multi-Address Checkout

Allows a single order to ship **different items** to **different addresses**. Despite common misconceptions, this feature is available in **Magento Open Source** — `module-multishipping` has OSL-3.0 license.

### How It Works

```
Standard Checkout (Open Source + Commerce):
  Cart -> ONE shipping address -> ONE shipment

Multi-Address Checkout (Open Source + Commerce):
  Cart -> MULTIPLE shipping addresses -> MULTIPLE shipments
          |                               |
          Item A -> Address 1             Shipment 1
          Item B -> Address 2             Shipment 2
          Item C -> Address 1             (merged with Shipment 1)
```

### Customer Flow

```
1. Cart page: click "Check Out with Multiple Addresses"
2. Assign each cart item to a shipping address
3. Add new addresses or select from address book
4. Each address gets its own shipping method selection
5. Each address gets its own shipping rate calculation
6. Single payment for the entire order
7. Single order number, but multiple shipments
```

### Admin Considerations

```
Multi-Address Order in Admin:
  - One Order record
  - Multiple Shipping Addresses visible in order detail
  - Multiple Shipments can be created
  - Each shipment has its own tracking
```

**Exam focus:**
- Multi-address checkout is available in **both Open Source and Commerce** (`module-multishipping` has OSL-3.0 license)
- Each address in a multi-address order gets its own **independent shipping method** selection
- It creates a **single order** with multiple shipping addresses — not multiple separate orders
- Real-time carrier rates are calculated **per destination address**, not per entire order

---

## 10. Free Shipping — Cart Rule vs Method Trigger

This is the **most commonly confused topic** in Magento shipping. There are TWO different mechanisms for offering free shipping.

### Mechanism 1: Free Shipping *Method* (Delivery Methods Config)

```
Location: Stores > Configuration > Sales > Delivery Methods > Free Shipping

How it works:
  - Dedicated "Free Shipping" shipping method appears at checkout
  - Appears ONLY when cart subtotal >= Minimum Order Amount
  - Applies to the ENTIRE ORDER regardless of which products are in cart
  - Minimum checked AFTER discounts applied

Customer sees:
  [ ] Flat Rate - $5.00
  [X] Free Shipping - $0.00   <-- appears when threshold met
```

### Mechanism 2: Free Shipping via *Cart Price Rule*

```
Location: Marketing > Promotions > Cart Price Rules
  > Actions tab > Apply Shipping Amount = "Free Shipping"

Sub-options:
  a) "For matching items only"   <- free shipping on specific items
  b) "For shipment with matching items" <- entire shipment free

How it works:
  - A coupon or automatic rule triggers free shipping
  - Can be product-specific (via conditions)
  - Can be triggered by coupon code, customer segment, date range, etc.
  - Can make a SPECIFIC CARRIER'S method free (e.g., UPS Ground becomes $0)
```

### Side-by-Side Comparison

```
+------------------------+-----------------------------+----------------------------+
| Aspect                 | Free Shipping METHOD        | Cart Rule Free Shipping    |
+------------------------+-----------------------------+----------------------------+
| Config location        | Delivery Methods config     | Cart Price Rules           |
| Trigger                | Minimum order amount        | Rule conditions (flexible) |
| Scope                  | Entire order always         | Specific items or order    |
| Coupon code needed?    | No (automatic)              | Optional                   |
| Discount check timing  | After discounts             | After discounts            |
| Carrier interaction    | Own method shown            | Can set existing method    |
|                        |                             | (e.g., UPS Ground) to $0   |
| Customer segment?      | No                          | Yes (Commerce)             |
+------------------------+-----------------------------+----------------------------+
```

### Cart Rule — Making a Specific Carrier Method Free

```
Example: Make UPS Ground free for orders over $50

Cart Price Rule:
  Conditions: Subtotal >= 50
  Actions:
    Apply Shipping Amount: For shipment with matching items

Each carrier config also has:
  "Free Method" setting (e.g., "UPS Ground")
  "Free Shipping Amount Threshold" (alternative trigger)

When cart rule fires -> Magento sets UPS Ground price to $0.00
Customer still selects UPS Ground, but pays nothing
```

**Exam focus:**
- Free Shipping minimum is checked **after discounts** — a $100 order with $20 coupon = $80 effective, may not meet $90 threshold
- Cart Rule "For matching items only" = only those items' shipping is free; other items still have shipping costs
- Cart Rule "For shipment with matching items" = the entire shipment containing those items is free
- A Cart Rule does NOT create a new "Free Shipping" method — it sets an existing method's price to $0
- Both mechanisms check post-discount amounts

### Free Shipping Decision Tree

```
Customer adds items to cart
          |
          v
  Is there an active Cart Price Rule
  with free shipping action that matches?
    YES -> relevant method(s) become $0
    NO  -> check next
          |
          v
  Is Free Shipping METHOD enabled?
    NO  -> no free shipping offered
    YES -> Is cart subtotal (after discounts) >= minimum?
              YES -> Free Shipping method shown at $0
              NO  -> Free Shipping method hidden
```

---

## 11. Hands-On Configuration Lab

### Lab Goal

Configure **Flat Rate** and **Free Shipping** with a minimum order threshold. Test behaviour with a cart below and above the threshold.

---

### Step 1 — Set Origin Address

```
Admin: Stores > Configuration > Sales > Shipping Settings > Origin

Set:
  Country: United States
  Region/State: California
  ZIP: 90210
  City: Beverly Hills
  Street: 123 Magento Way

Save Config
```

---

### Step 2 — Configure Flat Rate

```
Admin: Stores > Configuration > Sales > Delivery Methods > Flat Rate

Settings:
  Enabled:           Yes
  Title:             Standard Shipping
  Method Name:       Fixed Rate
  Type:              Per Order
  Price:             7.99
  Handling Fee Type: Fixed
  Handling Fee:      0.00
  Ship to Countries: All Allowed Countries
  Sort Order:        10

Save Config
```

---

### Step 3 — Configure Free Shipping with Minimum

```
Admin: Stores > Configuration > Sales > Delivery Methods > Free Shipping

Settings:
  Enabled:               Yes
  Title:                 Free Shipping
  Method Name:           Free
  Minimum Order Amount:  50.00
  Include Tax:           No
  Ship to Countries:     All Allowed Countries
  Sort Order:            20

Save Config
```

---

### Step 4 — Flush Cache

```bash
bin/magento cache:flush
bin/magento cache:clean config
```

---

### Step 5 — Test Below Threshold

```
Scenario: Cart subtotal = $35.00 (below $50 threshold)

Expected checkout shipping options:
  [X] Standard Shipping - Fixed Rate    $7.99
  [ ] Free Shipping method              (NOT shown)

Verify:
  - Navigate to storefront
  - Add product(s) totaling < $50.00
  - Proceed to checkout
  - Enter shipping address (US address)
  - Observe: Only "Standard Shipping" visible
```

---

### Step 6 — Test At/Above Threshold

```
Scenario: Cart subtotal = $55.00 (above $50 threshold)

Expected checkout shipping options:
  [ ] Standard Shipping - Fixed Rate    $7.99
  [X] Free Shipping                     $0.00

Verify:
  - Modify cart to total >= $50.00
  - Proceed to checkout
  - Observe: BOTH methods shown
  - Free Shipping is selectable
```

---

### Step 7 — Test Discount Interaction (Tricky)

```
Scenario:
  Cart subtotal (before discount): $55.00
  Apply coupon for $10 off
  Cart subtotal (after discount):  $45.00
  Free Shipping minimum:           $50.00

Expected result:
  - Free Shipping method: NOT shown (below threshold after discount)
  - Standard Shipping: shown at $7.99

This confirms: minimum is checked AFTER discounts
```

---

### Step 8 — Test Per-Item Flat Rate

```
Optional: Change Flat Rate "Type" from "Per Order" to "Per Item"

Cart: 4 items x Flat Rate $7.99

Expected:
  Shipping = 4 x $7.99 = $31.96

Observe at checkout how total shipping changes
```

---

### Verification Checklist for Lab

```
[ ] Origin address saved (country, state, ZIP)
[ ] Flat Rate enabled with correct price
[ ] Flat Rate type: Per Order vs Per Item — tested both
[ ] Free Shipping enabled with $50.00 minimum
[ ] Cache flushed after config changes
[ ] Tested cart below $50: only Flat Rate shown
[ ] Tested cart above $50: both methods shown
[ ] Tested cart above $50 with discount below $50: only Flat Rate shown
[ ] Verified tax inclusion/exclusion in threshold calculation
```

---

## 12. Common Pitfalls & Tricky Exam Scenarios

### Pitfall 1 — Table Rate Silent Failure

```
Problem: Import CSV, Save Config, but no shipping rates appear at checkout

Root causes (in order of likelihood):
  1. Column headers don't match selected condition
     - Using "Weight (and above)" header but condition set to "Price vs. Destination"

  2. BOM character in CSV file
     - Causes first header to be unreadable
     - Fix: Save CSV as UTF-8 WITHOUT BOM

  3. Wildcard not used — blank cells instead of *
     - Blank cells are NOT treated as wildcards
     - Must use literal asterisk: *

  4. Condition mismatch
     - Import CSV for "Weight" then switch condition to "# of Items"
     - Previous import is gone; need to re-import for new condition

  5. Config not saved after import
     - Import button uploads file but Save Config is still required
```

### Pitfall 2 — Free Shipping Threshold Timing

```
WRONG assumption: "My order is $60, threshold is $50, free shipping available"

CORRECT: 
  $60 (subtotal) - $15 (coupon code) = $45 effective
  $45 < $50 threshold
  Free shipping NOT available

Exam question style: "A customer has a $65 cart and applies a $20 coupon.
The Free Shipping minimum is $50. What shipping options are shown?"

Answer: Only Flat Rate (or other paid methods) — Free Shipping is hidden
because $65 - $20 = $45, which is below the $50 minimum.
```

### Pitfall 3 — Cart Rule vs Method Free Shipping Scope

```
Scenario: Cart Price Rule with "For matching items only" is active.
Cart contains:
  - Product A (matches rule condition)
  - Product B (does not match rule condition)

Result:
  - Product A's shipping portion is free
  - Product B's shipping portion is still charged
  - Customer may still see a shipping cost at checkout

vs.

"For shipment with matching items":
  - If ANY item in the shipment matches, ENTIRE shipment is free
```

### Pitfall 4 — Multi-Address Checkout Availability

```
Common misconception: "Multi-address checkout is Commerce (EE) only"

Correction: Multi-address checkout is available in BOTH Open Source and Commerce.
The module-multishipping module has OSL-3.0 license.
Configuration: Stores > Configuration > Sales > Multishipping Settings
```

### Pitfall 5 — Real-Time Carrier with Missing Product Weight

```
Problem: UPS/FedEx/USPS show "no rates available" for some products

Root cause: Products are missing weight attribute value

Fix:
  Catalog > Products > [Edit Product]
  Weight tab > enter weight in configured unit (lbs or kgs)

Note: The weight unit is set in:
  Stores > Configuration > General > Locale Options > Weight Unit
```

### Pitfall 6 — Table Rate Per Website Scope

```
Table Rate config is website-scoped (not global).
Different websites can have completely different rate tables.

Admin tip: When in global scope, Table Rate import won't work correctly.
Must switch to website scope to import Table Rates.
```

### Pitfall 7 — Shipping Method Enabled vs Visible

```
A method can be:
  - Enabled = Yes
  - But still not visible at checkout if:
    a) Customer's country is not in allowed countries
    b) No rates returned (API failure for online carriers)
    c) Minimum order amount not met (Free Shipping)
    d) Cart has no items requiring shipping (virtual products)
```

### Pitfall 8 — Virtual Products and Shipping

```
Virtual products (downloadable, services) do NOT require shipping.
If a cart contains ONLY virtual products:
  - Shipping step is SKIPPED entirely at checkout
  - No shipping methods are displayed
  - Shipping address may not be required (configurable)
```

---

## Quick-Reference Checklist

### Shipping Methods Overview
- [ ] **Flat Rate** — fixed price per order OR per item; ignores weight/destination
- [ ] **Free Shipping** — $0 method; optionally requires minimum order amount
- [ ] **Table Rate** — CSV-based; conditions: Weight vs. Destination, Price vs. Destination, # Items vs. Destination
- [ ] **UPS / FedEx / USPS / DHL** — real-time API rates; require account credentials + product weights
- [ ] **In-Store Pickup** — basic in Open Source; full MSI location picker in Commerce

### Origin Address
- [ ] Set at `Stores > Configuration > Sales > Shipping Settings > Origin`
- [ ] **Default + Website scope** (showInDefault=1, showInWebsite=1) — different websites can have different origins
- [ ] Missing/incorrect origin ZIP causes real-time carriers to return no rates

### Shipping Zones
- [ ] Configured per carrier: "Ship to Applicable Countries" / "Ship to Specific Countries"
- [ ] Countries NOT in allowed list = method is **hidden** from checkout (no error)

### Flat Rate — Key Facts
- [ ] **Per Order** = single fixed rate regardless of items
- [ ] **Per Item** = rate × number of items in cart
- [ ] Handling fee is additive (Fixed or Percent)
- [ ] Never contacts external APIs

### Free Shipping — Key Facts
- [ ] Minimum order amount checked **after discounts** are applied
- [ ] Entire order ships free (not per-item)
- [ ] "Include Tax to Amount" setting affects threshold calculation

### Table Rate — Key Facts
- [ ] CSV format is **strict** — incorrect headers cause **silent failure** (no rates shown)
- [ ] Always **export existing CSV** as template before editing
- [ ] Wildcard = `*` (asterisk), NOT blank
- [ ] Condition in Admin config **must match** CSV column headers
- [ ] Must **Save Config** after CSV import
- [ ] Table Rate is **website-scoped**
- [ ] Import must be done in **website scope**, not global scope

### Real-Time Carriers — Key Facts
- [ ] All require **account credentials** (specific fields differ per carrier)
- [ ] All require **product weight** to be set on each product
- [ ] UPS: Access License Number + User ID + Password + Shipper Number (for negotiated rates)
- [ ] FedEx: Account ID + Meter Number + Key + Password (4 credentials)
- [ ] USPS: Username (Web Tools User ID) only
- [ ] DHL: Access ID + Password + Account Number
- [ ] FedEx has native **Sandbox Mode** toggle
- [ ] Negotiated Rates (UPS): must be enabled in both UPS account and Magento
- [ ] UPS Destination Type: Residential costs more than Commercial

### Free Shipping — Cart Rule vs Method
- [ ] **Free Shipping Method**: configured in Delivery Methods; shows as separate option; triggers on minimum order amount
- [ ] **Cart Rule Free Shipping**: Marketing > Cart Price Rules; flexible conditions; coupon optional
- [ ] Cart Rule scope: "For matching items only" (partial) vs "For shipment with matching items" (entire shipment)
- [ ] Cart Rule does NOT create a new shipping method — it sets existing method to $0
- [ ] Both check thresholds **after discounts**

### Multi-Address Checkout
- [ ] Available in **both Open Source and Commerce** (`module-multishipping` has OSL license)
- [ ] Single order number, multiple shipping addresses, multiple shipments
- [ ] Each address gets independent shipping method selection
- [ ] Rates calculated per destination address

### Common Exam Traps
- [ ] Free Shipping minimum is checked **AFTER** discounts — $60 cart with $15 coupon = $45 effective
- [ ] Table Rate wrong CSV headers = silent failure, no products/rates shown
- [ ] Multi-address checkout = available in Open Source (NOT EE-only)
- [ ] Virtual-product-only carts skip the shipping step entirely
- [ ] Missing product weight = real-time carriers return no rates
- [ ] Table Rate import at global scope = won't apply correctly; use website scope
- [ ] Blank cell in Table Rate CSV ≠ wildcard; must use `*`
- [ ] "Ship to Specific Countries" hides method — doesn't show error

### Admin Config Quick Paths
- [ ] All shipping methods: `Stores > Configuration > Sales > Delivery Methods`
- [ ] Origin address: `Stores > Configuration > Sales > Shipping Settings > Origin`
- [ ] Cart Price Rules: `Marketing > Promotions > Cart Price Rules`
- [ ] In-Store Delivery: `Stores > Configuration > Sales > Delivery Methods > In-Store Delivery`
- [ ] Multi-address checkout settings: `Stores > Configuration > Sales > Multishipping Settings`

flashcards.question: What are the two broad categories of shipping methods in Magento 2, and how do they differ in rate calculation?
flashcards.answer: Offline carriers (Flat Rate, Free Shipping, Table Rate, In-Store Pickup) calculate rates locally with no external API calls and require no account credentials. Online/real-time carriers (UPS, FedEx, USPS, DHL) call external APIs to return live rates based on weight, dimensions, origin, and destination, requiring valid account credentials.
flashcards.hint: Think about whether the carrier needs to 'phone home' to get a price.

flashcards.question: At what scope is the origin (shipping) address configurable in Magento 2, and what happens if the origin ZIP is missing?
flashcards.answer: The origin address is configurable at Default and Website scope (showInDefault=1, showInWebsite=1, but NOT showInStore). If the origin ZIP is missing or incorrect, real-time carriers (UPS, FedEx, USPS, DHL) may return no rates at all.
flashcards.hint: Different websites can have different warehouses, but store views within a website share the same origin.

flashcards.question: What is the critical difference between Flat Rate 'Per Order' and 'Per Item' types?
flashcards.answer: Per Order charges a single fixed rate regardless of how many items are in the cart. Per Item multiplies the configured rate by the total number of items in the cart (not unique products). For example, 3 items at $5.00 Flat Rate: Per Order = $5.00, Per Item = $15.00.
flashcards.hint: Per Item counts quantity, not distinct SKUs.

flashcards.question: When is the Free Shipping minimum order amount checked — before or after discounts are applied?
flashcards.answer: The minimum order amount is checked AFTER discounts are applied. A $60 cart with a $15 coupon has an effective subtotal of $45. If the Free Shipping minimum is $50, Free Shipping will NOT be available because $45 < $50.
flashcards.hint: This is one of the most common exam traps — the coupon reduces the effective subtotal before the threshold check.

flashcards.question: What are the three condition options for Table Rate shipping, and what happens if the CSV column headers don't match the selected condition?
flashcards.answer: The three conditions are: Weight vs. Destination, Price vs. Destination, and # of Items vs. Destination. If the CSV column headers don't match the selected condition in Admin, a silent failure occurs — no rates are shown to the customer, with no error message displayed.
flashcards.hint: The word 'silent' is key — Magento doesn't tell you the CSV is wrong.

flashcards.question: In Table Rate CSV files, what must be used to represent 'any value' for Country, Region, or ZIP — and what is NOT acceptable?
flashcards.answer: The asterisk wildcard (*) must be used to represent 'any value.' Blank/empty cells are NOT treated as wildcards and will cause the row to be ignored, resulting in no rates for those destinations.
flashcards.hint: A star means 'match everything'; leaving it empty means 'match nothing.'

flashcards.question: What are the two different mechanisms for offering free shipping in Magento, and how do they differ in scope?
flashcards.answer: 1) Free Shipping Method (Delivery Methods config) — a dedicated $0 shipping method that appears when cart subtotal meets a minimum, applying to the entire order. 2) Cart Price Rule with free shipping action — uses flexible rule conditions (coupons, segments, product matching) and can set an existing carrier's method to $0. A Cart Rule does NOT create a new shipping method — it modifies an existing one.
flashcards.hint: One is a standalone method; the other piggybacks on existing carriers.

flashcards.question: What is the difference between Cart Price Rule free shipping scopes: 'For matching items only' vs 'For shipment with matching items'?
flashcards.answer: 'For matching items only' makes only the matching items' shipping free — other items in the cart still incur shipping costs. 'For shipment with matching items' makes the entire shipment free if ANY item in it matches the rule conditions.
flashcards.hint: One is partial (just those items), the other is all-or-nothing for the whole shipment.

flashcards.question: Is Multi-Address Checkout available in Magento Open Source, and how does it create orders?
flashcards.answer: Yes, Multi-Address Checkout is available in BOTH Open Source and Commerce — the module-multishipping has OSL-3.0 license. It creates a single order with multiple shipping addresses and multiple shipments, not multiple separate orders. Each address gets its own independent shipping method selection.
flashcards.hint: Common misconception — it's NOT EE-only. One order, many addresses.

flashcards.question: What four credentials does FedEx require for integration, and does FedEx have a native Sandbox Mode toggle in Magento?
flashcards.answer: FedEx requires four credentials: Account ID, Meter Number, Key, and Password. Yes, FedEx has a native Sandbox Mode toggle in the Admin configuration, allowing testing without real charges.
flashcards.hint: FedEx needs four keys to the door, and yes, there's a built-in test mode.

flashcards.question: At what scope is Table Rate configuration managed, and what must you do after importing a CSV?
flashcards.answer: Table Rate configuration is website-scoped. Different websites can have completely different rate tables. After importing a CSV, you must Save Config for the changes to take effect. Also, the import must be done at website scope, not global scope.
flashcards.hint: Website-level, not global. And don't forget to click Save!

flashcards.question: What happens to the shipping step at checkout if a cart contains ONLY virtual products?
flashcards.answer: If a cart contains only virtual products (downloadable, services), the shipping step is SKIPPED entirely at checkout. No shipping methods are displayed, and a shipping address may not be required.
flashcards.hint: No physical goods = nothing to ship = no shipping step.

flashcards.question: Why might UPS or FedEx show 'no rates available' for certain products, even though the carrier is properly configured?
flashcards.answer: Products are missing the weight attribute value. All real-time carriers require products to have weight configured. Without weight, the carrier API cannot calculate rates and returns no results.
flashcards.hint: No weight on the product = the carrier can't calculate how much to charge for shipping.

flashcards.question: What happens when a customer's billing country is NOT in the 'Ship to Specific Countries' list for a shipping method?
flashcards.answer: The shipping method is simply hidden from checkout — no error message is displayed. The customer will not see the method as an option at all.
flashcards.hint: It vanishes silently — no error, just gone.

flashcards.question: How does UPS Destination Type (Residential vs Commercial) affect shipping pricing?
flashcards.answer: Setting the UPS Destination Type to Residential typically results in higher shipping costs compared to Commercial. Negotiated Rates must be enabled in both the UPS account settings AND Magento configuration to work.
flashcards.hint: Home delivery costs more than shipping to a business.

studyNotes.title: Day 9 — Payment Methods & Processing
studyNotes.content:
# Magento 2 / Adobe Commerce: Payment Methods & Processing
## Study Notes — Week 2, Core Features

---

## Table of Contents

1. [Overview of Payment Method Categories](#1-overview-of-payment-method-categories)
2. [Offline Payment Methods](#2-offline-payment-methods)
3. [Online Payment Methods](#3-online-payment-methods)
4. [Payment Action: Authorize Only vs Authorize and Capture](#4-payment-action-authorize-only-vs-authorize-and-capture)
5. [Zero Subtotal Checkout](#5-zero-subtotal-checkout)
6. [Purchase Order (PO) Payments](#6-purchase-order-po-payments)
7. [Payment Restrictions](#7-payment-restrictions)
8. [PCI DSS Compliance & Security](#8-pci-dss-compliance--security)
9. [3D Secure (3DS2)](#9-3d-secure-3ds2)
10. [Braintree Deep Dive](#10-braintree-deep-dive)
11. [PayPal Methods Comparison](#11-paypal-methods-comparison)
12. [Payment Flow Diagrams](#12-payment-flow-diagrams)
13. [Admin Configuration Reference](#13-admin-configuration-reference)
14. [Hands-On: Sandbox Testing Checklist](#14-hands-on-sandbox-testing-checklist)
15. [Quick-Reference Checklist](#quick-reference-checklist)

---

## 1. Overview of Payment Method Categories

Magento 2 / Adobe Commerce organizes payment methods into two broad categories:

| Category | Processing | Gateway Required | Invoice Auto-Created |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Offline** | Manual / deferred | No | No (manual) |
| **Online** | Real-time via gateway | Yes | Depends on Payment Action |

```
+-----------------------------+
|   Payment Methods           |
+-----------------------------+
        |           |
   OFFLINE       ONLINE
        |           |
  Check/MO    PayPal Express
  Bank Wire   PayPal Standard
  COD         Braintree
  PO          Zero Subtotal*
```

> *Zero Subtotal Checkout is technically a special offline method triggered by a $0 order total.

- **Exam focus:** Know which methods are offline vs. online and whether they require a payment gateway.

---

## 2. Offline Payment Methods

Offline methods collect payment information (or promises of payment) **outside** the Magento platform. The system records the intent but does **not** contact a processor.

### 2.1 Check / Money Order

- Customer mails a physical check or money order.
- Order is placed in **Pending** status until the merchant manually changes it. *(The `order_status` source model is `NewStatus`, which provides statuses for the `new` state — default is "Pending", not "Pending Payment".)*
- Admin must verify receipt before fulfilling the order.

**Configuration path:**
```
Stores > Configuration > Sales > Payment Methods > Check / Money Order
```

Key fields:

| Field | Description |
|---|---|
| Enabled | Yes / No |
| Title | Displayed to the customer at checkout |
| New Order Status | Default: Pending |
| Payment from Applicable Countries | All / Specific |
| Minimum / Maximum Order Total | Optional amount gates |
| Make Check Payable To | Text printed on checkout |
| Send Check To | Mailing address shown to customer |

- **Exam focus:** The "Make Check Payable To" and "Send Check To" fields appear on the checkout confirmation page and in the order confirmation email.

---

### 2.2 Bank Transfer / Wire Transfer

- Customer initiates a bank wire to the merchant's account.
- Magento only records the intent; the actual payment happens **outside the system**.
- Admin verifies the incoming wire and manually processes the order.

**Configuration path:**
```
Stores > Configuration > Sales > Payment Methods > Bank Transfer Payment
```

- **Exam focus:** Like Check/MO, this method has **no automatic status transition**. The merchant must manually change the order status upon receiving funds.

---

### 2.3 Cash on Delivery (COD)

- Customer pays the delivery driver in cash upon receiving the order.
- Applicable only when a delivery method that supports COD is used.
- Can be restricted to specific countries.

**Configuration path:**
```
Stores > Configuration > Sales > Payment Methods > Cash On Delivery Payment
```

- **Exam focus:** COD is the only offline method where payment occurs **after shipment**, not before. The order can move to processing/shipped status before payment is confirmed.

---

### 2.4 Offline Methods — Common Characteristics

```
Customer Places Order
        |
        v
  [Order Status: Pending]
        |
        v
  Merchant Receives Payment (offline)
        |
        v
  Merchant Updates Order in Admin
        |
        v
  [Invoice Created Manually]
        |
        v
  [Order Fulfillment Begins]
```

- No gateway communication occurs.
- No automatic invoice creation.
- Order status management is **entirely manual**.
- **Exam focus:** For all offline methods, the merchant creates the invoice **manually** — this is also what happens with online Authorize Only orders (manual capture via invoice).

---

## 3. Online Payment Methods

### 3.1 PayPal Express Checkout

- Redirects the customer to PayPal to log in and confirm payment.
- Returns to Magento after authorization.
- Supports both **Authorize Only** and **Authorize and Capture** payment actions.
- Works as a **shortcut button** on the product page, mini cart, and cart — not only at checkout.

**Configuration path:**
```
Stores > Configuration > Sales > Payment Methods > PayPal Express Checkout
```

Key features:

| Feature | Detail |
|---|---|
| Shortcut buttons | Product page, cart, mini-cart |
| Guest checkout | Supported |
| In-context checkout | Overlay (no full redirect) option |
| Billing agreements | Recurring payments via PayPal |

- **Exam focus:** PayPal Express can be placed as a shortcut **before** the customer goes through normal checkout steps. This is a unique UX feature not shared by PayPal Payments Standard.

---

### 3.2 PayPal Payments Standard

- Customer is **fully redirected** to PayPal's hosted page to complete payment.
- Returns to Magento on completion.
- Simpler integration, but less seamless UX (full redirect vs. in-context).
- No shortcut buttons.

**Configuration path:**
```
Stores > Configuration > Sales > Payment Methods > PayPal Payments Standard
```

- **Exam focus:** PayPal Payments Standard always **fully redirects** the customer off-site. PayPal Express Checkout can use **in-context** checkout (modal overlay) keeping the customer on the merchant site.

---

### 3.3 Braintree

Covered in depth in [Section 10](#10-braintree-deep-dive).

---

## 4. Payment Action: Authorize Only vs Authorize and Capture

This is one of the most **exam-critical** topics in payment processing.

### 4.1 Authorize Only

```
Customer Checkout
        |
        v
  Gateway Contacts Bank
        |
        v
  Bank Reserves Funds (Hold)
  [No money moved yet]
        |
        v
  Order Status: Processing
  [NO invoice auto-created]
        |
        v
  Merchant Creates Invoice Manually
        |
        v
  Invoice Creation --> Triggers CAPTURE
        |
        v
  Funds Actually Transfer to Merchant
```

**Key facts:**
- Creates a **reservation** (authorization hold) at the customer's bank.
- **Does NOT move money.**
- **Does NOT automatically create an invoice.**
- Invoice must be created manually in Admin → this triggers the actual capture.
- Authorization holds typically expire in **7–30 days** depending on the card network/bank.

**Admin path to capture:**
```
Admin > Sales > Orders > [Order] > Invoice > Submit Invoice
```

- **Exam focus (critical):** Authorize Only does **NOT** create an invoice automatically. The manual invoice creation is what **triggers the capture** and moves funds. This distinction is extremely common on exams.

---

### 4.2 Authorize and Capture

```
Customer Checkout
        |
        v
  Gateway Contacts Bank
        |
        v
  Funds Immediately Captured
  [Money moves now]
        |
        v
  Invoice Auto-Created
        |
        v
  Order Status: Processing
```

**Key facts:**
- Single transaction: authorizes and captures in one step.
- Invoice is **automatically created** at order placement.
- No manual step required to collect payment.
- Appropriate when goods ship immediately or are digital.

---

### 4.3 Side-by-Side Comparison

| Aspect | Authorize Only | Authorize and Capture |
|---|---|---|
| Funds moved immediately? | **No** | **Yes** |
| Invoice auto-created? | **No** | **Yes** |
| Manual capture step? | **Yes** (via Invoice) | **No** |
| Bank hold created? | **Yes** | **Yes** (then immediately captured) |
| Good for... | Pre-orders, physical goods, B2B | Digital goods, immediate fulfillment |
| Risk | Auth may expire before capture | Immediate charge even if stock unavailable |

- **Exam focus:** Know both the workflow steps AND the business use cases for each payment action.

---

### 4.4 Partial Capture / Partial Invoice

With Authorize Only, you can create **multiple partial invoices** against a single authorization (if the gateway supports it):

```php
// Conceptual: Magento captures amount specified in invoice
// The invoice amount can be less than the full order total
// Multiple invoices can be created until the full amount is captured
```

- **Exam focus:** Partial invoices are only possible with Authorize Only. Once Authorize and Capture fires, the full amount is charged.

## 5. Zero Subtotal Checkout

### What It Is

When an order total reaches **exactly $0.00** — due to 100% discount coupons, store credit, gift cards, or reward points — the Zero Subtotal Checkout method is used.

### Configuration

```
Stores > Configuration > Sales > Payment Methods > Zero Subtotal Checkout
```

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Enabled | Yes |
| Title | "No Payment Information Required" (customizable) |
| New Order Status | Pending / Processing (configurable) |
| Automatically Invoice All Items | Yes / No |

### Workflow

```
Cart Total = $0.00
(100% coupon, gift card, store credit, etc.)
        |
        v
Zero Subtotal Checkout method shown
        |
        v
  If "Automatically Invoice" = Yes:
     Invoice created automatically
  If "Automatically Invoice" = No:
     Invoice created manually
        |
        v
  Order fulfillment proceeds
```

- **Exam focus:** Zero Subtotal Checkout is triggered **only** when the order total is exactly zero. If there's even $0.01 remaining, a normal payment method is required. The "Automatically Invoice All Items" setting controls whether an invoice fires immediately.

## 6. Purchase Order (PO) Payments

### What It Is

Purchase Order payment is a **B2B deferred payment method**. The customer submits a PO number as a promise to pay later (typically via invoice/net terms).

### How It Works

```
B2B Customer Places Order
        |
        v
  Enters PO Number at Checkout
  (e.g., "PO-2024-00123")
        |
        v
  Order Created, No Payment Gateway Contact
        |
        v
  Merchant Fulfills Order
        |
        v
  Merchant Issues Invoice
        |
        v
  Customer Pays Within Net Terms (Net 30, etc.)
```

### Configuration

```
Stores > Configuration > Sales > Payment Methods > Purchase Order
```

| Field | Description |
|---|---|
| Enabled | Yes / No |
| Title | "Purchase Order" |
| New Order Status | Pending |
| Payment from Countries | Restrict if needed |
| Min/Max Order Total | Useful for high-value B2B minimums |

### Key Characteristics

- No gateway; no automatic payment.
- PO number is **stored in the order** and visible in Admin.
- Typically used in conjunction with Adobe Commerce B2B module (company accounts, credit limits).
- **Exam focus:** PO is the standard method for **B2B deferred/net-terms payments**. It is an offline method that relies on trust/business relationships. In B2B module context, credit limits can auto-approve or block PO orders.

## 7. Payment Restrictions

### 7.1 Payment Method by Country

All payment methods have a **"Payment from Applicable Countries"** setting:

```
All Allowed Countries    -- Method available everywhere
Specific Countries       -- Shows a multi-select of countries
```

**Configuration field:**
```
Payment from Applicable Countries: [Specific Countries]
Payment from Specific Countries:   [United States, Canada, ...]
```

- If a customer's billing country is not in the list, the payment method **does not appear** at checkout.
- **Exam focus:** Country restrictions are based on the **billing address country**, not the shipping address.

---

### 7.2 Minimum and Maximum Order Amount

Every payment method supports optional order total gates:

| Field | Behavior |
|---|---|
| Minimum Order Total | Method hidden if order < this amount |
| Maximum Order Total | Method hidden if order > this amount |

**Use cases:**
- Hide COD for orders over $500 (fraud risk).
- Show Bank Transfer only for orders over $1,000 (wire fees make sense).
- Restrict PayPal Standard below $10 (micro-transaction handling).

**Example configuration scenario:**
```
Check/Money Order:
  Minimum Order Total: 0
  Maximum Order Total: 500.00

Bank Transfer:
  Minimum Order Total: 500.00
  Maximum Order Total: [empty = unlimited]
```

- **Exam focus:** Min/Max restrictions hide the payment method at checkout — they do **not** show an error. The method simply becomes unavailable.

---

### 7.3 Sort Order

```
Stores > Configuration > Sales > Payment Methods > [Method] > Sort Order
```

- Controls the display order of methods at checkout.
- Lower number = higher on the list (0 appears first).
- **Exam focus:** Sort order is numeric; **0 or lower = displayed first**.

## 8. PCI DSS Compliance & Security

### 8.1 What is PCI DSS?

**Payment Card Industry Data Security Standard** — a set of security standards to protect cardholder data during and after a transaction.

Applies to any organization that accepts, processes, stores, or transmits credit card information.

### 8.2 Core PCI Rules for Magento

| Rule | Magento Implication |
|---|---|
| Never store CVV | Magento **never** stores CVV/CVC — prohibited even transiently |
| Encrypt stored card data | Use tokenization (Vault) instead of raw PAN storage |
| Use HTTPS / TLS | All checkout pages must be HTTPS only |
| Limit access | Admin access controls, 2FA on Admin |
| Log and monitor | Audit logs for Admin actions |

### 8.3 CVV Rules — Critical Exam Topic

```
CVV (Card Verification Value):
  - The 3 or 4 digit code on the card
  - MUST be used for transaction verification
  - MUST NOT be stored ANYWHERE after authorization
  - Magento's core code does not store CVV in the database
  - Third-party modules that store CVV violate PCI DSS
```

- **Exam focus:** **Never store CVV** — not in the database, not in logs, not in session beyond the transaction. This is an absolute PCI DSS rule.

---

### 8.4 Tokenization and Vault

**Tokenization** replaces sensitive card data with a **token** — a non-sensitive reference that the payment gateway can exchange for the real card data.

```
Customer Enters Card Details
        |
        v
  Card data sent DIRECTLY to Gateway (Braintree, etc.)
  [Never touches Magento server]
        |
        v
  Gateway Returns Token (e.g., "tok_abc123xyz")
        |
        v
  Magento stores the TOKEN only
        |
        v
  Future charges use the Token
  [Customer's real card number never stored in Magento DB]
```

**Magento Vault:**
- Built-in framework for storing payment tokens.
- Enabled per payment method (e.g., Braintree Vault).
- Allows customers to save cards for future purchases ("Stored Payment Methods").
- Tokens are **gateway-specific** — a Braintree token cannot be used with Stripe.

```
Admin Path:
Stores > Configuration > Sales > Payment Methods > Braintree > Vault > Enabled: Yes
```

- **Exam focus:** Vault stores **tokens**, not card numbers. The actual PAN (Primary Account Number) is stored at the gateway, not in Magento.

---

### 8.5 HTTPS Configuration

```
Stores > Configuration > General > Web > Base URLs (Secure)
  Use Secure URLs on Storefront: Yes
  Use Secure URLs in Admin: Yes

There is no separate "Enable HTTPS on Checkout" setting in Magento 2. HTTPS enforcement for the entire storefront (including checkout) is controlled by the "Use Secure URLs on Storefront" setting above (`web/secure/use_in_frontend`). Enabling it applies HTTPS to all storefront pages, including checkout.
```

- **Exam focus:** Checkout HTTPS is a requirement for PCI compliance. Magento can be configured to redirect insecure checkout URLs to HTTPS automatically.

## 9. 3D Secure (3DS2)

### 9.1 What Is 3D Secure?

3D Secure (3DS) is an authentication protocol that adds an **additional verification step** between the customer and their card-issuing bank during online transactions.

**3DS2** is the modern version — supports:
- Risk-based authentication (may be invisible to low-risk customers)
- Biometric verification
- App-based push notifications
- Frictionless flow for trusted transactions

### 9.2 3DS2 Flow

```
Customer Enters Card at Checkout
        |
        v
  Merchant Sends Auth Request to Gateway
        |
        v
  Gateway Sends to Card Network (Visa/MC)
        |
        v
  Card Network Contacts Issuing Bank
        |
        v
  [Risk Assessment]
        |
        +-- LOW RISK --> Frictionless Flow
        |                (No customer action needed)
        |                Transaction Approved
        |
        +-- HIGH RISK --> Challenge Flow
                         Customer prompted to verify:
                         - OTP via SMS
                         - Push notification
                         - Password / PIN
                                |
                           Verified? Yes --> Approved
                           Verified? No  --> Declined
```

### 9.3 Liability Shift

The biggest business reason to implement 3DS2:

| Scenario | Chargeback Liability |
|---|---|
| No 3DS, fraud occurs | **Merchant** pays the chargeback |
| 3DS2 used, fraud occurs | **Issuing bank** pays the chargeback |

- **Exam focus:** **Liability shift** is the primary business benefit of 3DS2. When 3DS2 authentication occurs, the liability for fraudulent chargebacks shifts from the merchant to the card-issuing bank.

---

### 9.4 3DS2 Trade-offs

| Benefit | Drawback |
|---|---|
| Reduces chargebacks | Adds friction to checkout (challenge flow) |
| Liability shift to bank | Can increase cart abandonment |
| Required for SCA (EU/UK regulations) | Frictionless flow not always possible |
| Improves fraud detection | Gateway must support 3DS2 |

### 9.5 3DS2 in Magento (Braintree)

Braintree supports 3DS2 natively:

```
Stores > Configuration > Sales > Payment Methods > Braintree
  > 3D Secure Verification: Yes
  > Threshold Amount: [amount above which 3DS is always required]
  > Verify for Applicable Countries: All / Specific
```

- **Exam focus:** In Magento, 3DS2 is configured **per payment method**. Braintree has a dedicated 3DS2 section. The **threshold amount** allows low-value transactions to skip 3DS2 (reducing friction) while protecting high-value transactions.

### 13.4 Setting Payment Config Programmatically

```php
<?php
// Using Config Writer in a setup script or command
use Magento\Framework\App\Config\Storage\WriterInterface;

class EnablePaymentMethods
{
    public function __construct(
        private WriterInterface $configWriter
    ) {}

    public function execute(): void
    {
        // Enable Check/Money Order
        $this->configWriter->save(
            'payment/checkmo/active',
            '1',
            \Magento\Framework\App\Config\ScopeConfigInterface::SCOPE_TYPE_DEFAULT,
            0
        );

        // Set payment action for Braintree to Authorize Only
        $this->configWriter->save(
            'payment/braintree/payment_action',
            'authorize',  // 'authorize' or 'authorize_capture'
            \Magento\Framework\App\Config\ScopeConfigInterface::SCOPE_TYPE_DEFAULT,
            0
        );
    }
}
```

## 15. Common Exam Traps & Edge Cases

### Trap 1: Authorize Only ≠ Invoice

```
WRONG: "Authorize Only creates an invoice and reserves funds."
RIGHT: "Authorize Only reserves funds (authorization hold) but does NOT
        create an invoice. The invoice must be created manually, and
        that creation triggers the actual fund capture."
```

### Trap 2: PayPal Express vs. PayPal Payments Standard

```
WRONG: "Both PayPal methods offer shortcut checkout buttons."
RIGHT: "Only PayPal Express Checkout offers shortcut buttons.
        PayPal Payments Standard is a full redirect only."
```

### Trap 3: Zero Subtotal Triggers

```
WRONG: "Zero Subtotal Checkout appears for any discounted order."
RIGHT: "Zero Subtotal Checkout only appears when the order total
        is EXACTLY $0.00. $0.01 requires a normal payment method."
```

### Trap 4: CVV Storage

```
WRONG: "Magento Vault stores the CVV with the tokenized card."
RIGHT: "CVV is NEVER stored anywhere. Vault stores only the
        payment token. PCI DSS absolutely prohibits CVV storage."
```

### Trap 5: Country Restriction Basis

```
WRONG: "Payment method country restrictions check the shipping address."
RIGHT: "Payment method country restrictions are based on the
        BILLING address country."
```

### Trap 6: 3DS2 and Frictionless Flow

```
WRONG: "3DS2 always adds a visible authentication step."
RIGHT: "3DS2 includes a 'frictionless flow' where low-risk
        transactions are approved without customer interaction.
        The challenge flow is only triggered for high-risk transactions."
```

### Offline Payment Methods
- [ ] **Check/Money Order** — No gateway; customer mails payment; order stays Pending until manual update
- [ ] **Bank Transfer** — No gateway; wire transfer outside system; manually processed
- [ ] **Cash on Delivery** — Payment occurs at delivery; can be country/carrier restricted

- [ ] **PayPal Express Checkout** — In-context or redirect; shortcut buttons on product/cart/mini-cart
- [ ] **PayPal Payments Standard** — Full redirect only; no shortcut buttons; simplest setup
- [ ] **Braintree** — Supports CC, PayPal, Venmo, ACH; full gateway; Vault support; 3DS2

### Payment Actions
- [ ] **Authorize Only** — Reserves funds; does NOT move money; does NOT auto-create invoice
- [ ] **Authorize and Capture** — Immediately moves money; auto-creates invoice at order placement
- [ ] **Manual Capture** = Create Invoice on Authorize Only order → triggers gateway capture
- [ ] Auth holds expire in 7–30 days if not captured

### Zero Subtotal Checkout
- [ ] Triggered only when order total = **exactly $0.00**
- [ ] Caused by 100% coupons, gift cards, store credit, reward points
- [ ] "Automatically Invoice All Items" setting controls auto-invoicing

### Purchase Order
- [ ] B2B deferred payment method
- [ ] Customer enters PO number; no gateway contact
- [ ] PO number stored in `sales_order_payment.po_number`
- [ ] Works with Adobe Commerce B2B module for credit limits

### Payment Restrictions
- [ ] Country restrictions based on **billing address** (not shipping)
- [ ] Min/Max order total hides method (no error — method just disappears)
- [ ] Sort Order: lower number = displayed first (0 = top)

### PCI DSS
- [ ] **Never store CVV** — absolute rule, no exceptions
- [ ] Use **tokenization** (Vault) instead of raw card numbers
- [ ] Card data goes directly to gateway via JS SDK (never to Magento server)
- [ ] Vault table: `vault_payment_token`
- [ ] HTTPS required on all checkout pages

### 3D Secure (3DS2)
- [ ] Adds authentication step between customer and issuing bank
- [ ] **Frictionless flow** = low-risk, no customer action needed
- [ ] **Challenge flow** = high-risk, OTP/push notification required
- [ ] **Liability shift** — with 3DS2, chargeback liability moves to issuing bank
- [ ] Reduces chargebacks but may increase cart abandonment
- [ ] Required for **SCA** (Strong Customer Authentication) in EU/UK

### Braintree-Specific
- [ ] Supports: Credit/Debit Cards, PayPal, **Venmo**, **ACH Direct Debit**
- [ ] Configuration: Environment (Sandbox/Production), Merchant ID, Public Key, Private Key

- [ ] All payment methods: `Stores > Configuration > Sales > Payment Methods`

- [ ] Zero Subtotal: `payment/free/active`
- [ ] CLI: `bin/magento config:show payment` / `bin/magento config:set`

### Common Exam Traps
- [ ] Authorize Only ≠ invoice created ≠ funds moved
- [ ] Invoice creation on Authorize Only order = capture trigger
- [ ] Zero Subtotal = exactly $0.00 only
