```
  EE adds:
  - Stores > Other Settings > Gift Wrapping
  - Stores > Other Settings > Reward Exchange Rates
```

### Category Edit Page Differences

```
CE Category Edit:
  - Products in Category tab: basic grid with position column

EE Category Edit:
  - Products in Category tab: Visual Merchandiser with 
    drag-and-drop + auto-sort rules
```

### Product Edit Page Differences

```
CE Product Edit Types:
  Simple, Configurable, Grouped, Bundle, Virtual, Downloadable

EE Product Edit Types (adds):
  + Gift Card
```

**Exam focus:**
- If you see "Gift Card" in the product type dropdown → you are in EE admin.
- If you see "Dynamic Blocks" under Content > Elements → you are in EE admin.
- The Visual Merchandiser replaces the basic product position grid in EE category management.

---

## 8. Architecture & Licensing Notes

### Module Structure

EE modules follow a separate namespace and are delivered via Composer from Adobe's private repository (`repo.magento.com`).

```bash
# CE modules follow magento/module-* pattern
# EE-exclusive modules:

magento/module-admin-gws           # Admin permissions per website
magento/module-banner              # Dynamic Blocks
magento/module-catalog-permissions # Catalog Permissions
magento/module-customer-segment    # Customer Segments
magento/module-gift-card           # Gift Cards
magento/module-gift-wrapping       # Gift Wrapping
magento/module-reward              # Reward Points
magento/module-rma                 # RMA
magento/module-staging             # Content Staging core
magento/module-visual-merchandiser # Visual Merchandiser

# B2B modules (separate B2B package):
magento/module-company             
magento/module-shared-catalog      
magento/module-negotiable-quote    
magento/module-requisition-list    
magento/module-purchase-order      
```

### Composer Authentication

```bash
# EE requires authentication to repo.magento.com
# auth.json contains public/private key from Adobe Marketplace account

composer config repositories.adobe-commerce \
  composer https://repo.magento.com

# auth.json structure:
```

```json
{
    "http-basic": {
        "repo.magento.com": {
            "username": "your-public-key",
            "password": "your-private-key"
        }
    }
}
```

**Exam focus:**
- EE modules come from `repo.magento.com` and require valid Marketplace credentials.
- Access to EE packages is controlled at the Composer repository level via Marketplace credentials.

### License Enforcement

EE features are delivered via proprietary-licensed Composer packages from `repo.magento.com`. Access control is enforced at the Composer repository level — only accounts with a valid EE license can download the EE packages. There is no separate `magento/module-license` module in the codebase. The `crypt/key` in `app/etc/env.php` is the encryption key for sensitive data, not a license key.

---

## 9. Hands-On Sandbox Reference

When exploring your `local-instance` to compare CE vs EE:

### Checklist for EE Verification

```
Admin Panel Verification:
  [ ] Content > Elements menu shows "Dynamic Blocks"
  [ ] Content menu shows "Staging" submenu  
  [ ] Content > Elements shows "Hierarchy"
  [ ] Customers menu shows "Segments"
  [ ] Marketing > Promotions menu shows "Related Products Rules"
  [ ] Sales menu shows "Returns"
  [ ] Catalog shows "Shared Catalogs" (if B2B enabled)
  [ ] Customers shows "Companies" (if B2B enabled)
  [ ] Add Product shows "Gift Card" type option
  [ ] Category > Products tab shows Visual Merchandiser

Configuration Verification:
  [ ] Stores > Config > Customers > Reward Points exists
  [ ] Stores > Other Settings > Gift Wrapping exists
```

### Key Admin Paths to Memorize

```
Content Staging:         Content > Staging > Dashboard
Dynamic Blocks:          Content > Elements > Dynamic Blocks
CMS Hierarchy:           Content > Elements > Hierarchy
Customer Segments:       Customers > Segments
Related Product Rules:   Marketing > Promotions > Related Products Rules
Visual Merchandiser:     Catalog > Categories > [Category] > Products tab
Catalog Permissions:     Stores > Config > Catalog > Catalog > Category Permissions
Reward Points Config:    Stores > Config > Customers > Reward Points
Gift Wrapping:           Stores > Other Settings > Gift Wrapping
RMA:                     Sales > Returns
B2B Companies:           Customers > Companies
Shared Catalogs:         Catalog > Shared Catalogs
Negotiable Quotes:       Sales > Quotes
Gift Card Products:      Catalog > Products > Add Product > Gift Card
Advanced Reporting:      Reports > Business Intelligence > Advanced Reporting
```

### Testing Staging in Sandbox

```
1. Go to: Catalog > Products > Select any product
2. Click "Schedule New Update" button 
   (appears only in EE - this button does NOT exist in CE)
3. Set a future start date
4. Modify product name/price
5. Save update
6. Go to Content > Staging > Dashboard
7. Use Preview button to see future state
8. Note the preview toolbar at top of storefront
```

**Exam focus:** The **"Schedule New Update"** button on product/category/CMS pages is a definitive visual indicator of EE. It does not appear in CE.

---

## Quick-Reference Checklist

### EE-Exclusive Features (Must Memorize)

- [ ] **Content Staging & Preview** — schedule future content/price changes, preview by date
- [ ] **Dynamic Blocks** — content blocks that respond to customer segments and cart rules
- [ ] **CMS Hierarchy** — tree structure for CMS pages
- [ ] **Page Restrictions** — restrict CMS page access by segment/login status
- [ ] **Dynamic Block content type in Page Builder** — requires EE (Page Builder itself ships with both CE and EE)
- [ ] **B2B Suite** — entire B2B module is EE-only:
  - [ ] Company Accounts with roles/permissions/credit
  - [ ] Shared Catalog with custom pricing per company
  - [ ] Negotiable Quotes (back-and-forth price negotiation)
  - [ ] Requisition Lists (multiple named buy-again lists)
  - [ ] Quick Order (SKU-based ordering)
- [ ] **Customer Segments** — dynamic rule-based customer grouping
- [ ] **Related Product Rules** — attribute-based automated related/upsell/cross-sell
- [ ] **Visual Merchandiser** — drag-and-drop category product sorting with auto-rules
- [ ] **Catalog Permissions** — restrict categories/products by customer group
- [ ] **Gift Card** (product type) — Virtual, Physical, Combined
- [ ] **Gift Wrapping** — per-item or per-order, with fee
- [ ] **Reward Points** — earn/redeem loyalty points
- [ ] **Store Credit** — admin-assigned customer credit balance
- [ ] **RMA** — full return merchandise authorization workflow
- [ ] **Async Order Processing** — queue-based order processing
- [ ] ~~Advanced Reporting / BI~~ — **NOT EE-exclusive**, ships with both CE and EE (module-analytics has OSL-3.0 license)

### Available in BOTH CE and EE (Do NOT Say EE-Only)

- [ ] **MSI (Multi-Source Inventory)** — ships with CE since 2.3, NOT EE-exclusive
- [ ] **Page Builder** — ships bundled with CE since 2.4 (not a separate Marketplace download)
- [ ] **Cart Price Rules & Coupons** — both editions
- [ ] **Catalog Price Rules** — both editions
- [ ] **Customer Groups** — both editions (NOT the same as Customer Segments)
- [ ] **Wishlist** — both editions (NOT Requisition Lists)
- [ ] **CMS Pages & Blocks (basic)** — both editions
- [ ] **Elasticsearch/OpenSearch search** — both editions
- [ ] **Layered Navigation** — both editions

### SaaS Add-Ons (Separate Subscription, CE or EE)

- [ ] **Live Search** — Adobe SaaS search replacement (NOT included in any license)
- [ ] **Product Recommendations** — AI-powered Sensei recommendations (NOT included)
- [ ] **Payment Services** — Adobe hosted payment processing (NOT included)
- [ ] **Catalog Service** — high-performance SaaS GraphQL for headless (NOT included)

### Critical Distinctions for Exam

- [ ] Customer **Segments** (EE, dynamic) ≠ Customer **Groups** (CE+EE, static)
- [ ] **Related Product Rules** (EE, automated) ≠ manual related products (CE+EE)
- [ ] **Requisition Lists** (EE, B2B) ≠ Wishlist (CE+EE, consumer)
- [ ] **Page Builder** ships with both CE and EE — Dynamic Block content type requires EE
- [ ] **Advanced Reporting** is CE+EE (NOT EE-exclusive) ≠ Basic Reports also CE+EE
- [ ] SaaS add-ons are **not bundled** with EE or CE — separate subscription required
- [ ] **"Schedule New Update"** button = visual proof of EE admin panel
- [ ] Gift Card is an **EE-only product type** (not in CE product type list)
- [ ] B2B module is **EE-only** — no B2B features exist in CE natively
- [ ] Catalog Permissions is required for Shared Catalog; both are **EE-only**
- [ ] Dynamic Blocks require Customer Segments to be useful; both **EE-only**
- [ ] Live Search and native Elasticsearch **cannot run simultaneously**
- [ ] Product Recommendations requires **sufficient behavioral data** (cold-start issue)
- [ ] RMA is **EE-only** — CE has no built-in returns management
- [ ] Store Credit ≠ Gift Cards ≠ Reward Points (all EE-only but different mechanisms)

flashcards.question: What is Content Staging & Preview, and which edition provides it?
flashcards.answer: Content Staging (EE-only) allows merchants to schedule future changes to products, categories, CMS pages, CMS blocks, catalog price rules, and cart price rules, then preview exactly how the store will look at any future date/time. It introduces staging database tables and version records. The Staging Dashboard is under Content > Staging > Dashboard. Open Source has NO scheduling capability natively.
flashcards.hint: Schedule future content/price changes and preview them — the flagship EE feature.

flashcards.question: What are the three types of Gift Cards in Adobe Commerce (EE), and is this product type available in Open Source?
flashcards.answer: Gift Card is an EE-only product type with three subtypes: Virtual (email delivery only), Physical (mailed, no email), and Combined (both email and physical delivery). Gift Cards do NOT exist in Open Source — they only appear in the product type dropdown in EE installations.
flashcards.hint: Three flavors: virtual, physical, combined. Only on the EE menu.

flashcards.question: What is the difference between manual Related Products (CE) and Related Product Rules (EE)?
flashcards.answer: In CE, merchants manually assign related, up-sell, and cross-sell products on each product's edit page — a static, per-product assignment. In EE, Related Product Rules automatically generate these associations based on attribute matching rules (e.g., show accessories for all laptops in a brand). Automated rules are EE-only; manual assignment works in both editions.
flashcards.hint: Manual = pick each product by hand (CE+EE). Rules = automatic matching by attributes (EE only).

flashcards.question: Is Page Builder available in Magento Open Source (CE), and what is the one content type that requires EE?
flashcards.answer: Yes, Page Builder ships bundled with both CE and EE since Magento 2.4 — it is NOT a separate Marketplace download. The only content type within Page Builder that requires EE is the Dynamic Block content type, because Dynamic Blocks themselves are EE-only.
flashcards.hint: Page Builder = both editions since 2.4. Dynamic Block widget inside it = EE only.

flashcards.question: What is CMS Hierarchy, and which edition provides it?
flashcards.answer: CMS Hierarchy (EE-only) allows CMS pages to be organized into a tree hierarchy with parent-child relationships, enabling automatic navigation menus and prev/next links between CMS pages. The admin path is Content > Elements > Hierarchy. In CE, CMS pages are flat with no hierarchical organization.
flashcards.hint: Tree of CMS pages with navigation = EE. Flat, unrelated pages = CE.

flashcards.question: What is Visual Merchandiser, and how does it differ from CE category product sorting?
flashcards.answer: Visual Merchandiser (EE-only) provides a drag-and-drop interface for sorting products within categories, plus rules-based automatic sorting by price, color, stock status, or custom attributes. In CE, category product sorting is done only via a manual Position number field — no drag-and-drop and no automated rules.
flashcards.hint: Drag-and-drop + auto-sort rules = EE. Typing position numbers manually = CE.

flashcards.question: What five features make up the B2B Suite in Adobe Commerce, and is any part available in Open Source?
flashcards.answer: The B2B Suite (entirely EE-only) includes: 1) Company Accounts with roles/permissions/credit, 2) Shared Catalog with custom pricing per company, 3) Negotiable Quotes for price negotiation, 4) Requisition Lists for repeat ordering, and 5) Quick Order for SKU-based ordering. No B2B features are available in Open Source.
flashcards.hint: Company, Shared Catalog, Quotes, Requisition Lists, Quick Order — all EE, zero CE.

flashcards.question: What are the four SaaS add-on services for Adobe Commerce, and are they included with the EE license?
flashcards.answer: The four SaaS add-ons are: Live Search (replaces native search), Product Recommendations (AI-powered by Adobe Sensei), Payment Services (Adobe-managed payment processing), and Catalog Service (high-performance GraphQL API for headless). None are included in any license — they all require a separate SaaS subscription.
flashcards.hint: Four SaaS services, all sold separately — not bundled with CE or EE.

flashcards.question: Is MSI (Multi-Source Inventory) an EE-only feature?
flashcards.answer: No, MSI is NOT EE-only — this is the #1 most common exam trap. MSI was introduced in Magento 2.3.0 and ships with BOTH Open Source (CE) and Commerce (EE). It allows products to be stocked across multiple physical sources with reservation-based inventory deduction.
flashcards.hint: MSI = both editions since 2.3. If the exam says MSI is EE-only, that's wrong.

flashcards.question: What distinguishes Reward Points from Store Credit in Adobe Commerce, and which edition supports them?
flashcards.answer: Both are EE-only. Reward Points are earned through customer activity (purchases, registration, reviews, newsletter signup) with configurable expiry and exchange rates, redeemed at checkout. Store Credit is a balance directly assigned by the admin to a customer account — it's not earned through activity. Both appear as payment options at checkout.
flashcards.hint: Points = earned by the customer. Credit = given by the admin. Both EE-only.

flashcards.question: What distinguishes Requisition Lists (EE) from Wishlists (CE+EE)?
flashcards.answer: Wishlists are consumer-focused save-for-later lists available in both CE (single) and EE (multiple). Requisition Lists are B2B/EE-only features that allow buyers to save named lists of frequently ordered products optimized for repeat purchasing — items can be added to cart from the list with one click. A single buyer can have multiple requisition lists.
flashcards.hint: Wishlist = consumer, 'I want this someday.' Requisition List = B2B, 'I order this every month.'

flashcards.question: What is the 'Schedule New Update' button, and why is it significant for identifying editions?
flashcards.answer: The 'Schedule New Update' button appears on product, category, and CMS page edit screens ONLY in Adobe Commerce (EE). It allows scheduling future content/price changes via Content Staging. This button does NOT exist in Open Source (CE), making it a definitive visual indicator of which edition is installed.
flashcards.hint: See 'Schedule New Update'? You're in EE. Don't see it? You're in CE.

flashcards.question: Is Advanced Reporting an EE-exclusive feature?
flashcards.answer: No, Advanced Reporting (Reports > Business Intelligence > Advanced Reporting) is available in BOTH CE and EE. The module-analytics has OSL-3.0 license. It requires an active data sync to Adobe's reporting service. Both editions also have basic sales/product/customer reports.
flashcards.hint: Advanced Reporting = both editions. Don't mark it as EE-only on the exam.

## 1. Hosting Options Overview

Adobe Commerce is available across **four primary deployment models**, each targeting different business sizes, technical capabilities, and SLA requirements.

```
+---------------------------+-----------------------------+
|   Deployment Model        |   Who Manages Infra?        |
+---------------------------+-----------------------------+
| Cloud Pro (PaaS)          | Adobe                       |
| Cloud Starter (PaaS)      | Adobe                       |
| On-Premises               | Customer                    |
| Managed Services          | Adobe (with SLA)            |
+---------------------------+-----------------------------+
```

> **Exam focus:** Know the *ownership boundary* for each model — who patches, who scales, who manages uptime.

## 2. Adobe Commerce Cloud Pro

### 2.1 What It Is

Cloud Pro is Adobe's **enterprise-grade Platform-as-a-Service (PaaS)** offering. It is a *fully managed, high-availability* hosting solution with infrastructure purpose-built for large-scale commerce workloads.

### 2.2 Environment Architecture

Cloud Pro uses a **cluster-based architecture** with clearly separated tiers:

```
+--------------------------------------------------+
|               Cloud Pro Environments             |
+--------------------------------------------------+
|                                                  |
|  Integration Tier (x8 environments)              |
|  +----------+  +----------+  +----------+  ...  |
|  | Integ. 1 |  | Integ. 2 |  | Integ. 3 |       |
|  +----------+  +----------+  +----------+       |
|                                                  |
|  Dedicated Staging Cluster                       |
|  +------------------------------------------+   |
|  |  Mirrors production topology (HA)         |   |
|  +------------------------------------------+   |
|                                                  |
|  Dedicated Production Cluster                    |
|  +------------------------------------------+   |
|  |  HA: Web + DB + Cache + Search nodes      |   |
|  |  Auto-scaling enabled                     |   |
|  |  Fastly CDN natively integrated           |   |
|  +------------------------------------------+   |
|                                                  |
+--------------------------------------------------+
```

| Tier | Count | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| Integration | 8 environments | Dev/feature branch testing |
| Staging | 1 dedicated cluster | Pre-production QA, mirrors prod |
| Production | 1 dedicated cluster | Live traffic, HA, auto-scaling |

> **Exam focus:** Cloud Pro provides **8 integration environments**, plus **1 dedicated staging cluster** and **1 dedicated production cluster** — that is a total of **10 environments** across the tiers.

### 2.3 Key Infrastructure Features

- **High Availability (HA):** Production and staging run on *separate, dedicated clusters* with redundant nodes across web, database, cache, and search layers.
- **Auto-scaling:** Web tier scales horizontally based on traffic demand — no manual intervention required.
- **Global CDN via Fastly:** Fastly is **natively integrated** (not bolted on). It handles:
  - Full-page caching
  - DDoS protection
  - WAF (Web Application Firewall)
  - Image optimization
  - Edge-side logic via VCL (Varnish Configuration Language)
- **SLA:** **99.99% uptime** guarantee on production.
- **Managed services included:** Adobe manages OS patching, infrastructure security, scaling, backups, and monitoring.

```bash
# Example: Checking environment list via Magento Cloud CLI
magento-cloud environment:list

# Output example (Cloud Pro):
# ID           Title          Status
# master        Production     Active
# staging       Staging        Active
# feature-x     Feature X      Active
# feature-y     Feature Y      Active
```

> **Exam focus:** The SLA for Cloud Pro production is **99.99%** — this is a frequently tested specific figure.

> **Exam focus:** Fastly CDN is **native to Cloud Pro** — it is not an optional add-on but a core infrastructure component.

### 2.4 Technology Stack Components

```
+--------------------------------------------------+
|              Cloud Pro Stack Layers              |
+--------------------------------------------------+
| Layer            | Technology                    |
+------------------+-------------------------------+
| CDN              | Fastly                        |
| Load Balancer    | HAProxy / Cloud-managed       |
| Web Server       | Nginx                         |
| PHP Runtime      | PHP-FPM                       |
| Database         | MariaDB (Galera cluster)      |
| Cache            | Redis                         |
| Search           | Elasticsearch / OpenSearch    |
| Object Storage   | NFS / Cloud storage           |
| Queue            | RabbitMQ                      |
+--------------------------------------------------+
```

## 3. Adobe Commerce Cloud Starter

### 3.1 What It Is

Cloud Starter is Adobe's **entry-level PaaS** offering. It shares the same codebase as Cloud Pro but uses a **simpler, single-cluster infrastructure model** optimized for lower cost and smaller traffic volumes.

### 3.2 Environment Architecture

```
+------------------------------------------+
|         Cloud Starter Environments       |
+------------------------------------------+
|                                          |
|  Production (1)                          |
|  +------------------------------------+  |
|  |  Single cluster, no auto-scaling   |  |
|  |  Fastly included                   |  |
|  +------------------------------------+  |
|                                          |
|  Staging (1, shared infra)              |
|  +------------------------------------+  |
|  |  Included but NOT dedicated cluster |  |
|  +------------------------------------+  |
|                                          |
|  Integration Environments (x2)          |
|  +---------+ +---------+                |
|  | Integ.1 | | Integ.2 |               |
|  +---------+ +---------+                |
|                                          |
+------------------------------------------+
```

| Tier | Count | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Production | 1 | Single cluster (not HA dedicated) |
| Staging | 1 | Included but NOT on a dedicated cluster (shared infra) |
| Integration | 2 | Shared infrastructure |

> **Exam focus:** Cloud Starter has **4 total environments** (1 Production + 1 Staging + 2 Integration). Staging IS included, but it runs on shared infrastructure — NOT on a dedicated cluster like Cloud Pro. The critical differentiator from Pro is the lack of a **dedicated staging cluster**, not the absence of staging entirely.

### 3.3 Key Characteristics

- **Lower cost** than Cloud Pro — designed for SMB/mid-market
- **Simpler infrastructure** — single cluster topology
- **No auto-scaling** — fixed resource allocation
- **Fastly CDN is still included** (this is a key similarity with Cloud Pro)
- **No dedicated staging cluster** — Starter includes a staging environment but it runs on shared infrastructure, not a separate HA cluster like Cloud Pro

> **Exam focus:** Cloud Starter **does include Fastly CDN** even though it lacks dedicated staging. Do not assume Fastly is exclusive to Cloud Pro.

## 4. Cloud Pro vs Cloud Starter — Deep Comparison

> **Critical Exam Trap:** Cloud Pro is **NOT simply a "bigger" Cloud Starter**. They have **fundamentally different infrastructure architectures**. Cloud Pro uses separate, dedicated production and staging clusters with HA and auto-scaling. Cloud Starter uses a simplified, single-cluster model.

### 4.1 Side-by-Side Comparison

| Feature | Cloud Pro | Cloud Starter |
|---|---|---|
| Total environments | 10 (8 integration + staging + production) | 4 (2 integration + staging + production) |
| Dedicated staging cluster | **Yes** | **No** (staging on shared infra) |
| Production cluster type | Dedicated HA cluster | Single cluster |
| Auto-scaling | **Yes** | No |
| Fastly CDN | Yes (native) | Yes (included) |
| SLA | **99.99%** | Lower (not 99.99%) |
| Infrastructure complexity | High — multi-node HA | Simple — single cluster |
| Target market | Enterprise / large-scale | SMB / mid-market |
| Cost | Higher | Lower |
| OS / infra management | Adobe-managed | Adobe-managed |
| MariaDB cluster (Galera) | Yes (HA) | Single DB node |
| RabbitMQ | Yes | Limited |

### 4.2 The Architecture Difference Visualized

```
Cloud Pro Production:             Cloud Starter Production:

  +----------+                      +------------------+
  | Web Node |--+                   |                  |
  +----------+  |  +----------+    |   Single Node    |
  | Web Node |--+->| MariaDB  |    |   All-in-one     |
  +----------+  |  | Cluster  |    |   (simplified)   |
  | Web Node |--+  +----------+    |                  |
  +----------+                     +------------------+
       |
  +---------+
  |  Redis  |
  +---------+
  +-----------------+
  | Elasticsearch   |
  +-----------------+
       ^
  [Auto-scaled web
   nodes added here]
```

> **Exam focus:** The **separate production cluster** with HA nodes is what makes Cloud Pro architecturally distinct — not just "more resources."

## 5. On-Premises (Self-Hosted)

### 5.1 What It Is

The **on-premises** deployment model is the traditional self-hosted installation of Adobe Commerce (formerly Magento 2 Enterprise Edition). The customer downloads the software and runs it on their own or third-party infrastructure.

### 5.2 Customer Responsibilities

```
+------------------------------------------------+
|        On-Premises: Responsibility Matrix      |
+------------------------------------------------+
| Layer               | Who Is Responsible?      |
+---------------------+--------------------------+
| Commerce Software   | Customer (with Adobe lic)|
| Application Updates | Customer                 |
| Security Patches    | Customer                 |
| Server Hardware     | Customer / Hosting       |
| OS Management       | Customer                 |
| Database Admin      | Customer                 |
| CDN (optional)      | Customer                 |
| Scaling             | Customer                 |
| Uptime/Monitoring   | Customer                 |
| Backups             | Customer                 |
+------------------------------------------------+
```

> **Exam focus:** In on-premises, the **customer is responsible for all infrastructure, updates, and security patches** — Adobe only provides the software license and support.

### 5.3 Key Characteristics

- **Full control** over infrastructure, customization, and integrations
- **Full responsibility** for security, performance, scaling, and uptime
- **No Adobe-managed SLA** for infrastructure (software support only)
- Supported on Linux-based stacks (typically LEMP: Linux, Nginx/Apache, MySQL/MariaDB, PHP)
- Common choice for organizations with strict data sovereignty requirements or existing data center investments

```bash
# On-premises: Manual security patch application example
composer require magento/product-community-edition=2.4.7-p1 --no-update
composer update
bin/magento setup:upgrade
bin/magento setup:di:compile
bin/magento setup:static-content:deploy
```

## 6. Adobe Commerce Managed Services

### 6.1 What It Is

**Managed Services** is Adobe's offering where Adobe hosts and manages an on-premises-style Commerce installation on behalf of the customer. Think of it as "on-prem architecture, but Adobe runs it."

### 6.2 Key Characteristics

- Adobe provisions and manages the dedicated infrastructure
- Includes a formal **support SLA** for both software and infrastructure
- More customization flexibility than Cloud PaaS models (direct server access often available)
- Higher cost than Cloud options — positioned for large enterprise with specific infra needs
- Adobe handles OS, security patching, backups, and monitoring
- Not a "shared" environment — dedicated hardware/VMs per customer

### 6.3 Managed Services vs Cloud Pro

| Feature | Cloud Pro | Managed Services |
|---|---|---|
| Infrastructure model | PaaS / Cloud-native | Dedicated managed hosting |
| Deployment approach | Git-based, CI/CD pipeline | Traditional deployment |
| Auto-scaling | Yes | Limited / manual |
| Customization depth | PaaS constraints apply | Deeper access |
| Adobe manages infra | Yes | Yes |
| SLA | 99.99% | Yes (varies by contract) |

> **Exam focus:** Managed Services is **Adobe-managed on-premises** — it is NOT a PaaS product. Adobe manages the infrastructure, but the architecture pattern is closer to on-prem than to Cloud Pro.

## 7. SaaS Service Add-ons

Adobe Commerce SaaS add-ons are **separately deployed, Adobe-managed services** that connect to a Commerce instance (Cloud or on-prem EE) via API. They do **not** require modifying Commerce core code.

> **Exam focus:** SaaS add-ons work with **both Cloud (Pro and Starter) and on-premises Enterprise Edition** — they are not exclusive to Cloud.

### 7.1 Overview of SaaS Add-ons

```
+--------------------------------------------------------+
|                  Adobe Commerce Instance               |
|           (Cloud Pro / Cloud Starter / On-Prem EE)     |
+---------------------------+----------------------------+
                            |
                    [API / Data Feed]
                            |
         +------------------+------------------+
         |                  |                  |
+--------+--------+ +-------+------+ +---------+-------+
|   Live Search   | | Product Rec. | | Payment Services|
| (replaces native| | (AI-powered) | | (Adobe-managed) |
|    search)      | |              | |                 |
+-----------------+ +--------------+ +-----------------+
         |
+--------+--------+
| Catalog Service |
| (headless API)  |
+-----------------+
```

### 7.2 Live Search

**Live Search** is a SaaS replacement for Adobe Commerce's native Elasticsearch/OpenSearch-based catalog search.

| Attribute | Detail |
|---|---|
| Type | SaaS (Adobe-hosted) |
| Replaces | Native Commerce search (Elasticsearch/OpenSearch) |
| Technology | Adobe-managed search engine with faceting, ranking, synonyms |
| Integration | Data sync via Commerce Data Connector (feed export) |
| Storefront | Returns results via GraphQL API |
| Key advantage | No Elasticsearch cluster to manage; AI-powered ranking |

```javascript
// Live Search GraphQL query example
query {
  productSearch(phrase: "running shoes") {
    items {
      product {
        sku
        name
        price_range {
          minimum_price {
            final_price { value, currency }
          }
        }
      }
    }
    facets {
      title
      values { label, count }
    }
  }
}
```

> **Exam focus:** Live Search **replaces** native search — it is not layered on top. When enabled, Elasticsearch/OpenSearch is no longer used for storefront search.

### 7.3 Product Recommendations

**Product Recommendations** surfaces AI-powered "you may also like," "trending," "viewed this/viewed that" recommendation blocks throughout the storefront.

| Attribute | Detail |
|---|---|
| Type | SaaS (Adobe-managed, Adobe Sensei AI) |
| Powers | Behavioral data analysis + product affinity |
| Requires | Sufficient catalog and behavioral event data |
| Integration | Widget-based + GraphQL API |
| Configuration | Admin panel: choose recommendation type per page/placement |

**Recommendation Types Available:**

```
- Most Viewed
- Most Purchased
- Most Added to Cart
- Trending
- Recommended for You (personalized)
- Viewed This, Viewed That
- Viewed This, Bought That
- Bought This, Bought That
- More Like This
- Visual Similarity
```

> **Exam focus:** Product Recommendations is powered by **Adobe Sensei** (Adobe's AI/ML framework). It requires event data collection to be effective — new storefronts need a "warm-up" period.

### 7.4 Payment Services

**Payment Services** is an Adobe-managed payment processing solution that consolidates payment acceptance, reporting, and fraud management into a unified Commerce-native dashboard.

| Attribute | Detail |
|---|---|
| Type | SaaS (Adobe-managed payment processing) |
| Powered by | PayPal / Braintree infrastructure (Adobe partnership) |
| Features | Credit/debit, PayPal, Venmo, Apple Pay, Google Pay |
| Reporting | Unified order + payment reporting in Commerce Admin |
| PCI compliance | Adobe/PayPal manages PCI DSS compliance |
| Availability | US, Canada, Australia, UK, and select other markets |

> **Exam focus:** Payment Services is **Adobe-managed** — meaning the merchant does not need to independently manage PCI compliance for the payment gateway layer. Adobe handles this.

### 7.5 Catalog Service

**Catalog Service** is a high-performance, read-optimized catalog data API designed for **headless commerce storefronts**.

| Attribute | Detail |
|---|---|
| Type | SaaS (Adobe-managed) |
| Purpose | High-throughput product data retrieval for headless/PWA |
| API type | GraphQL |
| Key advantage | Faster than querying Commerce database directly |
| Use case | Decoupled frontends (React, Next.js, Vue Storefront, etc.) |
| Data sync | Near-real-time sync from Commerce catalog |

```graphql
# Catalog Service query example
query {
  products(skus: ["MH01-XS-Black"]) {
    sku
    name
    description { html }
    images(roles: ["thumbnail"]) {
      url
      label
    }
    priceRange {
      minimum { regular { amount { value currency } } }
    }
  }
}
```

> **Exam focus:** Catalog Service is specifically designed for **headless/composable commerce scenarios** — it is not a replacement for the Admin catalog management UI.

### 7.6 SaaS Add-ons: Compatibility Matrix

| Add-on | Cloud Pro | Cloud Starter | On-Prem EE | Open Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Live Search | Yes | Yes | Yes | No |
| Product Recommendations | Yes | Yes | Yes | No |
| Payment Services | Yes | Yes | Yes | Limited |
| Catalog Service | Yes | Yes | Yes | No |

> **Exam focus:** Most SaaS add-ons are marketed for **Adobe Commerce (EE/Cloud)**. However, the SaaS infrastructure modules in the codebase (services-connector, module-saas-catalog, module-payment-services-*) all carry OSL-3.0 licenses, meaning the data sync and payment services layers are technically CE-compatible. Adobe may restrict backend service access by license. Payment Services has the broadest CE support; Live Search and Product Recommendations are primarily positioned for Commerce.

## 8. Adobe Commerce as a Cloud Service (ACaaS)

### 8.1 What It Is

**ACaaS** represents Adobe's **next-generation, fully composable commerce architecture** — a SaaS-first approach where the entire Commerce platform is delivered as managed microservices, not a monolithic PaaS application.

### 8.2 Key Characteristics

```
+-----------------------------------------------------------+
|              ACaaS: Composable Commerce Model             |
+-----------------------------------------------------------+
|                                                           |
|   SaaS Storefront Layer (Adobe Commerce Storefront)       |
|   +--------------------------------------------------+    |
|   |  Edge Delivery Services + Storefront Components  |    |
|   +--------------------------------------------------+    |
|                          |                                |
|                     [API Layer]                           |
|                          |                                |
|  +----------+ +----------+ +----------+ +----------+      |
|  | Catalog  | |  Order   | | Checkout | | Customer |      |
|  | Service  | | Service  | | Service  | | Profile  |      |
|  +----------+ +----------+ +----------+ +----------+      |
|                                                           |
|  All services = Adobe-managed SaaS (no app server)        |
+-----------------------------------------------------------+
```

- **Emerging / next-gen offering** — not yet the primary deployment recommendation for all merchants (as of 2024/2025)
- Commerce capabilities delivered as **discrete SaaS services** rather than a monolithic app
- Merchant does not manage any servers, clusters, or deployment pipelines
- Adobe handles **all infrastructure, scaling, updates, and security**
- Designed for **maximum agility** — frontend fully decoupled from backend services
- Aligns with Adobe's broader **Experience Cloud composable strategy**

> **Exam focus:** ACaaS is positioned as **composable commerce** — not just "Cloud Pro in a new format." It is architecturally distinct: SaaS microservices, not a PaaS monolith.

> **Exam focus:** ACaaS is an **emerging** offering. Questions may test awareness of its existence and its composable/SaaS-first positioning rather than deep implementation details.

## 9. Extensibility: API Mesh & App Builder

Adobe's extensibility strategy for Commerce has shifted toward **out-of-process extensibility** — building customizations and integrations *outside* the Commerce core application, avoiding core modification.

### 9.1 App Builder

**Adobe Developer App Builder** is Adobe's **serverless, cloud-native application framework** for building custom Commerce extensions and integrations.

```
+--------------------------------------------------+
|              App Builder Architecture            |
+--------------------------------------------------+
|                                                  |
|  Custom Business Logic (serverless functions)    |
|  +---------+  +---------+  +---------+           |
|  | Action1 |  | Action2 |  | Action3 |           |
|  +---------+  +---------+  +---------+           |
|       |             |            |               |
|       v             v            v               |
|  +--------------------------------------------+  |
|  |  Adobe I/O Runtime (Apache OpenWhisk)      |  |
|  +--------------------------------------------+  |
|       |                                          |
|       v                                          |
|  +-----------------+  +---------------------+    |
|  | Commerce Events |  | Commerce REST/Graph  |    |
|  | (I/O Events)    |  | QL APIs             |    |
|  +-----------------+  +---------------------+    |
|                                                  |
+--------------------------------------------------+
```

| Feature | Detail |
|---|---|
| Platform | Adobe I/O Runtime (serverless, Apache OpenWhisk) |
| Purpose | Custom apps, integrations, workflows outside Commerce core |
| Trigger types | Commerce events (order placed, customer created, etc.), webhooks, scheduled |
| UI extension | Admin UI SDK — extend Commerce Admin without core modification |
| No core modification | Fully out-of-process — Commerce codebase untouched |
| Deployment | Adobe-hosted serverless infrastructure |

```javascript
// App Builder action example: respond to order.placed event
const { Core } = require('@adobe/aio-sdk')

async function main(params) {
  const order = params.data.value

  // Custom business logic: send to ERP
  await sendToERP({
    orderId: order.increment_id,
    items: order.items,
    total: order.grand_total
  })

  return { statusCode: 200, body: { result: 'synced' } }
}

module.exports = { main }
```

> **Exam focus:** App Builder enables extensibility **without modifying Commerce core** — this is the key architectural principle. Custom code runs on Adobe's serverless infrastructure, not inside the Commerce PHP application.

### 9.2 API Mesh

**API Mesh for Adobe Developer App Builder** is a **GraphQL gateway** that allows developers to combine multiple APIs (Commerce, third-party, custom) into a **single unified GraphQL endpoint**.

```
+--------------------------------------------------+
|                  API Mesh Gateway                |
+--------------------------------------------------+
|                                                  |
|  Single GraphQL Endpoint                         |
|  https://graph.adobe.io/api/{meshId}/graphql     |
|                                                  |
|  +-----------+  +-----------+  +-------------+  |
|  | Commerce  |  |  3rd Party|  | Custom API  |  |
|  | GraphQL   |  |  REST API |  | (REST/GQL)  |  |
|  | API       |  |  (ERP etc)|  |             |  |
|  +-----------+  +-----------+  +-------------+  |
|        ^               ^               ^         |
|        |               |               |         |
|  +-----+---------------+---------------+-----+   |
|  |          API Mesh (stitching layer)       |   |
|  +-------------------------------------------+   |
|                                                  |
+--------------------------------------------------+
```

| Feature | Detail |
|---|---|
| Type | Managed GraphQL gateway (Adobe-hosted) |
| Purpose | Unify multiple API sources into one GraphQL endpoint |
| Sources supported | GraphQL, REST, OpenAPI specs |
| Use case | Headless storefronts needing data from multiple systems |
| No server | Serverless, Adobe-managed |
| Authentication | Adobe IMS / API key |

```json
// API Mesh configuration: mesh.json
{
  "meshConfig": {
    "sources": [
      {
        "name": "Commerce",
        "handler": {
          "graphql": {
            "endpoint": "https://mystore.com/graphql"
          }
        }
      },
      {
        "name": "ERP",
        "handler": {
          "openapi": {
            "source": "https://my-erp.com/api/swagger.json"
          }
        }
      }
    ]
  }
}
```

```bash
# Deploy API Mesh configuration
aio api-mesh:create mesh.json

# Update existing mesh
aio api-mesh:update mesh.json

# Get mesh endpoint details
aio api-mesh:get
```

> **Exam focus:** API Mesh creates a **single unified GraphQL endpoint** that can aggregate Commerce + third-party APIs. It is **serverless and Adobe-managed** — no gateway infrastructure to operate.

### 9.3 App Builder vs API Mesh — When to Use What

| Scenario | Use | Reason |
|---|---|---|
| Custom order sync to ERP | App Builder | Event-driven business logic |
| Extend Commerce Admin UI | App Builder (Admin UI SDK) | Out-of-process UI extension |
| Combine Commerce + loyalty API in one query | API Mesh | API aggregation/stitching |
| Scheduled data export to BI system | App Builder | Serverless scheduled action |
| Headless storefront needs unified API | API Mesh | Single endpoint for frontend |
| Replace a core Commerce PHP class | Neither | Use plugins/interceptors in-process |
