# AD0-E712 Full Exam Simulation #3 — Comprehensive Study Notes ## Adobe Commerce Business Practitioner Professional Certification > **Correction:** The original notes incorrectly labeled this as "Front-End Developer (Professional)". AD0-E712 is the **Business Practitioner Professional** certification. --- ## Table of Contents 1. [Exam Blueprint & Scoring Strategy](#1-exam-blueprint--scoring-strategy) 2. [Section 1: Core Features (49%)](#2-section-1-core-features-49) 3. [Section 2: Commerce Basics (14%)](#3-section-2-commerce-basics-14) 4. [Section 3: Digital Marketing (24%)](#4-section-3-digital-marketing-24) 5. [Section 4: Compliance (13%)](#5-section-4-compliance-13) 6. [Score Trend Tracker & Weak Pattern Analysis](#6-score-trend-tracker--weak-pattern-analysis) 7. [Final Simulation Strategy & Time Management](#7-final-simulation-strategy--time-management) 8. [Quick-Reference Checklist](#8-quick-reference-checklist) --- ## 1. Exam Blueprint & Scoring Strategy ### 1.1 Official Section Weights | Section | Topic | Weight | ~Questions (of 60) | |---------|-------|--------|--------------------| | 1 | Core Features | 49% | ~29 | | 2 | Commerce Basics | 14% | ~8 | | 3 | Digital Marketing | 24% | ~14 | | 4 | Compliance | 13% | ~8 | > **Exam focus:** Section 1 alone drives nearly half your total score. A strong Core Features performance can carry a weak section; a weak Section 1 is almost impossible to compensate for. ### 1.2 Passing Score & Scoring Math - **Passing score:** 68% (approximately 41/60 correct) - **Strategy:** If you score 80%+ in Section 1 (~23/29) and 75%+ in Digital Marketing (~10-11/14), you can pass even with moderate performance elsewhere. ``` Minimum viable score model: Section 1: 23/29 correct = 79% * 0.49 = 38.7 weighted points Section 2: 5/8 correct = 62% * 0.14 = 8.7 weighted points Section 3: 10/14 correct = 71% * 0.24 = 17.0 weighted points Section 4: 5/8 correct = 62% * 0.13 = 8.1 weighted points TOTAL = 72.5% -> PASS ``` ### 1.3 Exam Logistics Reminder - **Duration:** ~105 minutes (60 questions) - **Pace:** ~1 minute 45 seconds per question - **Format:** Multiple choice, single and multiple response - **No notes, no references during exam** - **Flag and return** to uncertain questions — don't spend more than 2 min on any one question --- ## 2. Section 1: Core Features (49%) ### 2.1 Theme Architecture & Inheritance #### Theme Directory Structure ``` app/design/frontend/ / / etc/ view.xml web/ css/ source/ _theme.less images/ js/ / layout/ templates/ web/ registration.php theme.xml ``` > **Exam focus:** Know exactly which files are required for a valid theme (`theme.xml`, `registration.php`) and which are optional but common. #### theme.xml — Core Declaration File ```xml My Custom Theme Magento/luma media/preview.jpg ``` > **Exam focus:** The `` tag enables theme inheritance. If no parent is declared, the theme has **no fallback to any other theme** — it does NOT automatically inherit from `Magento/blank`. The `` tag must be explicitly set for inheritance to work. `Magento/blank` itself has no parent. #### registration.php ```php **Exam focus:** The path string format is `frontend//` — the area prefix (`frontend`) is mandatory. #### Theme Inheritance Resolution Order (Fallback Chain) ``` Custom Theme | v Parent Theme (e.g., Luma) | v Magento/blank | v lib/web (global library assets) ``` **Exam focus:** - Files are resolved from most specific (child theme) to most generic - Layout XML files are **merged**, not overridden - Template `.phtml` files **override** — the first match wins - Static files (CSS, JS, images) follow the same fallback as templates --- ### 2.2 Layout XML #### Layout File Types | File Type | Location | Purpose | |-----------|----------|---------| | Page Layout | `/Magento_Theme/page_layout/` | Defines column structure (1-column, 2-columns-left, etc.) | | Page Configuration | `//layout/` | Configures blocks, containers, references | | Generic Layout | `//layout/` | Reusable layout definitions | #### Common Layout Instructions ```xml value ``` > **Exam focus:** `` targets existing blocks; `` targets containers. Containers hold blocks but have no template of their own. #### Layout Handle Hierarchy ``` default | +-- catalog_product_view | | | +-- catalog_product_view_type_simple | +-- catalog_product_view_type_configurable | +-- cms_page_view | +-- checkout_cart_index ``` > **Exam focus:** The `default` handle applies to every page. More specific handles (like `catalog_product_view`) apply only to matching pages. Custom handles can be added via controllers. #### Page Layouts Available by Default ```xml 1column.xml 2columns-left.xml 2columns-right.xml 3columns.xml empty.xml ``` --- ### 2.3 Templates (.phtml Files) #### Template Overriding To override `Magento/Catalog/view/frontend/templates/product/view/form.phtml`: ``` app/design/frontend/Vendor/theme/ Magento_Catalog/ templates/ product/ view/ form.phtml <-- your override ``` > **Exam focus:** The module directory name uses underscore notation (`Magento_Catalog`), not the namespace separator. #### Escape Methods in Templates ```php escapeHtml($text); // Escape HTML attributes echo $block->escapeHtmlAttr($attribute); // Escape URLs echo $block->escapeUrl($url); // Escape JavaScript strings echo $block->escapeJs($js); // Escape CSS echo $block->escapeCss($css); ?> ``` > **Exam focus:** Always use the appropriate escape method. Using `escapeHtml()` on a URL is incorrect — use `escapeUrl()`. This is a common trick question. #### Calling Block Methods in Templates ```php getData('custom_argument'); // Access child blocks $childBlock = $block->getChildBlock('child.block.name'); // Get child HTML echo $block->getChildHtml('child.block.name'); // Get child HTML with sorting echo $block->getChildHtml('child.block.name', true); ?> ``` --- ### 2.4 UI Components #### Form UI Component Structure ```xml
my_form.my_form_data_source ``` > **Exam focus:** Cookie Restriction Mode prevents non-essential cookies until user consent. When enabled, it delays page personalization. This is required for EU ePrivacy compliance. ### 5.2 PCI DSS (Payment Card Industry Data Security Standard) #### PCI DSS Levels | Level | Criteria | Requirements | |-------|----------|-------------| | Level 1 | >6M transactions/year | On-site audit (QSA) | | Level 2 | 1M-6M transactions/year | SAQ + quarterly scan | | Level 3 | 20K-1M e-commerce | SAQ + quarterly scan | | Level 4 | <20K e-commerce | SAQ recommended | #### Magento & PCI Compliance Approach ``` Recommended: Use payment vaulting / hosted payment pages PCI Scope Reduction Methods: 1. Tokenization - Store token, not card number 2. Hosted payment fields (e.g., Braintree, Stripe.js) 3. iFrame-based payment forms 4. PayPal redirect (customer leaves site) Magento Payment Vault: - Stores payment tokens (not actual card data) - Admin > Stores > Configuration > Sales > Payment Methods ``` > **Exam focus:** Magento Commerce (Adobe Commerce) does NOT store raw card data. Payment data should be handled by PCI-compliant payment providers. Using hosted payment pages significantly reduces PCI scope. #### SSL/HTTPS Requirements ``` Admin > Stores > Configuration > General > Web - Base URL (Secure): https://domain.com/ - Use Secure URLs on Storefront: Yes - Use Secure URLs in Admin: Yes - HTTP Strict Transport Security (HSTS): Enable via server config Magento auto-redirects HTTP to HTTPS when configured. ``` > **Exam focus:** PCI DSS requires TLS 1.2 or higher. TLS 1.0 and 1.1 are deprecated. This must be configured at the server level (Apache/Nginx), not Magento config. ### 5.3 ADA / WCAG Accessibility Compliance #### WCAG 2.1 Principles (POUR) ``` P - Perceivable - Alt text on images - Captions on video - Sufficient color contrast (4.5:1 normal text, 3:1 large text) - Text resizable to 200% O - Operable - All functionality via keyboard - Skip navigation links - No seizure-inducing content (< 3 flashes/second) - Enough time to read content U - Understandable - Readable text (lang attribute on ) - Predictable page behavior - Input assistance (error identification) A - Robust - Valid, parseable HTML - ARIA attributes on interactive elements ``` #### Magento Accessibility Features ```html Skip to Content * ``` > **Exam focus:** WCAG Level AA is the standard target for e-commerce. Adobe Commerce (Luma theme) includes baseline accessibility features. Custom themes must maintain ARIA labels, keyboard navigation, and color contrast requirements. #### ADA Compliance in Magento Context ``` Legal requirement in US under: - Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA) - Section 508 (federal agencies) - California Unruh Act Key testing tools: - axe DevTools - WAVE (Web Accessibility Evaluation Tool) - Chrome Lighthouse (Accessibility audit) - Screen reader testing (NVDA, JAWS, VoiceOver) ``` ### 5.4 Privacy Laws Beyond GDPR | Law | Jurisdiction | Key Requirement | |-----|-------------|-----------------| | GDPR | EU/EEA | Consent, erasure, portability | | CCPA | California, USA | Opt-out of data sale, disclosure | | PIPEDA | Canada | Consent, breach notification | | LGPD | Brazil | Similar to GDPR | | PDPA | Thailand/Singapore | Consent-based | #### CCPA Specific Requirements in Magento ``` California Consumer Privacy Act (CCPA): - "Do Not Sell My Personal Information" link required - Disclosure of data categories collected - Right to know what data is collected - Right to delete (same as GDPR erasure) Magento implementation: - Add "Do Not Sell" link in footer CMS block - Privacy policy CMS page must disclose data practices - Customer data export satisfies "right to know" ``` > **Exam focus:** CCPA applies to businesses with >$25M revenue, OR data on >50K consumers, OR >50% revenue from data sales — operating in California. Unlike GDPR, it does NOT require consent before collection. ### 5.5 Content Security Policy (CSP) ``` Admin > Stores > Configuration > Security > Content Security Policy CSP prevents XSS attacks by whitelisting: - Script sources - Style sources - Image sources - Connect sources (API calls) - Frame sources Magento 2.3.5+ introduced CSP support: ``` ```xml https://cdn.example.com https://images.example.com ``` > **Exam focus:** CSP is configured in `csp_whitelist.xml` per module. Inline scripts (`eval()`, `inline`) are blocked by default in report-only or enforced modes. This is frequently tested as a compliance + security topic. ### 5.6 Two-Factor Authentication (2FA) ``` Admin > Stores > Configuration > Security > 2FA - Force providers on all admin users - Providers: Google Authenticator, Authy, U2F, Duo Security CLI commands: bin/magento security:tfa:reset # Reset 2FA for user bin/magento security:tfa:providers # List providers ``` > **Exam focus:** 2FA is enabled by default in Magento 2.4+. It cannot be disabled for admin without a code modification. This is a security compliance requirement. --- ## 6. Score Trend Tracker & Weak Pattern Analysis ### 6.1 Score Tracking Template ``` =========================================== AD0-E712 Practice Exam Score Tracker =========================================== Test 1 Test 2 Test 3 Target Section 1 ____% ____% ____% 70%+ Section 2 ____% ____% ____% 65%+ Section 3 ____% ____% ____% 70%+ Section 4 ____% ____% ____% 65%+ -----------+------+----------+----------+--------- OVERALL ____% ____% ____% 68%+ Trend: [ Up / Down / Flat ] per section ``` ### 6.2 Common Weak Pattern Analysis #### Pattern 1: Layout XML Confusion **Common mistake:** Confusing `` vs `` vs `` vs `` ``` Rule: - and DECLARE new elements - and MODIFY existing elements - Containers cannot have templates - Blocks always have a class attribute ``` #### Pattern 2: Template Path Errors **Common mistake:** Wrong module directory naming in theme ``` Wrong: Magento/Catalog/templates/ Correct: Magento_Catalog/templates/ Wrong: vendor/magento/module-catalog/view/frontend/templates/ Correct (theme override): app/design/frontend/Vendor/theme/Magento_Catalog/templates/ ``` #### Pattern 3: RequireJS Map vs Mixin ``` map: { '*': { 'ModuleA': 'ModuleB' } } -> Completely replaces ModuleA with ModuleB -> ModuleA is NEVER loaded config: { mixins: { 'ModuleA': 'MyMixin' } } -> Loads ModuleA AND applies MyMixin wrapper -> _super() calls original methods ``` #### Pattern 4: GDPR vs CCPA Differences ``` GDPR: - Requires CONSENT before processing - Applies to EU residents (regardless of company location) - Right to erasure = anonymization - Data Protection Officer (DPO) may be required CCPA: - Requires OPT-OUT mechanism (not opt-in consent) - Applies to California residents - "Do Not Sell" link required - No DPO requirement ``` #### Pattern 5: SEO Canonical Tags ``` Question type: "A product appears in 3 categories. What prevents duplicate content?" Answer: Canonical URL pointing to the primary product URL Wrong answers to watch for: - 301 redirect (breaks category navigation) - robots.txt block (prevents indexing entirely) - Meta robots NOINDEX (removes from index entirely) Correct: ``` #### Pattern 6: Cache Type Selection ``` "After changing layout XML, which cache should you clean?" Answer: layout (and block_html) "After adding a translation string?" Answer: translate "After changing system configuration?" Answer: config (and block_html) "After enabling a new module?" Answer: config, full_page ``` ### 6.3 Final Weak Pattern Identification Checklist ``` [ ] Can I name all 4 required sections by weight without looking? [ ] Do I know the fallback chain order? [ ] Can I distinguish requirejs map vs mixin vs shim? [ ] Do I know when to use vs ? [ ] Can I explain GDPR anonymization vs hard deletion? [ ] Do I know PCI tokenization vs hosted payment? [ ] Can I identify CSP config file location? [ ] Do I know the difference between clean and flush? [ ] Do I know which Magento modes auto-generate static files? [ ] Can I write a correct theme.xml from memory? [ ] Do I know WCAG POUR acronym and each pillar? [ ] Can I explain canonical tags for duplicate content? ``` --- ## 7. Final Simulation Strategy & Time Management ### 7.1 Time Allocation Per Section ``` Total Time: 105 minutes Questions: 60 Recommended allocation: ---------------------------- Section 1 (29 Qs): ~51 min (1:45 avg per question) Section 2 ( 8 Qs): ~14 min Section 3 (14 Qs): ~24 min Section 4 ( 8 Qs): ~14 min Review flagged: ~10 min (reserved buffer) ---------------------------- Total used: ~113 min (pad 8 min buffer - work faster) ``` > **Exam focus:** Go through all questions once at ~90 sec each (~90 minutes), flag uncertain ones, then review flagged in remaining 15 minutes. Never leave a question blank — guess if necessary. ### 7.2 Question Type Strategies #### Single-Answer (Most Common) - Eliminate obviously wrong answers first - Look for Magento-specific terminology traps - "Best practice" questions have one clearly superior answer #### Multi-Answer (Select All That Apply) - The question will specify: "Choose TWO" or "Choose THREE" - Each correct choice is independently correct - No partial credit — all required choices must be selected #### Scenario-Based Questions - Read the full scenario before looking at answers - Identify: What type of problem is this? Layout? JS? Cache? Compliance? - The correct answer must address the specific stated problem ### 7.3 Red Flag Answer Patterns (Usually Wrong) ``` Red flags in answer choices: - "Edit core Magento files directly" -> Always wrong - "Use app/code to override vendor files" -> Wrong (use theme/plugin) - "Disable cache in production" -> Wrong - "Use inline JavaScript" -> Wrong (CSP issues) - "Store card numbers in database" -> Wrong (PCI violation) - "Hard delete all customer records" -> Wrong (GDPR - anonymize) - "Set robots to NOINDEX sitewide" -> Wrong (kills SEO) ``` ### 7.4 High-Confidence Quick Wins ``` Quick win topics (high testability, straightforward answers): 1. theme.xml required fields (title, parent) 2. registration.php format (frontend/Vendor/theme) 3. cache:clean vs cache:flush 4. developer mode vs production mode static files 5. escapeHtml() vs escapeUrl() distinction 6. GDPR double opt-in = "Need to Confirm" setting 7. Canonical tags = duplicate content solution 8. PCI tokenization = store tokens not card numbers 9. 2FA required by default in Magento 2.4+ 10. CSP whitelist file = csp_whitelist.xml ``` ### 7.5 Last 24 Hours Strategy ``` DO: - Review this document once completely - Do one quick 20-question practice quiz - Review your flagged/wrong questions from Tests 1 and 2 - Sleep 7-8 hours - Eat before the exam DON'T: - Study new material the night before - Cram layout XML syntax at midnight - Skip sections because they're "small" (Compliance at 13% can make/break) - Overthink multi-answer questions ``` --- ## 8. Quick-Reference Checklist > Everything testable on the AD0-E712 exam, organized for final review. ### Core Features (49%) - [ ] **Theme files:** `theme.xml` (title + parent) and `registration.php` are required minimum - [ ] **registration.php path format:** `frontend//` — area prefix is mandatory - [ ] **Theme inheritance:** Child → Parent → Blank → lib/web fallback chain - [ ] **Layout XML:** `.phtml` files override; layout XML files merge - [ ] **`` vs ``:** blocks have templates/classes; containers have neither - [ ] **`` vs ``:** reference modifies existing; block declares new - [ ] **Layout handles:** `default` applies globally; specific handles apply to matching pages - [ ] **Template override path:** `Magento_Module/templates/path/file.phtml` (underscore notation) - [ ] **Escape methods:** `escapeHtml()`, `escapeUrl()`, `escapeHtmlAttr()`, `escapeJs()` — use the right one - [ ] **Block constructor:** always call `parent::__construct()`; use `Context` for common deps - [ ] **RequireJS `map`:** fully replaces one module with another - [ ] **RequireJS `mixins`:** wraps a module; original still loads; `_super()` calls original - [ ] **`data-mage-init`:** must be on the element; `x-magento-init` can target any selector - [ ] **LESS overrides:** done in `_theme.less` or module-level `_module.less` within theme - [ ] **Developer mode:** static files generated on-the-fly (no deploy needed) - [ ] **Production mode:** `setup:static-content:deploy` required after any static change - [ ] **`cache:clean`:** removes valid cache; `cache:flush` destroys entire storage - [ ] **Layout cache type:** `layout` — clean after layout XML changes - [ ] **Translate cache:** `translate` — clean after i18n changes - [ ] **UI Components:** `dataSource` → `dataProvider` → `fieldset` → `field` hierarchy - [ ] **Widget types:** CMS Block, Page Link, Product List, Recently Viewed, etc. - [ ] **CMS Block in layout:** use `Magento\Cms\Block\Block` class with `block_id` argument ### Commerce Basics (14%) - [ ] **Configurable products:** no inventory; inventory on child simples - [ ] **Grouped products:** each simple sold separately with individual quantity - [ ] **Virtual products:** no shipping; for services - [ ] **Downloadable products:** links or uploaded files - [ ] **EAV tables:** `_varchar`, `_int`, `_decimal`, `_datetime`, `_text` - [ ] **Store hierarchy:** Default < Website < Store < Store View (config scope) - [ ] **Catalog price rules:** applied before cart (no coupon codes) - [ ] **Cart price rules:** applied in cart (supports coupon codes) - [ ] **Quote → Order flow:** quote = cart; converts to order on placement ### Digital Marketing (24%) - [ ] **Canonical tags:** prevent duplicate content for products in multiple categories - [ ] **robots.txt vs meta robots:** robots.txt controls crawling; meta robots controls indexing - [ ] **Sitemap:** generated via Admin > Marketing > SEO & Search > Site Map - [ ] **GA4 integration:** configured in Stores > Configuration > Sales > Google API - [ ] **GTM:** uses `window.dataLayer` for event data; reduces code deployments - [ ] **Email template syntax:** `{{var}}`, `{{if}}`, `{{depend}}` — NOT PHP/Twig - [ ] **Newsletter double opt-in:** "Need to Confirm: Yes" in newsletter config - [ ] **Related vs Upsells vs Cross-sells:** detail page / detail page / cart page - [ ] **Related product rules:** EE-only; default shows BOTH manual and rule-based (not override) - [ ] **Structured data:** only microdata (ratings, images) natively; NO JSON-LD for Product/BreadcrumbList - [ ] **JS/CSS merging:** Admin > Advanced > Developer — enable in production for performance - [ ] **Core Web Vitals:** LCP < 2.5s, FID < 100ms, CLS < 0.1 — Google SEO factors - [ ] **URL suffix:** `.html` is default for both products and categories (configurable) - [ ] **Category path in product URLs:** option in Catalog > SEO configuration ### Compliance (13%) - [ ] **GDPR erasure = anonymization** (not hard delete) — order history preserved - [ ] **GDPR vs CCPA:** GDPR = opt-in consent required; CCPA = opt-out mechanism required - [ ] **CCPA "Do Not Sell" link:** required in footer; applies to California residents - [ ] **Cookie Restriction Mode:** delays personalization until user consents; required for EU ePrivacy - [ ] **Cookie domain leading dot:** `.domain.com` allows subdomain cookies - [ ] **PCI tokenization:** store tokens, never raw card numbers; hosted payment fields reduce scope - [ ] **TLS 1.2+:** required for PCI; configured at server level (Apache/Nginx), not Magento - [ ] **CSP whitelist file:** `etc/csp_whitelist.xml` — added per module - [ ] **CSP blocks inline scripts** by default in enforced mode - [ ] **2FA:** enabled by default in Magento 2.4+; cannot be disabled without code change - [ ] **WCAG POUR:** Perceivable, Operable, Understandable, Robust - [ ] **WCAG AA color contrast:** 4.5:1 for normal text; 3:1 for large text - [ ] **ARIA labels:** required on interactive elements for screen reader accessibility - [ ] **Skip navigation link:** Magento Luma includes this by default - [ ] **HTTP Only cookies:** `Use HTTP Only: Yes` — prevents JavaScript cookie access - [ ] **HSTS:** configured at server level; forces HTTPS for subsequent visits --- *Study notes generated for AD0-E712 Adobe Commerce Business Practitioner Professional certification — Full Exam Simulation #3 preparation. These notes cover all four exam sections weighted by their contribution to the final score.*

flashcards.question: What is the exam weight breakdown for the four sections of the AD0-E712 exam?
flashcards.answer: Section 1: Core Features = 49% (~29 questions), Section 2: Commerce Basics = 14% (~8 questions), Section 3: Digital Marketing = 24% (~14 questions), Section 4: Compliance = 13% (~8 questions). Total: 60 questions, 105 minutes, 68% passing score (~41 correct).
flashcards.hint: Core Features is nearly half the exam

flashcards.question: What two files are required as the minimum for a valid Magento theme?
flashcards.answer: theme.xml (declares theme title, parent theme, and preview image) and registration.php (registers the theme with Magento using ComponentRegistrar). The registration.php path format must include the area prefix: 'frontend/Vendor/theme-name'.
flashcards.hint: One XML declaration file and one PHP registration file

flashcards.question: What is the theme inheritance fallback chain in Magento?
flashcards.answer: Custom Theme → Parent Theme (e.g., Luma) → Magento/blank → lib/web (global library assets). Files are resolved from most specific to most generic. Layout XML files are merged (not overridden), while template .phtml files override (first match wins).
flashcards.hint: Four levels from most specific to most generic, with different behavior for layouts vs templates

flashcards.question: What happens if no <parent> tag is declared in theme.xml?
flashcards.answer: The theme has no fallback to any other theme — it does NOT automatically inherit from Magento/blank. The <parent> tag must be explicitly set for inheritance to work. Magento/blank itself has no parent.
flashcards.hint: There's no automatic fallback — it must be explicitly declared

flashcards.question: What is the difference between <block> and <container> in Magento layout XML?
flashcards.answer: Blocks have a class attribute and can have templates; they generate output. Containers hold blocks but have no template or class of their own — they are structural wrappers. <block> and <container> declare new elements, while <referenceBlock> and <referenceContainer> modify existing elements.
flashcards.hint: One renders content, the other is just a structural wrapper

flashcards.question: What is the correct directory naming convention for overriding a module's template in a theme?
flashcards.answer: Use underscore notation: Magento_Catalog/templates/ (not Magento/Catalog/templates/). For example, to override vendor/magento/module-catalog/view/frontend/templates/product/view/form.phtml, place it at app/design/frontend/Vendor/theme/Magento_Catalog/templates/product/view/form.phtml.
flashcards.hint: Think underscore between vendor and module name, not slash

flashcards.question: What is the difference between RequireJS 'map' and 'mixins' in Magento?
flashcards.answer: map: { '*': { 'ModuleA': 'ModuleB' } } completely replaces ModuleA with ModuleB — ModuleA is never loaded. Mixins (config.mixins) wraps a module — the original still loads and _super() calls the original methods. Use map for full replacement, mixins for extending behavior.
flashcards.hint: One replaces entirely, the other wraps and extends

flashcards.question: What is the difference between data-mage-init and x-magento-init in Magento?
flashcards.answer: data-mage-init must be placed directly on the element as an HTML attribute. x-magento-init can be placed in a <script type='text/x-magento-init'> tag anywhere on the page and target any CSS selector. Use '*' as the selector to apply to the entire document. Both use RequireJS module paths.
flashcards.hint: One is inline on the element, the other can target any selector from anywhere

flashcards.question: What is the difference between cache:clean and cache:flush in Magento?
flashcards.answer: cache:clean removes valid cache entries (specific cache types only). cache:flush destroys the entire cache storage including third-party caches. Use clean during development for specific cache types; use flush when you need a complete reset.
flashcards.hint: One is surgical, the other is a full wipe

flashcards.question: How do Magento's developer mode and production mode differ regarding static files?
flashcards.answer: In developer mode, static files are generated on-the-fly (symlinked from source) — no deploy needed. In production mode, setup:static-content:deploy must be run explicitly after any static file changes. Forgetting to deploy in production is a common mistake.
flashcards.hint: One auto-generates, the other requires manual deployment

flashcards.question: What are the escape methods available in Magento .phtml templates and when should each be used?
flashcards.answer: escapeHtml() for HTML output (most common), escapeUrl() for URLs, escapeHtmlAttr() for HTML attributes, escapeJs() for JavaScript strings, escapeCss() for CSS. Using the wrong method (e.g., escapeHtml on a URL) is a common exam trick question.
flashcards.hint: Five methods, each for a specific output context — using the wrong one is always incorrect

flashcards.question: What is the difference between Catalog Price Rules and Cart Price Rules?
flashcards.answer: Catalog Price Rules are applied before the cart (at the product listing/detail level), show as reduced prices, don't support coupon codes, and are based on product conditions. Cart Price Rules are applied at checkout/cart, appear as discount line items, support coupon codes, and are based on cart conditions. Both support customer group filtering.
flashcards.hint: One changes the displayed price, the other creates a discount at checkout

flashcards.question: How does Magento prevent duplicate content from products appearing in multiple categories?
flashcards.answer: Through canonical tags: <link rel='canonical' href='...primary-product-url...'/>.  Enable at Stores → Config → Catalog → Search Engine Optimization for both products and categories. Canonical for categories points to the root category page (no filter params). Other solutions like 301 redirects or NOINDEX would break navigation or remove from index entirely.
flashcards.hint: A specific HTML meta tag that points to the primary URL — not redirects or blocking

flashcards.question: What is the configurable scope for store configuration values in Magento, and what is the override order?
flashcards.answer: Default (global) < Website < Store < Store View (most specific). Values at lower (more specific) scopes override parent scopes. For example, a Store View setting overrides the same setting at Default, Website, or Store level.
flashcards.hint: Four levels from broadest to most specific — the most specific wins

studyNotes.title: Day 20 — Weak Area Drill + Final Cheat Sheet
studyNotes.content:
# Magento 2 / Adobe Commerce — Weak Area Drill & Final Cheat Sheet

## Table of Contents
1. [How to Use These Notes](#1-how-to-use-these-notes)
2. [Pricing Hierarchy (Deep Drill)](#2-pricing-hierarchy-deep-drill)
3. [Order States & Statuses Diagram](#3-order-states--statuses-diagram)
4. [Product Types Reference](#4-product-types-reference)
5. [CE vs EE Feature Matrix](#5-ce-vs-ee-feature-matrix)
6. [Hosting Options Comparison](#6-hosting-options-comparison)
7. [GDPR Key Rights](#7-gdpr-key-rights)
8. [PCI SAQ Types](#8-pci-saq-types)
9. [Accessibility — WCAG Levels](#9-accessibility--wcag-levels)
10. [SEO Checklist](#10-seo-checklist)
11. [Digital Marketing — Native vs Third-Party Tools](#11-digital-marketing--native-vs-third-party-tools)
12. [Quick-Reference Checklist](#12-quick-reference-checklist)

---

## 1. How to Use These Notes

These notes cover every concept flagged as a **weak area** in Practice Test #3. Work through them in order:

1. **Read** each section carefully, paying attention to `Exam focus` callouts.
2. **Recite** the hierarchy / diagram from memory before looking at the next section.
3. **Test yourself** using the Quick-Reference Checklist at the bottom.

---

## 2. Pricing Hierarchy (Deep Drill)

### 2.1 The Six-Level Waterfall

Magento evaluates prices top-to-bottom and uses the **lowest applicable price** presented to the customer at the point of comparison, subject to the rules below.

```
PRICING WATERFALL (highest precedence → lowest precedence)
----------------------------------------------------------
1.  Regular Price          (base catalog price on the product)
2.  Special Price          (date-range override; beats regular)
3.  Tier Price             (qty-break discounts; per customer group)
4.  Group Price            (customer-group specific price; legacy in M2)
5.  Catalog Price Rule     (condition-based %; applied to catalog layer)
6.  Cart Price Rule        (applied at checkout; coupon or auto)
----------------------------------------------------------
NOTE: The LOWEST of Special / Tier / Catalog Rule wins at catalog layer.
Cart Price Rules are always applied AFTER catalog prices are resolved.
```

### 2.2 Regular Price

- Set directly on the product form under **Price**.
- Acts as the **floor** from which all discounts derive.
- Shown as "was" price when a lower price is active.

### 2.3 Special Price

| Attribute | Detail |
|---|---|
| Field | `special_price` |
| Scope | Website (SCOPE_WEBSITE = 2, not Store View — same as Regular Price) |
| Activation | Requires **Special Price From/To** date range (optional but recommended) |
| Wins over | Regular price unconditionally |
| Loses to | Tier price **if** the tier price is lower |

- **Exam focus:** Special price does **not** require a customer group — it applies to everyone.
- **Exam focus:** If both a special price AND a tier price exist, Magento shows the **lower** of the two.

### 2.4 Tier Price

```
Qty >= 5  → $18.00   (instead of $20.00 regular)
Qty >= 10 → $15.00
Qty >= 20 -> $12.00
```

- Configured per product → **Advanced Pricing → Tier Price** grid.
- Can be scoped to **All Groups**, a specific customer group, or **NOT LOGGED IN**.
- Displays as "Buy X for $Y each" on the product page.
- **Exam focus:** Tier prices are **percentage** or **fixed** amounts in Magento 2 (unlike M1 fixed-only).
- **Exam focus:** Tier prices replace Group Prices in the Magento 2 UI — group price is now a tier price with qty = 1.

### 2.5 Group Price (Legacy)

- In Magento 2, group prices are **stored as tier prices with qty = 1**.
- Still visible via API (`tier_prices` with `qty: 1`).
- **Exam focus:** You will NOT find a separate "Group Price" field in the Admin UI for M2 — it was folded into Tier Price.

### 2.6 Catalog Price Rule

```
Rule Conditions (attribute-based)
        |
        v
Discount Action (by %, by fixed amount, to %, to fixed)
        |
        v
Scheduled Update (optional — staging in EE)
        |
        v
Applied nightly via cron (CE) or Staging Preview (EE)
```

| Property | Value |
|---|---|
| Location | **Marketing → Promotions → Catalog Price Rules** |
| Applied to | Product price in catalog (before cart) |
| Combinability | Multiple rules can stack (lowest wins unless stop-rules used) |
| Priority | Lower number = higher priority |
| "Stop Further Rules Processing" | Prevents lower-priority rules from applying |
| EE Scheduling | Rules can be tied to Staging campaigns |

- **Exam focus:** Catalog price rules run via cron (`catalogrule_apply_all` — runs `DailyCatalogUpdate` daily at 1 AM). Changes are NOT instant in CE without manual re-index.
- **Exam focus:** The "Discard subsequent rules" / "Stop Further Rules Processing" checkbox is the mechanism to prevent stacking.

### 2.7 Cart Price Rule

```
Customer adds item to cart
        |
        v
Cart Price Rules evaluated (by priority)
        |
        +---> Condition met? YES
        |           |
        |           v
        |     Apply Action (discount %)
        |     Optionally generate coupon code
        |
        +---> Condition not met? SKIP
```

| Property | Value |
|---|---|
| Location | **Marketing → Promotions → Cart Price Rules** |
| Coupon types | No Coupon / Specific Coupon / Auto-generated |
| Actions | Percent of cart, Fixed amount, Fixed per item, Buy X Get Y Free |
| Free Shipping | Can be applied as part of the action |
| Uses per coupon | Configurable (0 = unlimited) |
| Uses per customer | Configurable per rule |

- **Exam focus:** Buy X Get Y Free is a **Cart Price Rule** action, NOT a catalog rule.
- **Exam focus:** Cart rules can be limited by **website, customer group, and date range**.
- **Exam focus:** "Auto-generated" coupons let you mass-generate unique single-use codes. This is a **CE feature** — `COUPON_TYPE_AUTO = 3` and the entire auto-generation infrastructure (`Massgenerator`, `CouponManagementService`) are in `module-sales-rule` (OSL-3.0).

### 2.8 Final Price Resolution Logic

```
Final displayed price = MIN(
    special_price (if active),
    min_tier_price (if qty threshold met),
    catalog_rule_price (if rule applies)
)

Then at checkout:
    final_price - cart_rule_discount = grand_total_item_price
```

- **Exam focus:** Cart rules **never** change the catalog-layer price — they create a discount line item in the quote/order.

---

## 3. Order States & Statuses Diagram

### 3.1 Concepts: State vs Status

| Term | Definition |
|---|---|
| **State** | Hard-coded system state (PHP constant in `Order.php`) |
| **Status** | Admin-configurable label mapped to one or more states |

A single **state** can have **multiple statuses**. You create custom statuses in **Stores → Order Status** and assign them to a state.

- **Exam focus:** States are immutable code constants; statuses are configurable labels. You can add statuses, not states.

### 3.2 Core Order State Machine

```
[Quote / Cart]
      |
      | (place order)
      v
+-------------+
|     NEW     |  <-- state='new', default status='pending'; payment not yet confirmed
+-------------+
      |
      | (payment received / authorized)
      v
+------------------+
| PENDING_PAYMENT  |  <-- awaiting payment gateway confirmation
+------------------+
      |
      | (payment captured / confirmed)
      v
+-------------+
| PROCESSING  |  <-- invoice created; order being fulfilled
+-------------+
      |
      +------------------------+
      |                        |
      | (fully shipped)        | (partial ship + backorder)
      v                        v
+----------+         +---------------------+
| COMPLETE |         |   PROCESSING (still)|
+----------+         +---------------------+
      |
      | (can still be refunded)
      v
[CLOSED]  <-- after full credit memo issued on a complete order

Alternate paths:
NEW / PROCESSING
      |
      | (admin cancels)
      v
+----------+
| CANCELED |
+----------+

PENDING_PAYMENT
      |
      | (payment suspected fraud)
      v
+-----------------+
| PAYMENT_REVIEW  |
+-----------------+
      |
      +-> PROCESSING (accepted)
      +-> CANCELED   (rejected)

Any state (except COMPLETE/CLOSED/CANCELED)
      |
      | (put on hold manually)
      v
+--------+
|  HOLDED |
+--------+
      |
      | (unhold)
      v
  [previous state]
```

### 3.3 State Constants Reference

| State Constant | Admin Label | Typical Trigger |
|---|---|---|
| `new` | New (default status: Pending) | Order placed, payment not confirmed |
| `pending_payment` | Pending Payment | Redirect payments (PayPal, etc.) |
| `processing` | Processing | Invoice created / payment captured |
| `complete` | Complete | All items shipped + invoiced |
| `closed` | Closed | Full credit memo issued |
| `canceled` | Canceled | Order canceled |
| `holded` | On Hold | Manual admin hold |
| `payment_review` | Payment Review | Fraud check pending |

- **Exam focus:** `closed` ≠ `canceled`. Closed = completed then fully refunded. Canceled = never fulfilled.
- **Exam focus:** You **cannot** cancel a `complete` order — you issue a **credit memo** which moves it to `closed`.
- **Exam focus:** `holded` is a temporary state; the underlying original state is preserved and restored on unhold.

### 3.4 Invoice, Shipment, Credit Memo Lifecycle

```
Order (PROCESSING)
  |
  +---> Create Invoice  (captures payment)
  |         |
  |         +---> Invoice State: OPEN -> PAID
  |
  +---> Create Shipment (fulfills items)
  |         |
  |         +---> Shipment + Tracking added
  |         +---> Order -> COMPLETE (when all items shipped + invoiced)
  |
  +---> Create Credit Memo (refund)
            |
            +---> Partial refund: Order stays PROCESSING or COMPLETE
            +---> Full refund on COMPLETE: Order -> CLOSED
```

- **Exam focus:** A credit memo can be created from an invoice **or** directly from the order — `CreditmemoLoader` supports both `createByInvoice()` and `createByOrder()` paths. An invoice is NOT strictly required.
- **Exam focus:** Partial shipments keep the order in `processing`; only **all** items shipped + invoiced = `complete`.

---

## 4. Product Types Reference

### 4.1 Overview Table

| Product Type | SKU Has Stock? | Configurable? | Needs Children? | Key Use Case |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Simple | Yes | No | No | Single physical item |
| Configurable | No (parent) | Yes | Yes (Simple) | T-shirt with size/color |
| Grouped | No (parent) | No | Yes (Simple) | Product set sold together |
| Bundle | No (parent) | Yes | Yes (Simple/Virtual) | Custom PC build |
| Virtual | Yes | No | No | Service, subscription, warranty |
| Downloadable | Yes | No | No | Digital file / software |
| Gift Card | Yes | No | No | EE only (native); CE via extension |

### 4.2 Simple Product

- Most fundamental product type; **all other types reference simples**.
- Has its own SKU, stock qty, weight.
- Can be sold standalone OR as a child of Configurable/Grouped/Bundle.

### 4.3 Configurable Product

```
Configurable Product (Parent SKU: TSHIRT-PARENT)
  |
  +---> Simple: TSHIRT-RED-S  (color=Red, size=S)
  +---> Simple: TSHIRT-RED-M  (color=Red, size=M)
  +---> Simple: TSHIRT-BLUE-S (color=Blue, size=S)
```

- Customer selects attribute values → dropdowns morph → a specific child simple is added to cart.
- **Stock is tracked at the child (simple) level.**
- Configurable product itself has **no stock qty**.
- Uses `super_attribute` in the cart item.
- **Exam focus:** Configurable attributes must use **Global scope** and be of input type **Dropdown** or **Visual/Text Swatch**.

### 4.4 Grouped Product

- Collection of simple products presented on one page; each **added to cart separately** (individual line items).
- No forced bundling — customer chooses qty of each.
- Parent grouped product has **no price of its own**.
- **Exam focus:** Grouped products do NOT have a configurable "build" — customers set individual qtys. Compare with Bundle which has required/optional selections.

### 4.5 Bundle Product

```
Bundle: Custom PC
  |
  +---> Option 1: Processor (Required, Dropdown)
  |         +---> Intel i5 (+$0)
  |         +---> Intel i7 (+$150)
  |
  +---> Option 2: RAM (Required, Radio)
  |         +---> 8GB (+$0)
  |         +---> 16GB (+$50)
  |
  +---> Option 3: SSD (Optional, Checkbox)
            +---> 512GB (+$80)
            +---> 1TB (+$120)
```

- Price can be **Dynamic** (sum of selections) or **Fixed** (base price ± options).
- Each selection links to a **Simple or Virtual** product.
- **Exam focus:** Bundle product has **Fixed** vs **Dynamic** price types — an exam favourite.
- **Exam focus:** Bundle items can have their own **SKU suffix** or use the parent SKU.

### 4.6 Virtual Product

- Like a simple product but **no weight / shipping** — never triggers shipping calculation.
- Examples: warranties, digital services, online consultations.
- Can be added to grouped or bundle products.

### 4.7 Downloadable Product

- Virtual + **downloadable links** (files or URLs).
- Customer receives links after purchase in My Account → **My Downloads**.
- Options: max downloads per link, open download in new window. (Note: there is NO time-based "link expiry" field in Magento 2.4.x — only max download count.)
- **Exam focus:** Downloadable products have **Samples** (free preview) and **Links** (purchased content). These are distinct attributes.

### 4.8 Gift Card (EE)

| Type | Description |
|---|---|
| Virtual | Delivered by email |
| Physical | Physical card shipped |
| Combined | Both methods |

- Gift card accounts tracked under **Marketing → Gift Card Accounts**.
- Redeemable at checkout; balance tracked per code.
- **Exam focus:** Gift Cards are an **Adobe Commerce (EE) exclusive** feature natively.

---

## 5. CE vs EE Feature Matrix

### 5.1 Magento Open Source (CE) vs Adobe Commerce (EE)

| Feature | Open Source (CE) | Adobe Commerce (EE) |
|---|---|---|
| **Page Builder** | Yes — full version (since 2.4.0) | Yes — full version |
| **B2B Features** | No | Yes (Companies, Quotes, Requisition Lists, Purchase Orders) |
| **Staging & Preview** | No | Yes (Content Staging) |
| **Customer Segments** | No | Yes |
| **Gift Cards** | Extension only | Native |
| **Reward Points** | Extension only | Native |
| **Store Credit** | No (EE-only — `module-customer-balance` is proprietary) | Yes |
| **Product Restrictions** | No | Yes (Customer Segment targeting) |
| **Advanced Reporting** | Yes (`module-analytics` is OSL-3.0 — ships with both) | Yes |
| **Elasticsearch/OpenSearch** | Yes (both) | Yes (both) |
| **PWA Studio** | Yes (both) | Yes (both) |
| **Live Search** | SaaS add-on | SaaS add-on |
| **Multi-Source Inventory (MSI)** | Yes (both) | Yes (both) |
| **Split Database** | No (deprecated 2.4.2) | No (deprecated) |
| **Catalog Permissions** | No | Yes (per category, per group) |
| **Scheduled Import/Export** | No | Yes |
| **Auto-generated Coupons** | Yes (`COUPON_TYPE_AUTO` in `module-sales-rule`, OSL-3.0) | Yes |
| **RMA (Returns)** | Extension only | Native |
| **Private Sales / Invitations** | No | Yes |
| **WYSIWYG + Dynamic Blocks** | CMS Blocks only | Dynamic Blocks (formerly Banners) |
| **Google Tag Manager** | No native integration (`module-google-tag-manager` is EE-only / proprietary) | Yes — native integration (adds "Account type" dropdown to GA/GA4 config) |

- **Exam focus:** **B2B module** (Companies, Quotes, Purchase Orders, Requisition Lists, Shared Catalogs) is **EE ONLY**.
- **Exam focus:** **Content Staging** (scheduling CMS and product updates) is **EE ONLY**.
- **Exam focus:** **Customer Segments** and **Catalog Permissions** — **EE ONLY**.
- **Exam focus:** MSI (Multi-Source Inventory) is available in **both CE and EE** since 2.3.

### 5.2 Adobe Commerce on Cloud vs Self-Hosted EE

| Aspect | Cloud (Pro/Starter) | On-Premise EE |
|---|---|---|
| Infrastructure | Managed by Adobe | Customer-managed |
| Deployment | Git push → pipeline | Manual or CI/CD |
| Patching | Assisted via ECE-Tools | Manual |
| Fastly CDN | Included | External |
| Elasticsearch | Included | Self-provision |
| RabbitMQ | Included (Pro) | Optional |

## 6. Hosting Options Comparison

### 6.1 Three Deployment Models

```
+------------------+------------------+--------------------+
|   Cloud Starter  |   Cloud Pro      |   On-Premises      |
+------------------+------------------+--------------------+
| Single region    | Multi-region     | Any infrastructure |
| 4 envs           | Staging + Prod   | Full control       |
| Shared infra     | Dedicated infra  | Own team           |
| No RabbitMQ      | RabbitMQ incl.   | Optional           |
| Fastly incl.     | Fastly incl.     | DIY CDN            |
| ~$2k/mo entry    | ~$5k+/mo         | CapEx model        |
+------------------+------------------+--------------------+
```

### 6.2 Cloud Starter

- **Environments:** `master` (production) + 3 active branches.
- **Architecture:** Single server per environment (no separate staging cluster).
- **No** dedicated staging environment (uses a branch for staging).
- **No** RabbitMQ message queue included.
- **Suitable for:** Small-to-medium merchants; lower traffic volumes.
- **Fastly** CDN and WAF included.
- **Exam focus:** Starter has **4 total environments** (master + 3). Pro has **two permanent** (Staging, Production) + many Integration branches.

### 6.3 Cloud Pro

- **Environments:** Integration cluster (up to 8 branches) + dedicated **Staging** + dedicated **Production**.
- **Architecture:** Three-node cluster in production (HA).
- **Includes:** RabbitMQ, dedicated Elasticsearch nodes, Fastly, New Relic.
- **Backups:** Automated snapshots (production + staging).
- **Scaling:** Vertical and horizontal scaling options.
- **Multi-region** capable.
- **Exam focus:** Pro Production is a **three-node HA cluster**. Starter is single-node per env.
- **Exam focus:** Only **Pro** includes dedicated **Staging** environment that mirrors production configuration.

### 6.4 On-Premises / Self-Hosted

- Full control of server stack (Nginx/Apache, PHP, MySQL, Redis, Elasticsearch).
- Requires own team for patching, security, scaling.
- Licensing: Annual subscription (EE) or free (CE/Open Source).
- Supports any cloud provider (AWS, Azure, GCP) or bare metal.
- **Exam focus:** On-prem is the **only** deployment where you control PHP version independently of Adobe's release schedule.

### 6.5 ECE-Tools (Cloud-specific)

```bash
# Build and deploy hooks in .magento.app.yaml
hooks:
  build: |
    set -e
    php ./vendor/bin/ece-tools run scenario/build/generate.xml
    php ./vendor/bin/ece-tools run scenario/build/transfer.xml
  deploy: |
    php ./vendor/bin/ece-tools run scenario/deploy.xml
  post_deploy: |
    php ./vendor/bin/ece-tools run scenario/post-deploy.xml
```

- **Exam focus:** ECE-Tools handles **static content deployment, DI compilation, and database migrations** during cloud deploy hooks.

## 7. GDPR Key Rights

### 7.1 The Eight GDPR Rights

| # | Right | Description | Magento Mechanism |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | **Right to be Informed** | Transparency about data collection | Privacy Policy page; cookie consent |
| 2 | **Right of Access** | Customer can request their personal data | Admin: Customer account export |
| 3 | **Right to Rectification** | Correct inaccurate personal data | Customer can edit account; admin edit |
| 4 | **Right to Erasure** (Right to be Forgotten) | Delete all personal data on request | Anonymize customer; admin action |
| 5 | **Right to Restrict Processing** | Limit how data is used | Manual admin process |
| 6 | **Right to Data Portability** | Receive data in machine-readable format | Customer data export (JSON/CSV) |
| 7 | **Right to Object** | Object to processing (e.g., marketing) | Unsubscribe; newsletter opt-out |
| 8 | **Rights related to Automated Decision-Making** | No purely automated profiling decisions | Relevant if AI/ML scoring used |

- **Exam focus:** "Right to be Forgotten" = **anonymization** of customer data in Magento. Personal data is replaced with anonymized values; orders are retained for tax/legal purposes.
- **Exam focus:** GDPR applies to any merchant **processing data of EU citizens**, regardless of where the merchant is based.

### 7.2 Magento Native GDPR Features

Magento does NOT have built-in "Export Personal Data" or "Anonymize Customer" admin actions. There is no `privacy` config group under Customer Configuration. GDPR data export/deletion requires **Adobe Commerce Privacy extension** or third-party modules.

The only native privacy-related feature is **Cookie Restriction Mode** (see below).

### 7.3 Cookie Consent

- **Cookie Restriction Mode** — when enabled, drops a consent banner; no persistent cookies until accepted.
- Magento cookies of note: `frontend` (session), `mage-cache-sessid`, `form_key`, `recently_viewed_product`, `persistent_shopping_cart`.
- **Exam focus:** Cookie Restriction Mode is in **Stores → Config → General → Web → Cookie Restriction Mode**, NOT in the Customers section.

### 7.4 Key GDPR Technical Requirements

| Requirement | Implementation |
|---|---|
| Consent logging | Log timestamp, IP, and what was consented to |
| Data breach notification | 72 hours to notify supervisory authority |
| Privacy by Design | Collect minimum data; anonymize where possible |
| Data Processing Agreement | Required with third-party processors |
| DPO (Data Protection Officer) | Required for large-scale processing |

- **Exam focus:** 72-hour breach notification window is a critical exam fact.

## 8. PCI SAQ Types

### 8.1 What is PCI DSS?

Payment Card Industry Data Security Standard — a set of security standards for any entity that stores, processes, or transmits cardholder data.

### 8.2 SAQ (Self-Assessment Questionnaire) Types

| SAQ | Type | Who It Applies To | Card Data Environment |
|---|---|---|---|
| **SAQ A** | Card-not-present; fully outsourced | Merchants using hosted payment (iframe/redirect) — NO card data on merchant server | Fully outsourced (e.g., Braintree hosted fields, PayPal redirect) |
| **SAQ A-EP** | E-commerce; partially outsourced | Merchants where payment page is on their server but processing outsourced | JavaScript-based; page served from merchant |
| **SAQ B** | Imprint / standalone terminal | Brick-and-mortar with dial-up terminals; no electronic storage | Physical terminal only |
| **SAQ B-IP** | Standalone IP-connected terminal | Physical terminal over IP | IP terminal; no card data storage |
| **SAQ C** | Payment app connected to internet | Merchants with payment apps on internet-connected systems | POS app; no cardholder data storage |
| **SAQ C-VT** | Virtual terminal | Merchants entering card data via web-based virtual terminal | Web interface only |
| **SAQ D** | All others | Any merchant not qualifying for above; all service providers | Most complex; full audit |
| **SAQ P2PE** | Point-to-point encryption | Hardware P2PE solutions only | Encrypted from swipe |

- **Exam focus:** **SAQ A** = simplest = **fully hosted** payment page (iframe from payment provider). Merchant NEVER touches card data.
- **Exam focus:** **SAQ A-EP** = more complex = merchant serves the checkout page (JavaScript redirects). Merchant controls the page environment.
- **Exam focus:** Most modern Magento merchants using **Braintree Drop-In UI** or **PayPal hosted fields** qualify for **SAQ A**.
- **Exam focus:** Merchants who self-host a custom payment form that posts card data qualify for **SAQ D** at minimum.

### 8.3 PCI Compliance Levels

| Level | Criteria | Requirements |
|---|---|---|
| Level 1 | >6M transactions/year | On-site QSA audit annually + quarterly scan |
| Level 2 | 1M–6M/year | Annual SAQ + quarterly scan |
| Level 3 | 20K–1M e-commerce/year | Annual SAQ + quarterly scan |
| Level 4 | <20K e-commerce/year | Annual SAQ recommended |

### 8.4 Magento Payment Security Features

```
Admin → Stores → Config → Sales → Payment Methods
  → Payment Action: Authorize Only vs Authorize and Capture

Vault (Token storage):
  - Card data NEVER stored in Magento DB
  - Payment providers return a token (vault token)
  - Token stored in `vault_payment_token` table
```

- **Exam focus:** Magento Payment Vault stores **tokens**, not card numbers. This is key for PCI scope reduction.
- **Exam focus:** **Authorize Only** = funds reserved but not captured until invoice created. **Authorize and Capture** = immediate capture.

## 9. Accessibility — WCAG Levels

### 9.1 WCAG Overview

**Web Content Accessibility Guidelines (WCAG)** — published by W3C/WAI. Current version: **WCAG 2.1** (2.2 published Oct 2023).

### 9.2 The POUR Principles

| Principle | Meaning |
|---|---|
| **P**erceivable | Information must be presentable in ways users can perceive |
| **O**perable | UI components and navigation must be operable |
| **U**nderstandable | Information and operation must be understandable |
| **R**obust | Content must be robust enough for assistive technologies |

- **Exam focus:** POUR = Perceivable, Operable, Understandable, Robust. All WCAG criteria map to one of these.

### 9.3 Conformance Levels

| Level | Meaning | Criteria Count (2.1) | Typical Requirement |
|---|---|---|---|
| **A** | Minimum | 30 criteria | Baseline; without this, some users CANNOT access content |
| **AA** | Standard | 20 additional (50 total) | **Legal standard** in most jurisdictions; ADA, EN 301 549, AODA |
| **AAA** | Enhanced | 28 additional (78 total) | Aspirational; not required for full conformance |

- **Exam focus:** **WCAG 2.1 AA** is the standard referenced in legal compliance (ADA in USA, EN 301 549 in EU). Adobe Commerce targets AA.
- **Exam focus:** AAA conformance is NOT required for any legal standard — it's aspirational.

### 9.4 Key WCAG Success Criteria (Exam-relevant)

| SC | Level | Requirement |
|---|---|---|
| 1.1.1 Non-text Content | A | All images need alt text |
| 1.3.1 Info and Relationships | A | Structure conveyed through markup |
| 1.4.3 Contrast (Minimum) | AA | 4.5:1 ratio for normal text; 3:1 for large text |
| 1.4.4 Resize Text | AA | Text resizable to 200% without loss of content |
| 2.1.1 Keyboard | A | All functionality available via keyboard |
| 2.4.4 Link Purpose | A | Link purpose determinable from context |
| 2.4.6 Headings and Labels | AA | Descriptive headings and labels |
| 3.1.1 Language of Page | A | Default language identified in HTML |
| 4.1.2 Name, Role, Value | A | All UI components have accessible name/role |

- **Exam focus:** Contrast ratio **4.5:1** for body text, **3:1** for large text (18pt+ or 14pt bold) — memorize these numbers.
- **Exam focus:** **2.1.1 Keyboard** — every feature must be keyboard-operable. This catches inaccessible custom JavaScript widgets.

### 9.5 Magento / Adobe Commerce Accessibility

- Adobe Commerce ships with **ARIA roles** and keyboard navigation in Luma theme.
- **Luma** is designed to meet WCAG 2.1 AA.
- Custom themes must be independently assessed.
- Admin UI has known AA gaps — tracked in GitHub issues.

## 10. SEO Checklist

### 10.1 URL Key

```
Product URL Key:
  Admin: Catalog → Products → [Product] → Search Engine Optimization tab
  Field: "URL Key"
  Example: "blue-widget-12-inch" (NOT "blue_widget_12_inch")

Rules:
  - Lowercase only
  - Hyphens as word separator (not underscores — Google treats _ as word joiner)
  - No special characters
  - Unique per store view
  - Autogenerated from product name (can override)
```

- **Exam focus:** URL keys use **hyphens** (`-`) not underscores (`_`) for best SEO practice. Google treats underscores as word-joiners.
- **Exam focus:** URL keys are **per Store View** — you can have different URL keys per language/locale.
- **Exam focus:** When you change a URL key, Magento creates a **301 permanent redirect** from the old URL if "Create Permanent Redirect" is checked.

### 10.2 Canonical Tags

```html
<!-- Canonical prevents duplicate content -->
<link rel="canonical" href="https://example.com/blue-widget.html" />

<!-- Magento generates these for: -->
<!-- - Paginated category pages (page 2, 3...) -->
<!-- - Configurable product URLs (child simples) -->
<!-- - Filtered/layered navigation URLs -->
```

| Config | Path |
|---|---|
| Use Canonical Link Meta Tag for Categories | Stores → Config → Catalog → Search Engine Optimization |
| Use Canonical Link Meta Tag for Products | Same section |

- **Exam focus:** Canonical tags should be enabled for both **products** and **categories** to prevent duplicate content from layered navigation/pagination.
- **Exam focus:** Canonical for categories = points to the **root category page** (no filter params). Canonical for products = points to the **product's primary URL**.

### 10.3 Meta Tags

```html
<!-- Meta Title -->
<title>Blue Widget 12 Inch | Brand Name</title>

<!-- Meta Description (not a ranking factor, but affects CTR) -->
<meta name="description" content="Buy the Blue Widget 12 inch. Free shipping on orders $50+." />

<!-- Meta Keywords (largely ignored by Google) -->
<meta name="keywords" content="blue widget, 12 inch widget" />

<!-- Robots -->
<meta name="robots" content="INDEX,FOLLOW" />
<meta name="robots" content="NOINDEX,NOFOLLOW" />
```

| Field | Magento Location | Scope |
|---|---|---|
| Meta Title | Product → SEO tab | Store View |
| Meta Description | Product → SEO tab | Store View |
| Meta Keywords | Product → SEO tab | Store View |
| Page Title | CMS Page | Store View |
| Default Description | Stores → Config → General → Design | Store View |

- **Exam focus:** Meta title and description are **Store View** scoped — essential for multi-language stores.
- **Exam focus:** Meta keywords are **not a Google ranking signal** — exam may test whether - **Exam focus:** The `<title>` tag is populated from: product meta title > product name (if no meta title set) + store name suffix.

### 10.4 XML Sitemap

```xml
<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
<urlset xmlns="http://www.sitemaps.org/schemas/sitemap/0.9">
  <url>
    <loc>https://example.com/blue-widget.html</loc>
    <lastmod>YYYY-MM-DD</lastmod>
    <changefreq>daily</changefreq>
    <priority>0.5</priority>
  </url>
</urlset>
```

```
Admin: Marketing → SEO & Search → Site Map
  → Generate Sitemap (manual or cron)
  → Outputs: sitemap.xml (or custom filename)

Config: Stores → Config → Catalog → XML Sitemap
  → Frequency settings per type (product/category/CMS)
  → Priority per type
  → Cron schedule
  → Add sitemap to robots.txt
```

- **Exam focus:** Sitemap is generated at: **Marketing → SEO & Search → Site Map**.
- **Exam focus:** Sitemap cron is separate from catalog price rule cron. Configure under `XML Sitemap` section.
- **Exam focus:** Magento can **automatically add sitemap to robots.txt** — enable in config.

### 10.5 Hreflang

```html
<!-- Hreflang tells search engines which language/region a page targets -->
<link rel="alternate" hreflang="en-us" href="https://example.com/product.html" />
<link rel="alternate" hreflang="de-de" href="https://example.de/produkt.html" />
<link rel="alternate" hreflang="x-default" href="https://example.com/product.html" />
```

| Aspect | Detail |
|---|---|
| Purpose | Avoid duplicate content penalties for multi-language sites |
| `x-default` | Fallback for unmatched language/region |
| Implementation | In `<head>`, XML sitemap, or HTTP headers |
| Magento Native | NOT built-in; requires **extension** or custom theme |
| Scope | Must be bidirectional — each page references all its alternates |

- **Exam focus:** Magento does **NOT** natively generate hreflang tags — requires a third-party extension.
- **Exam focus:** `x-default` should point to the **default/fallback version** of the page.
- **Exam focus:** Hreflang is implemented using **BCP 47 language codes** (e.g., `en-US`, `fr-FR`, `de-DE`).

### 10.6 Complete SEO Checklist Summary

```
[ ] URL Keys: lowercase, hyphens, unique per store view
[ ] 301 redirects: enabled on URL key change
[ ] Canonical tags: enabled for products AND categories
[ ] Meta titles: unique per product (not duplicate of page title)
[ ] Meta descriptions: 150-160 chars, unique, compelling
[ ] XML Sitemap: generated, submitted to Google Search Console
[ ] robots.txt: sitemap URL included; crawl directives correct
[ ] Hreflang: extension installed for multi-language stores
[ ] Image alt text: all product images have descriptive alt
[ ] Page load speed: optimized (PageSpeed / Core Web Vitals)
[ ] Structured data: rich snippets (Product schema) enabled
[ ] Layered nav: canonical prevents filter URL indexing
[ ] Pagination: rel="next" / rel="prev" (deprecated by Google; canonical preferred)
```

flashcards.question: What are the six price levels in Magento's pricing waterfall, in order?
flashcards.answer: 1) Regular Price (base catalog price), 2) Special Price (date-range override), 3) Tier Price (quantity-break discounts per customer group), 4) Group Price (legacy — stored as Tier Price with qty=1 in M2), 5) Catalog Price Rule (condition-based, applied to catalog layer), 6) Cart Price Rule (applied at checkout). The lowest of Special/Tier/Catalog Rule wins at catalog layer; Cart Rules apply after.
flashcards.hint: Six levels — catalog-layer resolution first, then cart-layer discounts

flashcards.question: How does Group Price work in Magento 2 compared to Magento 1?
flashcards.answer: In Magento 2, Group Price is stored as a Tier Price with qty = 1. There is no separate 'Group Price' field in the Admin UI — it was folded into the Tier Price functionality. You can set a price for a specific customer group by creating a tier price with quantity = 1 for that group.
flashcards.hint: No separate field in M2 — it's a special case of another pricing feature

flashcards.question: What is the difference between an order State and an order Status in Magento?
flashcards.answer: States are hard-coded system constants in PHP (Order.php) that cannot be changed. Statuses are admin-configurable labels mapped to one or more states (created in Stores → Order Status). You can add custom statuses and assign them to existing states, but you cannot create new states.
flashcards.hint: One is immutable code, the other is a configurable label

flashcards.question: What are the 8 core order states in Magento, and what triggers each?
flashcards.answer: new (order placed, payment not confirmed), pending_payment (awaiting payment gateway confirmation), processing (invoice created/payment captured), complete (all items shipped + invoiced), closed (complete then fully refunded via credit memo), canceled (order canceled), holded (manual admin hold), payment_review (fraud check pending).
flashcards.hint: Eight states covering the full lifecycle from placement to completion or cancellation

flashcards.question: What is the difference between 'complete' and 'closed' order states, and can you cancel a complete order?
flashcards.answer: Complete means all items are shipped and invoiced. Closed means the order was complete and then fully refunded via credit memo. You CANNOT cancel a complete order — you must issue a credit memo, which moves it to closed. Canceled means the order was never fulfilled.
flashcards.hint: Think about the difference between never fulfilled vs fulfilled then refunded

flashcards.question: What are the seven product types in Magento, and which is EE-only?
flashcards.answer: Simple, Configurable, Grouped, Bundle, Virtual, Downloadable, and Gift Card. Gift Card is natively available in Adobe Commerce (EE) only. Key distinctions: Configurable stock lives on child simples, Grouped items are added to cart separately, Bundle can have Fixed or Dynamic pricing.
flashcards.hint: Six available in both editions, one is enterprise-exclusive

flashcards.question: What are the requirements for configurable product attributes in Magento?
flashcards.answer: Configurable attributes must use Global scope and be of input type Dropdown or Visual/Text Swatch. The configurable product itself has no stock quantity — inventory is tracked at the child simple product level. Each child simple represents a unique combination of attribute values.
flashcards.hint: Think about scope and input type restrictions for the parent product's variation attributes

flashcards.question: What is the difference between Fixed and Dynamic pricing for Bundle products?
flashcards.answer: Dynamic pricing: the bundle's price is calculated as the sum of all selected child product prices. Fixed pricing: the bundle has a base price, and each option adds or subtracts from that base. Dynamic pricing shows the range (e.g., 'From $99'), while Fixed pricing shows the base price with option adjustments.
flashcards.hint: One calculates from children, the other starts with a base and adjusts

flashcards.question: Name five features that are exclusive to Adobe Commerce (EE) and not available in Magento Open Source (CE).
flashcards.answer: EE-only features include: B2B module (Companies, Quotes, Requisition Lists, Purchase Orders, Shared Catalogs), Content Staging (scheduling CMS/product updates), Customer Segments, Catalog Permissions (per category/group), RMA (Returns), Dynamic Blocks, Scheduled Import/Export, Reward Points, native Gift Cards, native GTM integration, Store Credit, and Email Reminders.
flashcards.hint: Think about B2B, staging, segmentation, and advanced marketing features

flashcards.question: What is the difference between Adobe Commerce Cloud Starter and Cloud Pro?
flashcards.answer: Starter: 4 environments (master + 3 branches), single-node per environment, no dedicated staging, no RabbitMQ. Pro: Integration branches + dedicated Staging + dedicated Production (3-node HA cluster), includes RabbitMQ, dedicated Elasticsearch nodes, automated backups, multi-region capable. Both include Fastly CDN and WAF.
flashcards.hint: Compare environment count, node architecture, and included services

flashcards.question: How do Catalog Price Rules get applied in Magento, and what is 'Stop Further Rules Processing'?
flashcards.answer: Catalog Price Rules run via cron (catalogrule_apply_all — daily at 1 AM). Changes are NOT instant in CE without manual reindex. The 'Stop Further Rules Processing' checkbox prevents lower-priority rules from applying — it's the mechanism to prevent price rule stacking. Lower priority number = higher priority.
flashcards.hint: Think about cron-based application and rule stacking prevention

flashcards.question: Does Magento natively generate hreflang tags for multi-language stores?
flashcards.answer: No. Magento does NOT natively generate hreflang tags — this requires a third-party extension. Hreflang tags use BCP 47 language codes (e.g., en-US, fr-FR), must be bidirectional (each page references all alternates), and should include x-default for the fallback version.
flashcards.hint: This SEO feature for multi-language sites requires additional tools

flashcards.question: What are the eight GDPR rights, and what is the 72-hour rule?
flashcards.answer: The 8 rights: 1) Right to be Informed, 2) Right of Access, 3) Right to Rectification, 4) Right to Erasure, 5) Right to Restrict Processing, 6) Right to Data Portability, 7) Right to Object, 8) Rights related to Automated Decision-Making. The 72-hour rule requires businesses to notify the supervisory authority within 72 hours of discovering a data breach.
flashcards.hint: Eight rights plus a critical breach notification timeline

flashcards.question: What is the difference between 'Authorize Only' and 'Authorize and Capture' payment actions in Magento?
flashcards.answer: Authorize Only reserves the funds on the customer's card but does not capture them until an invoice is created. Authorize and Capture immediately captures the payment at the time of order placement. Authorize Only is commonly used when merchants want to verify stock before capturing payment.
flashcards.hint: Think about when the money actually moves — at order time or at invoice time
